meta.title: The 24 gurus of Dattātreya: pointwise teachings from three sants
meta.description: For each of the 24 gurus Dattātreya names to King Yadu (Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 11.7.33-35), plus the body as a twenty-fifth teacher, the statements of three sants: Prabhupāda's Bhāgavatam translation and purports (verbatim), Sant Eknath's Eknathi Bhagavat and Tembe Swami's Datta Mahatmya (selected ovis, translated from Marathi). Every statement carries its sant, guru and source.
meta.how_to_read: `statements` is one flat list. Filter it by `guru_number` and `sant_slug`. `gurus` describes each guru and where its material sits in each work. Guru numbers follow the Bhāgavatam's list.

sants.name: A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
sants.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Canto 11, chapters 7-9 (Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition)
sants.what_is_here: Each verse's translation and each paragraph of its purport, verbatim. The Sanskrit, transliteration and word-for-word meanings travel with the translation in `original`.

sants.name: Sant Eknath
sants.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), a 16th-century Marathi commentary in ovi verse on Bhāgavata Canto 11. Adhyays 7, 8 and 9 comment on Bhāgavatam 11.7, 11.8 and 11.9.
sants.language_of_statements: English, translated from the Marathi by Claude (an AI)
sants.what_is_here: A selection of ovis for each guru. The Marathi is kept in `original.text`.

sants.name: Tembe Swami (Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī)
sants.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya), Marathi ovis in 51 adhyays, composed 1901 at Mahatpur; edited by Pt. Atmaram Shastri Jere, published by Yogiraj Gulavani Maharaj. Adhyays 47-50 carry the 24 gurus.
sants.language_of_statements: English, translated from the Marathi by Claude (an AI)
sants.what_is_here: A selection of ovis for each guru. The Marathi (or Sanskrit, for 8 ovis) is kept in `original.text`.

statement_fields.id: Stable id: g<guru number>.<sant slug>.<running number>.
statement_fields.guru_number: 1-24 in the Bhāgavatam's order; 25 is the body (an additional teacher, not one of the 24).
statement_fields.guru_sanskrit: The guru's name as it appears in Bhāgavatam 11.7.33-35 (null for the body).
statement_fields.sant: Who the statement is credited to.
statement_fields.statement: The statement in English. Verbatim for Prabhupāda; our translation for Eknath and Tembe. [Square brackets] in those two are translator glosses, not the sant's words.
statement_fields.statement_kind: translation (a verse's meaning) | purport | teaching (an ovi).
statement_fields.source: work, reference, url, and verse_id (Prabhupāda) or adhyay and ovi (Eknath, Tembe). Eknath's `ovi` is our running count of ovis through the adhyay in page order (the page prints only an ovi's last two digits, in full at every tenth ovi; that is kept as `ovi_as_printed`); `follows_bhagavata_verse_id` is the Sanskrit verse the ovi comes after.
statement_fields.original: The text in its own language, for translations: {language, script, text} plus, for Prabhupāda's verse translations, transliteration and word_for_word. null for purports.
statement_fields.verbatim: true only where `statement` is the published English, unaltered.
statement_fields.machine_translated: true where `statement` is our translation of a Marathi or Sanskrit original.
statement_fields.needs_review: true on every machine-translated statement: not yet checked by a person who reads Marathi.

bhagavatam_list_verse.transliteration:
pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam
āpo ’gniś candramā raviḥ
kapoto ’jagaraḥ sindhuḥ
pataṅgo madhukṛd gajaḥ

madhu-hā hariṇo mīnaḥ
piṅgalā kuraro ’rbhakaḥ
kumārī śara-kṛt sarpa
ūrṇanābhiḥ supeśakṛt

ete me guravo rājan
catur-viṁśatir āśritāḥ
śikṣā vṛttibhir eteṣām
anvaśikṣam ihātmanaḥ
bhagavatam_list_verse.translation: O King, I have taken shelter of twenty-four gurus, who are the following: the earth, air, sky, water, fire, moon, sun, pigeon and python; the sea, moth, honeybee, elephant and honey thief; the deer, the fish, the prostitute Piṅgalā, the kurara bird and the child; and the young girl, arrow maker, serpent, spider and wasp. My dear King, by studying their activities I have learned the science of the self.
bhagavatam_list_verse.note: The verse that names the 24 gurus. Its only purport (on the wasp) sits under guru 24.

notes: PRABHUPĀDA, COPYRIGHT: the Bhāgavatam text on vedabase.io is © The Bhaktivedanta Book Trust International. Quoting it in the app, or anywhere public, needs the BBT's permission.

PRABHUPĀDA, AUTHORSHIP: Bhāgavatam Canto 11 is published under Prabhupāda's name, but ISKCON-affiliated sources say its translation and purports were finished after 1977 by Hridayananda Dasa Goswami with Gopiparanadhana Dasa. The saved Vedabase pages do not name the individual author, so this was not confirmed from them. Before presenting these purports as Prabhupāda's own words, check with the BBT.

PRABHUPĀDA, FIDELITY: nothing is reworded. Each statement is a verse's translation or one purport paragraph, copied from Vedabase. Within each guru's verses nothing was left out; the first verses (11.7.24-32, 36), which introduce the Yadu-avadhūta conversation, and the closing verses 11.9.30-33 are not included.

EKNATH AND TEMBE, TRANSLATION: both English texts are our own machine translation, made from the Marathi in one pass, and selective: ovis that repeat a point, only narrate, or only link one section to the next were left out. Only Tembe's adhyay 50 got a second line-by-line audit against the Marathi (a first draft had errors); the rest has not been audited by a person. Treat all of it as a draft (`needs_review`).
EKNATH, BOUNDARIES: each guru's `ovis` range is our own sectioning of the adhyay and is approximate to an ovi or two, since the ovi that announces the next guru often closes the previous section.

TEMBE, SOURCE TEXT: the only copy found is a PDF set in an old Devanagari font that does not extract as text. We decoded the font's encoding and checked adhyays 47-50 against page images, but a stray mis-decoded letter is possible. The print's footnote-reference digits were removed from `original.text`. Eight ovis are Sanskrit verses (`original.language` is "sa"): 47:23, 47:54, 47:107, 48:39, 48:55, 48:102, 49:30, 50:99.

TEMBE, ORDER: Tembe numbers the last four gurus differently from the Bhāgavatam: serpent 21st, arrow-maker 22nd, wasp 23rd, spider 24th. This file uses the Bhāgavatam's order throughout; Tembe's own number is in `gurus[].datta_mahatmya.tembe_ordinal`.
THE BODY: the avadhūta also takes his own body as a teacher (Bhāgavatam 11.9.24-29; Eknath 9:247-380; Tembe 50:87-99). It is not one of the 24, so it is guru number 25 with `additional_teacher` true.

VOICE: Eknath and Tembe speak as male renunciates, and on the pigeon, moth, elephant, Piṅgalā and the body much of their text treats women as a snare. Lines that carry a lesson are translated faithfully; a few that only insult were left out (Eknath 9:302-303 and 9:367; Tembe 49:34-37, 50:2-3 and 50:5-7), and so were Eknath's polemics against classes of people in the body lesson (9:349, 9:351-357). The Prabhupāda text is unabridged, so it keeps whatever the Bhāgavatam and its purports say there.
TEMBE, OTHER OMISSIONS: 48:52-62 (a digression on the moon's phases), 50:97 (unreadable in the print) and 50:100-103 (the closing narrative: Yadu bows and departs).

statements.statement: A sober person, even when harassed by other living beings, should understand that his aggressors are acting helplessly under the control of God, and thus he should never be distracted from progress on his own path. This rule I have learned from the earth.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
भूतैराक्रम्यमाणोऽपि धीरो दैववशानुगै: ।
तद् विद्वान्न चलेन्मार्गादन्वशिक्षं क्षितेर्व्रतम् ॥ ३७ ॥
original.transliteration:
bhūtair ākramyamāṇo ’pi
dhīro daiva-vaśānugaiḥ
tad vidvān na calen mārgād
anvaśikṣaṁ kṣiter vratam
original.word_for_word: bhūtaiḥ — by various creatures; ākramyamāṇaḥ — being harassed; api — although; dhīraḥ — sober; daiva — of fate; vaśa — the control; anugaiḥ — who are simply following; tat — this fact; vidvān — he who is in knowledge of; na calet — should not deviate; mārgāt — from the path; anvaśikṣam — I have learned; kṣiteḥ — from the earth; vratam — this fixed practice.

statements.statement: The earth is the symbol of tolerance. By deep oil-drilling, atomic explosions, pollution, and so on, the earth is constantly harassed by demoniac living entities. Sometimes lush forests are cut down by greedy men with commercial interests, and thus a wasteland is created. Sometimes the earth’s surface is soaked by the blood of soldiers fighting in savage warfare. Yet, despite all these disturbances, the earth continues to provide all the necessities of the living beings. In this way one may learn the art of tolerance by studying the earth.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A saintly person should learn from the mountain to devote all his efforts to the service of others and to make the welfare of others the sole reason for his existence. Similarly, as the disciple of the tree, he should learn to dedicate himself to others.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
शश्वत्परार्थसर्वेह: परार्थैकान्तसम्भव: ।
साधु: शिक्षेत भूभृत्तो नगशिष्य: परात्मताम् ॥ ३८ ॥
original.transliteration:
śaśvat parārtha-sarvehaḥ
parārthaikānta-sambhavaḥ
sādhuḥ śikṣeta bhū-bhṛtto
naga-śiṣyaḥ parātmatām
original.word_for_word: śaśvat — always; para — of others; artha — for the sake; sarva-īhaḥ — all of one’s efforts; para-artha — the benefit of others; ekānta — sole; sambhavaḥ — reason for living; sādhuḥ — a saintly person; śikṣeta — should learn; bhū-bhṛttaḥ — from the mountain; naga-śiṣyaḥ — the disciple of the tree; para-ātmatām — dedication to others.

statements.statement: Great mountains bear unlimited quantities of earth, which in turn give sustenance to innumerable forms of life such as trees, grass, birds, animals, and so on. Mountains also pour forth unlimited quantities of crystalline water in the form of waterfalls and rivers, and this water gives life to all. By studying the example of mountains, one should learn the art of providing for the happiness of all living entities. Similarly, one may take excellent lessons from the pious trees, who offer innumerable benefits, such as fruits, flowers, cooling shade and medicinal extracts. Even when a tree is suddenly cut down and dragged away, the tree does not protest but continues to give service to others in the form of firewood. Thus, one should become the disciple of such magnanimous trees and learn from them the qualities of saintly conduct.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: According to Śrīla Madhvācārya, the word parārthaikānta-sambhavaḥ indicates that one should dedicate all of one’s wealth and other assets to the welfare of others. By one’s acquired opulence, one should especially try to please the spiritual master and the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Thus, the demigods, as well as all truly respectable superior personalities, will automatically be pleased. By developing saintly conduct, as described in this verse, one will become tolerant, and this will free one from the useless agitation of the material senses, which drive one to wander throughout the world searching in vain for material happiness. Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has also emphasized the tree’s quality of tolerance: taror iva sahiṣṇunā, kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ. One who is as tolerant as a tree can chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa constantly, finding ever-new satisfaction.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Peace is the chief thing in the spiritual quest; a seeker must surely have it. Therefore, for the sake of his own peace, the first guru is the earth.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: परमार्थी मुख्य शांती । साधकांसी पाहिजे निश्चितीं । यालागीं प्रथम गुरु क्षिती । निजशांतीलागूनी

statements.statement: Inward restraint is 'śānti' (peace); restraint of the outer senses is 'dānti'; tolerance of both is 'kṣānti' (forbearance). For forbearance the earth was made guru.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अंतरनिग्रहो ते ’शांती’ । बाह्येंद्रियनिग्रहो ते ’दांती’ । उभयसहिष्णुता ते ’क्षांती’ । क्षांतीसी क्षिति गुरु केली

statements.statement: The earth herself carries on the separate dealings of those beings, but she never lets her undividedness be broken - know this - at any time.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: त्या भूतांचे भिन्न वर्तन । पृथ्वी संपादी आपण । मोडों नेदी अभिन्नपण । अखंड जाण सर्वदा

statements.statement: Such too is the mark of yogīs: while performing different actions, their disposition must ever remain unbroken and steady.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसें योगियांचे लक्षण । करितां कर्म भिन्नभिन्न । वृत्ति अखंडदंडायमान । सर्वदा जाण असावी

statements.statement: Here, beings worship the earth, or trouble her with excrement and urine; joy or sorrow never came to her; she stayed unmoved in her own forbearance.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: येथ भूतीं पृथ्वी पूजिली । नातरी विष्ठामूत्रीं गांजिली । हर्षविषादा नाहीं आली । निश्चल ठेली निजक्षांती

statements.statement: Know the yogī too to be so: he is not shaken by the unevenness of beings; amid the uneven he stays equal, contemplating his own Self in all beings.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसाचि योगियाही जाणा । भूतवैषम्यें डंडळेना । सर्वभूती निजात्मभावना । विषमीं समाना भावितां

statements.statement: Not counting it an offence, the earth immediately becomes pleasing to those beings, and growing various wealth right there, she gives satisfaction to the beings.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तो अपराधु न मनूनि क्षिती । सवेंचि भूतांतें प्रसन्न होती । तेथेंचि पिकवूनि नाना संपत्ती । तृप्ति देती भूतांतें

statements.statement: Taking the offence on one's own body, and acting for the good of the offender - that is 'śānti' in the world: strong and free of the dualities.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अपराध साहोनु अंगी । त्याच्या प्रवर्ते हितालागीं । तेचि ’शांति’ पैं जगीं । होय दाटुगी निर्द्वंद्व

statements.statement: He [the mountain] neither fixes a limit for anyone nor forbids anyone; he does not tire of them and throw them out; according to the petitioner's wish, he gives, out of benevolence.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: कोणासी नेमी ना निवारी । उबगोनि न घाली बाहेरी । याचकाचे इच्छेवरी । परोपकारीं देतसे

statements.statement: Like that mountain, in truth, generosity should be in the seeker: giving everything with joy - body, speech and mind.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: त्या पर्वता‌ऐशी तत्त्वतां । असावी साधकासी उदारता । काया वाचा आणि चित्ता । सर्वस्व देतां उल्हासु

statements.statement: To be dependent on all - with the whole body, with all feeling, at all times, in all places - this I learned from the tree.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सर्वांगें सर्वभावेंसी । सर्वकाळ सर्वदेशीं । पराधीन हो‌आवें सर्वांसी । हें वृक्षापाशीं शिकलों

statements.statement: Giving up the ego in the body, the yogī has become dependent; 'the universe is wholly my Self' - so he acts within the word of all.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सांडूनि देहींची अहंता । योगियासी झाली पराधीनता । विश्व माझा आत्मा सर्वथा । सर्वांच्या वर्तता बोला‌आंतु

statements.statement: When a guest comes to the tree, it does not deceive him; leaves, flowers, fruits, roots, shade, bark and wood - it gives them all.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अतिथि आल्या वृक्षापासीं । वंचनार्थु न करी त्यासी । पत्रपुष्पफलमूळच्छायेसीं । त्वचाकाष्ठांसी देतसे

statements.statement: When a petitioner comes to ask, not to turn away from him with all that one has - this I learned from the tree, with discernment, in my own mind.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अर्थी आल्या अर्थावयासी । विमुख न व्हावें सर्वस्वेंसी । हें शिकलों वृक्षापासीं । विवेकेंसीं निजबुद्धीं

statements.statement: As a ladder is needed to go up, so forbearance is needed by one who longs for liberation. This I learned from the earth.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: उपरि जावया शिडी जशी। सहनशीलता तशी। पाहिजे मुमुक्षूसी। हें भूमीपाशीं शिकलों मी

statements.statement: People drop excrement and urine on the earth and spit on her; yet without turning harsh, she forgives.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जेंवी भूमीवरी नर। टाकिती मळमूत्र। थुंकिती तरी त्यांवर। न होतां क्रूर क्षमा करी

statements.statement: In every way I am like a mother and these beings are like children. Whatever they may do, I should not hold it in my heart.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सर्वथा मी मातेपरी। हे जीव पोरापरी। यांहीं कांहीं केलें तरी। म्यां अंतरीं तें न धरावें

statements.statement: Keeping the eye on liberation, one should bear everything; even if people torment one, one should not be angry with them.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मोक्षार्थाकडे दृष्टि देऊन। करावें सर्व सहन। जरी पीडिती जन। त्यांवरी कोप न करावा

statements.statement: Knowing this body to be perishable, leaving it to prārabdha [the destiny already in motion] and remaining a witness, then to whom is there sorrow?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हा नश्वर देह जाणून। त्याला प्रारब्धाधीन करून। साक्षिभूत होऊन। राहतां आपण दुःख कोणा

statements.statement: Let someone call one uncultured, someone cultured, someone a fool; one should hold to forbearance.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: असभ्य कोणी म्हणो। कोणी सभ्य म्हणो। कोणी मूर्ख म्हणो। आपण क्षमा धरावी

statements.statement: He who has this forbearance in his keeping sees no enemy anywhere in the universe, since his eye is on destiny.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ही क्षमा ज्याचें पदरीं। त्याला ब्रह्मांडोदरीं। कोणी न दिसती वैरी। दैवावरी दृष्टी ज्याची

statements.statement: The uncultured becomes cultured in whose control forbearance stands; even the cultured becomes uncultured who is wrathful and has given up forbearance. [Sanskrit verse]

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: असभ्यः सभ्यतां याति क्षमा यस्य वशे स्थिता। सभ्योप्यसभ्यतां याति क्रोधनो यः क्षमोज्झितः

statements.statement: Anger is thick darkness; forbearance is the great world of the gods. The man who knows this will cross over.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: क्रोध अंधकार घोर। क्षमा ही देवलोक थोर। असा जाणे जो नर । तोचि पार जाईल

statements.statement: Let one's work be for the good of others; this birth too is for that. This itself is one's own interest, by which a man is fulfilled.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: कीजे धंदा परोपकारार्थ। हे जन्मही तदर्थ। हाची आपुला स्वार्थ। कृतार्थ हो जेणें नर

statements.statement: Though born of tamas [the quality of darkness], those trees stand always and spend their whole lives doing good to others.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जे तमःप्रभव असून। ते वृक्ष नित्य उभे राहून। परोपकार करून। सर्व जन्म घालविती

statements.statement: They are ever cheerful; though dependent on others, they do good to others, the tribe of trees, until death.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नित्य प्रसन्न असती। जरी पराधीन असती। तरी परोपकार करिती। वृक्षजाती आमरणान्त

statements.statement: As trees are of use in every way, so a man should make use of his body.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जसा सर्व प्रकारें वृक्षांचा। उपयोग होतो साचा। तसा मनुष्यानें देहाचा। उपयोग करावा

statements.statement: As those trees give rest to the weary traveller, so a householder should give rest to travellers.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जसे ते श्रमलियासी। विसांवा देती पांथांसी। तसा गृहस्थें पांथांसी। विसावा द्यावा

statements.statement: A man should recognise another's hunger and thirst and fulfil that person's wish, within the limit of his own strength.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नरें भूक तहान दुसऱ्याची। जाणूनि तयाची। पुरवावी इच्छा त्याची। करूनि शक्तिची मर्यादा

statements.statement: If, by fortune, wealth ever comes, one should not become intoxicated, just as trees do not become stiff and proud when the wealth of fruit comes to them.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: दैवें यदा कदाचित। संपत्ती येतां न व्हावें उन्मत्त। जेवीं फलसंपत्ति येतां वृक्ष। ताठा न धरिती

statements.statement: Therefore, when wealth comes, men should bow low; this is what should be learned from trees.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: यास्तव नरांनीं। संपत्ति येतां नमूनी। असावें हें वृक्षांपासूनी। घ्यावें शिकूनी उत्तमें

statements.statement: When the wealth of fruit comes to trees, they lower their heads; if someone plucks the fruit, they feel no dejection at heart.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: वृक्षाते फलसंपत्ति येतां। खालीं करिती माथा। कोणी फळें तोडितां। चित्तीं खिन्नता न धरिती

statements.statement: I took instruction from the mountain, [a product] of the earth: having gathered everything within oneself, one should keep it for the sake of helping others.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: पर्वत पृथ्वीपासून। घेतलें मी शिक्षण। पोटीं सर्व संग्रह करून। परोपकारार्थ ठेवावा

statements.statement: By effort a man should store up excellent learning and give it to people; only then is it an ornament to him.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नरें यत्नेंकरून। उत्तम विद्या सांठवून। द्यावी लोकां लागून। तरीच भूषण तयांचे होय

statements.statement: As the mountain lets forth springs of water, so a man should let forth cool, sweet, good words that truly bring peace.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जसे उदकाचे झरे। पर्वत सोडीतसे तसे नरें। थंड गोड शब्द बरे। सोडावे खरे शांतिकर

statements.statement: Because the mountain keeps various caves, saints and good people come, make their hermitages and live there.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जेंवी विविध गुहा राखून। पर्वत राही म्हणून। संतसज्जन येऊन। आश्रम करून राहती

statements.statement: So a man should give shelter to others; when good company is had, welfare will result. This is certain. This I learned from mountains.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तसा द्यावा नरें नरा आश्रय। सत्संगती होतां श्रेय। होईल हा निश्चय। पर्वतांपासून हें शिकलों

statements.statement: Thus, cleverly, I made the earth my guru, took this instruction, and remained at peace.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: चतुरपणें असा म्यां। पृथ्वी गुरु करुनियां। असा उपदेश घेऊनियां। शांत होऊनियां राहिलो

statements.statement: A learned sage should take his satisfaction in the simple maintenance of his existence and should not seek satisfaction through gratifying the material senses. In other words, one should care for the material body in such a way that one’s higher knowledge is not destroyed and so that one’s speech and mind are not deviated from self-realization.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
प्राणवृत्त्यैव सन्तुष्येन्मुनिर्नैवेन्द्रियप्रियै: ।
ज्ञानं यथा न नश्येत नावकीर्येत वाङ्‍मन: ॥ ३९ ॥
original.transliteration:
prāṇa-vṛttyaiva santuṣyen
munir naivendriya-priyaiḥ
jñānaṁ yathā na naśyeta
nāvakīryeta vāṅ-manaḥ
original.word_for_word: prāṇa-vṛttyā — with the mere functioning of his vital air; eva — even; santuṣyet — should be satisfied; muniḥ — a sage; na — not; eva — indeed; indriya-priyaiḥ — with things that gratify the senses; jñānam — consciousness; yathā — so that; na naśyeta — may not be destroyed; na avakīryeta — may not become disturbed; vāk — his speech; manaḥ — and mind.

statements.statement: A wise man does not absorb his consciousness in the forms, flavors, aromas and sensations of material sense gratification, but rather accepts activities such as eating and sleeping simply to keep body and soul together. One must properly maintain one’s body by regulated activities of eating, sleeping, cleansing, etc., otherwise the mind will become weak, and one’s spiritual knowledge will fade away. If one eats too austerely, or if in the name of selflessness one accepts impure food, surely one loses control of the mind. On the other hand, if one eats food that is excessively fatty or rich there will be an unwanted increase in sleep and semen, and thus the mind and speech will be overwhelmed by the modes of passion and ignorance. Lord Kṛṣṇa has summarized the whole matter in Bhagavad-gītā by His statement yuktāhāra-vihārasya yukta-ceṣṭasya karmasu. One should moderately and intelligently regulate all of one’s bodily activities so that they are favorable for self-realization. This technique is taught by the bona fide spiritual master. If one is too austere or if one engages too much in sense gratification, self-realization is impossible.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: It is the duty of a devotee of the Lord to avoid seeing any object as separate from Kṛṣṇa, because that is illusion. A gentleman will never try to enjoy the property of another gentleman. Similarly, if one sees everything in relation to Kṛṣṇa, there is no scope for material sense gratification. But if one sees material objects as separate from Kṛṣṇa, then one’s material enjoying propensity is immediately aroused. A human being must be intelligent enough to distinguish between preyas, or temporary gratification, and śreyas, permanent benefit. One may accept sense activity in a regulated, limited fashion so that one will be strong for serving Kṛṣṇa, but if one excessively indulges the material senses, one will lose one’s gravity and seriousness in spiritual life and act like an ordinary materialist. The ultimate goal, as stated here, is jñānam, or steady consciousness of the Absolute Truth, Lord Kṛṣṇa.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Even a transcendentalist is surrounded by innumerable material objects, which possess good and bad qualities. However, one who has transcended material good and evil should not become entangled even when in contact with the material objects; rather, he should act like the wind.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
विषयेष्वाविशन् योगी नानाधर्मेषु सर्वत: ।
गुणदोषव्यपेतात्मा न विषज्जेत वायुवत् ॥ ४० ॥
original.transliteration:
viṣayeṣv āviśan yogī
nānā-dharmeṣu sarvataḥ
guṇa-doṣa-vyapetātmā
na viṣajjeta vāyu-vat
original.word_for_word: viṣayeṣu — into contact with material objects; āviśan — entering; yogī — one who has attained self-control; nānā-dharmeṣu — which have different varieties of qualities; sarvataḥ — everywhere; guṇa — good qualities; doṣa — and faults; vyapeta-ātmā — a person who has transcended; na viṣajjeta — should not become entangled; vāyu-vat — like the wind.

statements.statement: The wind is the external manifestation of air, whereas prāṇa is the internal manifestation. When the wind passes over waterfalls it carries sprinkles of clear water and thus becomes most refreshing. Sometimes the wind blows through a beautiful forest, carrying the fragrances of fruits and flowers; at other times the wind may fuel a fire that burns the same forest to ashes. The wind, however, being fixed in its own nature, remains neutral in both its auspicious and inauspicious activities. Similarly, within this material world we will inevitably face both pleasing and disgusting situations. If, however, we remain fixed in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, we will not be disturbed by the inauspicious, nor will we become attached to the materially auspicious. In the course of his spiritual duties, a devotee sometimes finds himself chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa in a beautiful country atmosphere, and sometimes he finds himself doing the same thing in a hellish city. In both cases the devotee fixes his mind upon Lord Kṛṣṇa and experiences transcendental bliss. Although the wind passes through the most dark and forbidding places, the wind is not frightened or disturbed. Similarly, a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa should never be fearful or anxious, even when in the most difficult situation. One who is attached to materially pleasing forms, tastes, smells, sounds and touches will also be repelled by the opposite in each category. Thus finding himself surrounded by innumerable good and bad things, the materialist is constantly disturbed. When the wind blows in many directions at once, the atmosphere becomes agitated. Similarly, if the mind is constantly attracted and repelled by material objects there will be such mental disturbance that it will be impossible to think of the Absolute Truth. Therefore, one should learn from the blowing wind the art of moving throughout the material world without attachment.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Although a self-realized soul may live in various material bodies while in this world, experiencing their various qualities and functions, he is never entangled, just as the wind which carries various aromas does not actually mix with them.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
पार्थिवेष्विह देहेषु प्रविष्टस्तद्गुणाश्रय: ।
गुणैर्न युज्यते योगी गन्धैर्वायुरिवात्मद‍ृक् ॥ ४१ ॥
original.transliteration:
pārthiveṣv iha deheṣu
praviṣṭas tad-guṇāśrayaḥ
guṇair na yujyate yogī
gandhair vāyur ivātma-dṛk
original.word_for_word: pārthiveṣu — composed of earth (and other elements); iha — in this world; deheṣu — within bodies; praviṣṭaḥ — having entered; tat — of them; guṇa — the characteristic qualities; āśrayaḥ — having assumed; guṇaiḥ — with those qualities; na yujyate — does not entangle himself; yogī — a yogī; gandhaiḥ — with different odors; vāyuḥ — the air; iva — just as; ātma-dṛk — he who can see himself properly (as separate from this matter).

statements.statement: Although we experience the wind as fragrant or foul, depending on the aromas it carries, the wind does not in fact change its actual nature. Similarly, although we regard a particular person as strong or weak, intelligent or retarded, beautiful or homely, good or bad, the pure spirit soul, who is the actual person, does not really possess any of the qualities of the body but is merely covered by them, just as the wind is covered by different aromas. Thus, a Kṛṣṇa conscious person is always aware that he is different from the temporary body. He experiences the various transformations of the body, such as childhood, adolescence, adulthood and old age; but although he experiences the pains, pleasures, qualities and functions of that body, a Kṛṣṇa conscious person never thinks that he is the body. He always understands that he is an eternal spirit soul, part and parcel of Lord Kṛṣṇa. As stated in this verse, na yujyate yogī: he is not entangled. The conclusion is that one should never consider a Kṛṣṇa conscious person in terms of bodily designation, but should see him as an eternal servitor of the Lord.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The guruhood that is in air - listen - is of two kinds: one is the prāṇa (vital breath) with its functions; the other is the outer air.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: गुरुत्व जें वायूसी । तें दों प्रकारीं परियेसीं । एक तें प्राण वृत्तीसीं । बाह्य वायूसी दुसरें

statements.statement: Like the prāṇa, he who holds no attachment in sense-objects: even after enjoying the objects he does not become egoistic, as the prāṇa does not.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: प्राणाचियेपरी । जो विषयीं आसक्ती न धरी । विषय सेविलियाही वरी । नव्हे अहंकारी प्राणु जैसा

statements.statement: Just so is the yogī: he holds no pride in the body; he enjoys objects, but has no attachment at all to them.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसाचि योगिया पाहीं । तो अभिमान न धरी देहीं । विषयो सेवी परी कांही । आसक्ति नाहीं तयासी

statements.statement: So that the steadiness of knowledge does not slip and the senses do not become weak, one should take food by the force of skill, solely with one's own firmness.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ज्ञानधारणा न ढळे । इंद्रियें नव्हती विकळें । तैसा आहार युक्तिबळें । सेविजे केवळें निजधैर्यें

statements.statement: As is the state of the prāṇa, so does the yogī's disposition act: doing everything, he has no attachment; he does not touch the body's condition.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: त्या प्राणाच्या ऐसी स्थिती । योगियाची वर्तती वृत्ती । सर्व करूनि न करी आसक्ती । देहस्थिति नातळे

statements.statement: Whether to nourish the body of Brahmā and others or to avoid the body of swine and others - the compassionate prāṇa holds no such impurity; it is of equal feeling.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ब्रह्मादिकांचा देह पाळूं । कां सूकरादिकांचा देह टाळूं । ऐसा न मानीच विटाळू । प्राणु कृपाळु समभावें

statements.statement: Prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna - and vyāna dwells in all the joints; though it has reached so many names and places, the prāṇa does not give up its oneness.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: प्राण अपान समान उदान । सर्व संधी वसे व्यान । इतुकीं नामें स्थानें पावोनि जाण । न सांडी प्राण एकपणा

statements.statement: Though the prāṇa is within the body, it makes no difference from the outer air; so the yogī makes his feeling: oneness inside and outside.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: प्राणु असोनि देहाभीतरीं । बाह्य वायूसी भेद न धरी । तैशी योगिया भावना करी । बाह्यभ्यंतरीं ऐक्यता

statements.statement: The wind goes touching everything, but it does not stay stuck anywhere; so the yogī, while enjoying objects, does not become attached.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: वायु सर्वांतें स्पर्शोनि जाये । परी अडकला कोठें न राहे । तैसें विषय सेवितां पाहे । आसक्तु नव्हे योगिया

statements.statement: As the flame flares up by the wind, but the wind is not caught in the flame, so the yogī, though enjoying enjoyments intensely, is not caught in the enjoyments.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जैसें वारेनीं जाळ उडे । परी जाळीं वारा नातुडे । तेवीं भोग भोगितां गाढे । भोगीं नातुडे योगिया

statements.statement: By the strength of the vision of the Self he does not touch the qualities of the body, as the wind rolls over fragrance yet is not seized by fragrance.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: निजात्मदृष्टीचेनि बळें । तो देहगुणांसी नातळे । जैसा गंधावरी वारा लोळे । परी नाकळे गंधासी

statements.statement: 'The dispassionate are liberated'; such are the views. Even if forbearance is established in one, without dispassion it is useless.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: विरताः परिमुच्यंते। असीं असती मतें। जरी क्षमा अंगीं ठरे ते। विरक्ततेवांचूनि व्यर्थ

statements.statement: Though forbearance is in him, if he is outward-turned and enjoys sense-objects he is not dispassionate; then how will he be a yogi?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: क्षमा असोनी अंगीं। बहिर्मुख विषय भोगी। न होय तो विरागी। मग योगी कसा होईल

statements.statement: One who, looking for no other relish, takes satisfaction in food as mere nourishment, to him fitness comes; this is understood by taking the air as guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो अन्य गोडी न पाहतां। आहारमात्रें घे तृप्तता। त्याला ये योग्यता। वायु गुरु करितां हें कळे

statements.statement: When the life-breath gets no food it truly becomes slack; when it gets mere food, it expects no taste.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: प्राणवायु अन्न न मिळतां। शिथिल होय तत्वतां। आहारमात्र मिळतां। रसाची अपेक्षा न ठेवी

statements.statement: The life-breath takes whatever chewed food it gets, keeps its own work going, and stays cheerful.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जें चर्वित अन्न। मिळे तें सेवून। आपुला व्यापार चालवून। राहे प्रसन्न प्राणवायू

statements.statement: The food that is one's own, got by the working of destiny: with that one's mind must be made content.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जें खाद्य असे आपुलें। दैवयोगें मिळालें। म्हणजे मन आपुलें। समाधान केलें पाहिजे

statements.statement: When both of these [mind and speech] become empty, knowledge will be ruined; then from where will liberation come to one lolling in bed?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हीं शून्य होतां दोनीं। ज्ञान जाईल नासूनी। मग मुक्ति तरी कोठूनी। येईल शयनीं लोळतां

statements.statement: Then even bliss will be wholly broken; without moderate eating, yoga will be wholly defective.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: आनंदाचाही मग। सर्वथा होईल भंग। मिताहार नसतां योग। सर्वथा व्यंग होईल

statements.statement: One who eats very tasty food to his fill, his mind too gets distracted, and meditation does not happen at all.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो बहु स्वादिष्ट अन्न। खाई पोटभरून। त्याचेंही चित्त विक्षेपून। न होय ध्यान सर्वथा

statements.statement: The tongue knows all tastes; the moment one follows her lead, one misses the supreme goal and takes birth again.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सर्व रस रसना जाणे। तिच्या नादा लागतां क्षणें। परमार्थापासूनी मुकणें। जन्म घेणें घडे पुनः

statements.statement: Whether a man is learned or unlearned, if he conquers all tastes he alone is to be known as God, though a man in body.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सुविद्य अथवा अविद्य नर। सर्व रस जिंकी तर। तोची जाणावा ईश्वर। हो कां नर देहानें

statements.statement: Whether one wishes or not, when sense-enjoyments come by destiny, one should keep no attachment; this is learned by taking the air as guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नरें इच्छा असतां किंवा नसतां। दैवें विषयभोग मिळतां। न ठेवावी आसक्तता। वायु गुरू करितां कळे हें

statements.statement: The wind, moving, meets cold and heat on the way but is not attached; it is not touched by good or bad qualities.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो गति करिता वात। शीत उष्ण मार्गात। भेटतां न हो आसक्त। न शिवे तो गुणदोषां

statements.statement: A man should live in his pure nature, should not take account of good and bad qualities, should move among cold and heat, and should not linger anywhere.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नरें शुद्ध स्वभावें रहावें। गुणदोषादि न मानावें। शीतोष्णांत फिरावें। न रमावें कोठेंही

statements.statement: Even while living in the body, one should give up ego-sense, as the wind, though it carries the fragrance, remains separate from it.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: देहामध्येंही राहून। अहंपणा द्यावा सोडून। जसा गंधाश्रय होऊन। जसा पवन वेगळा

statements.statement: A wise embodied person, even if he takes sense-objects by destiny, sees himself as separate and does not form a connection with the objects.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो सुधी देहधारी। दैवें विषय घे जरी। आपणां वेगळा पाहे तरी। न धरी विषयसंबंधासी

statements.statement: In these two ways, knowing the air [as inner breath and as outer wind], I took this instruction and gave up attachment to taste.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हे दोन प्रकारेंकरून। अंतर्बाह्य वायु जाणून। म्यां घेतलें हें शिक्षण। दिली सोडून रसासक्ती

statements.statement: Of all practices, to remain content with the life-breath [food only to sustain life], always leaving attachment to taste, is the best practice.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: समस्त साधनांहून। प्राणवृत्तीनें संतोषून। राहणें हें उत्तम साधन। नित्य सोडून रसासक्ती

statements.statement: A thoughtful sage, even while living within a material body, should understand himself to be pure spirit soul. Similarly, one should see that the spirit soul enters within all forms of life, both moving and nonmoving, and that the individual souls are thus all-pervading. The sage should further observe that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, as the Supersoul, is simultaneously present within all things. Both the individual soul and the Supersoul can be understood by comparing them to the nature of the sky: although the sky extends everywhere and everything rests within the sky, the sky does not mix with anything, nor can it be divided by anything.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
अन्तर्हितश्च स्थिरजङ्गमेषु
ब्रह्मात्मभावेन समन्वयेन ।
व्याप्त्याव्यवच्छेदमसङ्गमात्मनो
मुनिर्नभस्त्वं विततस्य भावयेत् ॥ ४२ ॥
original.transliteration:
antarhitaś ca sthira-jaṅgameṣu
brahmātma-bhāvena samanvayena
vyāptyāvyavacchedam asaṅgam ātmano
munir nabhastvaṁ vitatasya bhāvayet
original.word_for_word: antarhitaḥ — present within; ca — also; sthira — all nonmoving living bodies; jaṅgameṣu — and all moving forms of life; brahma-ātma-bhāvena — by realization that he himself is pure spirit; samanvayena — as a result of the different contacts (with different bodies); vyāptyā — because of being all-pervading; avyavacchedam — the feature of being undivided; asaṅgam — being unattached; ātmanaḥ — possessed by the Supersoul; muniḥ — a sage; nabhastvam — the similarity with the sky; vitatasya — of the expansive; bhāvayet — should meditate upon.

statements.statement: Although air exists within the sky, the sky, or space, is different from air. Even in the absence of air, space or sky is present. All material objects are situated within space, or within the vast material sky, but the sky remains undivided and, although accommodating all objects, never actually mixes with anything. In the same way one can understand the situation of both the individual soul and the Supersoul. The individual soul is all-pervading, because there are innumerable jīvātmās, which enter within all things; yet, as confirmed in Vedic literature, each individual ātmā remains infinitesimal. The Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad (5.9) states:

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement:
bālāgra-śata-bhāgasya
śatadhā kalpitasya ca
bhāgo jīvaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ
sa cānantyāya kalpate

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: “When the upper point of a hair is divided into one hundred parts and again each of such parts is further divided into one hundred parts, each such part is the measurement of the dimension of the spirit soul.” The same is stated in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam:

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement:
keśāgra-śata-bhāgasya
śatāṁśaḥ sādṛśātmakaḥ
jīvaḥ sūkṣma-svarūpo ’yaṁ
saṅkhyātīto hi cit-kaṇaḥ

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: “There are innumerable particles of spiritual atoms, which are measured as one ten-thousandth of the upper portion of the hair.”

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, however, is all-pervading because He Himself is personally present everywhere. The Lord is known as advaita, or indivisible. Thus the same unique Personality of Godhead exists everywhere, just like the sky, and yet is not attached to anything, although everything is resting within Him. The Lord Himself has confirmed this analysis of His all-pervasiveness in Bhagavad-gītā (9.6):

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement:
yathākāśa-sthito nityaṁ
vāyuḥ sarvatra-go mahān
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni
mat-sthānīty upadhāraya

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: “As the almighty wind, blowing everywhere, always rests in ethereal space, know that in the same manner all beings rest in Me.”

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Therefore, although both the jīva soul and the Supersoul are said to be all-pervading, it should be remembered that there are innumerable individual jīva souls, whereas there is only one Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Lord is always supreme, and one who is actually a thoughtful sage never doubts the supreme position of the Lord.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Although the mighty wind blows clouds and storms across the sky, the sky is never implicated or affected by these activities. Similarly, the spirit soul is not actually changed or affected by contact with the material nature. Although the living entity enters within a body made of earth, water and fire, and although he is impelled by the three modes of nature created by eternal time, his eternal spiritual nature is never actually affected.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
तेजोऽबन्नमयैर्भावैर्मेघाद्यैर्वायुनेरितै: ।
न स्पृश्यते नभस्तद्वत् कालसृष्टैर्गुणै: पुमान् ॥ ४३ ॥
original.transliteration:
tejo-’b-anna-mayair bhāvair
meghādyair vāyuneritaiḥ
na spṛśyate nabhas tadvat
kāla-sṛṣṭair guṇaiḥ pumān
original.word_for_word: tejaḥ — fire; ap — water; anna — and earth; mayaiḥ — consisting of; bhāvaiḥ — by objects; megha-ādyaiḥ — clouds and so on; vāyunā — by the wind; īritaiḥ — which are blown; na spṛśyate — is not touched; nabhaḥ — the ethereal sky; tat-vat — in the same way; kāla-sṛṣṭaiḥ — which have been sent forth by time; guṇaiḥ — by the modes of nature; pumān — a person.

statements.statement: Although the sky appears to be affected by the mighty movements of wind, rain, hurricanes, lightning and thunder, etc., the sky, being very subtle, is actually not affected, but is rather the background for such visible activities. Similarly, although the material body and mind undergo innumerable changes, such as birth and death, happiness and distress, love and hate, the eternal living entity is merely the background for such activities. The spirit soul, being most subtle, is not actually affected; only due to misidentification with the superficial activities of the body and mind does the soul undergo terrible distress within the material world.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: In this regard, Śrīla Madhvācārya has pointed out that the individual living entity must struggle to revive his divine spiritual qualities. The living entity is part and parcel of the supreme entity, called Kṛṣṇa, and as such the individual soul is also a reservoir of godly qualities. The Personality of Godhead, however, automatically manifests these qualities without any hindrance, whereas the conditioned soul must struggle to revive such qualities. Thus, although both the Personality of Godhead and the personality of the living entity are eternal and transcendental, the Personality of Godhead is always supreme. By realizing all this with clear intelligence, the conditioned soul can rise to the spiritual platform.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Equality in all things - for this reason guruhood belongs to the sky - knowing its non-attachment, non-difference and purity.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सर्व पदार्थी समत्व । यालागीं आकाशासी गुरुत्व । असंगत्व अभेदत्व । निर्मळत्व जाणोनी

statements.statement: Though in the uneven, equality; though in contact, non-attachment; though making difference, non-difference - therefore guruhood belongs to the sky.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: विषमीं असोनि समत्व । संगीं असोनि असंगत्व । भेदु करितां अभेदत्व । यालागीं गुरुत्व आकाशा

statements.statement: There is enmity between snake and mongoose, yet the sky dwells in the heart of both; to the sky enmity is non-enmity; that state the yogī should have.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: वैर सर्पामुंगुसांसी । आकाश दोंहीचे हृदयवासी । वैर निर्वैरता आकाशासी । ते स्थिती योगियासी पाहिजे

statements.statement: The sky is in all things, yet that it is there is not seen by all; so, in a state beyond the seen and the seer, the yogī is everywhere.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: आकाश सर्व पदार्थीं असे । परी असे हें सर्वासी न दिसे । तेवीं दृश्य-द्रष्टा-अतीतदशें । सर्वत्र असे योगिया

statements.statement: The sky appears drowned in a pool, yet it has not got wet by the water; so, though he is in all bodies, the yogī is unattached.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: गगन बुडालें दिसे डोहीं । परी तें उदकें भिजलेंचि नाहीं । तैसा असोनियां सर्व देहीं । अलिप्त पाहीं योगिया

statements.statement: If someone goes to smear mud on the sky, it is not smeared - the one who smears gets smeared; so if one calls the yogī guilty, the fault wholly belongs to the one who says so.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: आकाशा चिखल माखूं जातां । तें न माखे माखे लाविता । तैसा योगिया दोषी म्हणतां । दोषु सर्वथा म्हणत्यासी

statements.statement: The sky, though among the people, is not soiled by the rubbing of the people; so the yogī, doing all actions, is not soiled in his doing of action.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: गगन असोनियां जनीं । मैळेना जनघसणीं । तैसा योगिया सकळ कर्में करूनी । कर्मठपणीं न मैळे

statements.statement: If one tries to tie the sky into bundles, the four ends fall empty; so when actions bind the yogī, the action there is non-action.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मोटे बांधितां आकाशातें । चारी पालव पडती रिते । तेवीं कर्मी बांधितां योगियातें । कर्म तेथें निष्कर्म

statements.statement: When a thundering cloud comes and covers the sky, the sky touches none of it; it stays established, unattached, by its own strength.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: कडकडीत आभाळें । ये‌ऊनि आकाश झांकोळे । त्या समस्तां नभ नातळे । अलिप्त बळें संस्थित

statements.statement: So it is with the yogī: when he abides in union with his own Self, he does not come under the sway of the qualities that Time has created.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसेंचि योगियासी । असतां निजात्मसमरसीं । काळें सृजिलिया गुणांसी । वश्य त्यांसी तो नव्हे

statements.statement: Time, which devours the bodies of Brahmā and others, bows at the feet of the yogī; he who has become the very Self of Time is fearless Mahākāla.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जो ब्रह्मादि देहांसी खाये । तो काळु वंदी योगियाचे पाये । जो काळाचाही आत्मा होये । निधडा पाहें महाकाळु

statements.statement: The ātman pervades the moving and the unmoving, remains one and unchanging, and stays immovable. This knowledge I learned from the sky.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: आत्मा चराचर व्यापून। निर्विकारपणें एक असून। राहे अचळ असें ज्ञान। आकाशापासून शिकलों

statements.statement: In the bodies of the moving and the unmoving, know the ātman to be one, as the sky, though in many pots, is one.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: चराचर देहांतरीं। आत्मा एकची अवधारीं। जेवी नाना घटांतरीं।असे आकाश तरी एक

statements.statement: The ātman who is the witness, even if he appears as having qualities, is not inert; he is the one ātman of being, consciousness and bliss.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो साक्षिभूत आत्मा। तो जरी भासला गुणात्मा। तरी तो नोहे जडात्मा। सच्चिदानंदात्मा एक तो

statements.statement: Though this is true, because there is a veil it does not impress itself on the mind; therefore one should reflect on this.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हें खरेपण असून। आवरण आहे म्हणून। मना न ये ठसून। म्हणून विचार करावा हा

statements.statement: Know that for these various bodies, time, karma and the guṇas are the cause; as long as the cause remains, so long know this difference [multiplicity] to remain.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ह्या विविध देहासी जाण तूं। काल कर्म गुण हेतू। जोंवरी असे हेतू। तंव वरी जाण तूं भेद हा

statements.statement: That which agitates the guṇas, people call Time; and the one occasion for birth, O king, listen, is karma.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: गुणां चा जो क्षोभक। त्याला काळ म्हणती लोक। जें जन्माला निमित्त एक। नृपा ऐक कर्म तें

statements.statement: The threefold guṇas, sattva, rajas and tamas, are the material cause, as clay is the cause of a pot.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जे त्रिविध गुण। सत्त्व रज तम म्हणून। तेंचि उपादान कारण। घड्याला कारण माती जसी

statements.statement: Even if all bodies die, the ātman neither dies nor kills; like the sky he is unchanging, all-pervading, one.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: समस्त देह मेले तरी। आत्मा न मरे न मारी। तो आकाशाचे परी। निर्विकारी व्यापक एक

statements.statement: Let the bodies look fine; they are transformations of fire, food [earth] and water, and they come and go like clouds in the sky by the force of the wind.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हो कां भलीं दिसोंत शरीरें। तीं तेजोन्नजलविकारें। येती जाती जसीं अभ्रें। वायूच्या जोरें आकाशीं

statements.statement: The ātman, the one controller, pervades all bodies; though the bodies are many, this inner Self is one.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो नियंता आत्मा एक। तो सर्व देहव्यापक। जरी देह अनेक। तरी एक प्रत्यगात्मा हा

statements.statement: Though it seems that he moves and walks with the body, he neither moves nor walks. So I have known, O king.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: देहासह तो हाले चाले। असे जरी भासले। तरी तो न हाले न चाले। असें जाणिलें म्यां राजा

statements.statement: The appearance of shape that the ātman seems to have through association with the body is like the appearance of shape that the sky seems to have through a pot.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो देहयोगे आत्म्यास। दिसे आकाराचा भास। तो जेवीं आकाशास। घड्यानें आकाराभास दिसे तसा

statements.statement: Though the sky is motionless, it seems to move along with the pot; but it is not so.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जरी अचळ आकाश असे। तरी घड्याबरोबर जसें। चालतसे असें भासे। परी नसे तसें तें

statements.statement: The ātman is thus without appearance; who can destroy him? As, when a pot breaks, the sky, being indestructible, does not break.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: आत्मा यापरी निराभास। त्याचा कोण करील नाश। जसा घडा फुटतां आकाश। अविनाश न फुटे

statements.statement: The lump of clay breaks; so, when the body-lump dies, the ātman, who is firm, does not die; he is unbroken, unborn, forever.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: फुटे मृत्तिकेचा पिंड। तेवीं मरतां देहपिंड। आत्मा न मरे जो सुदृढ। तो अखंड अज सदैव

statements.statement: He becomes a conqueror of death, the one who contemplates That; before him poor Death is helpless. The inner Self is that alone; thus is the discrimination of Brahman made.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हो मृत्युंजय तच्चिंतक। त्यापुढे बापुडा अंतक। जो प्रत्यगात्मा तेंच एक। ब्रह्मविवेक असा केला

statements.statement: For him there is no association with the three bodies; this difference is truly not real [for him]. The disciple of the sky knows this.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तया तीनीं देहांचा। संग नसे तयाचा। भेद नोहे हा साचा। आकाशाचा शिष्य जाणे हें

statements.statement: Those who, having crossed the shoreless ocean of ignorance by the boat of knowledge, reach the inner Self, which is like the sky, in non-difference. [Sanskrit verse]

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ये तीर्त्वाऽपारमज्ञानसागरं ज्ञाननौकया। आकाशकल्पमात्मानं प्रत्यञ्चं यांत्यभेदतः

statements.statement: O king, thus I obtained this knowledge by making the sky my guru, and through oneness I left fear behind.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: असें विज्ञान म्यां राया। आकाश गुरू करूनियां। मिळविलें म्हणूनियां। सोडिलें भया एकत्वें

statements.statement: O King, a saintly person is just like water because he is free from all contamination, gentle by nature, and by speaking creates a beautiful vibration like that of flowing water. Just by seeing, touching or hearing such a saintly person, the living entity is purified, just as one is cleansed by contact with pure water. Thus a saintly person, just like a holy place, purifies all those who contact him because he always chants the glories of the Lord.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
स्वच्छ: प्रकृतित: स्‍निग्धो माधुर्यस्तीर्थभूर्नृणाम् ।
मुनि: पुनात्यपां मित्रमीक्षोपस्पर्शकीर्तनै: ॥ ४४ ॥
original.transliteration:
svacchaḥ prakṛtitaḥ snigdho
mādhuryas tīrtha-bhūr nṛṇām
muniḥ punāty apāṁ mitram
īkṣopasparśa-kīrtanaiḥ
original.word_for_word: svacchaḥ — pure; prakṛtitaḥ — by nature; snigdhaḥ — soft or softhearted; mādhuryaḥ — sweet or gentle speech; tīrtha-bhūḥ — a place of pilgrimage; nṛṇām — for human beings; muniḥ — a sage; punāti — sanctifies; apām — of the water; mitram — the exact counterpart; īkṣā — by being seen; upasparśa — by being respectfully touched; kīrtanaiḥ — and by being glorified verbally.

statements.statement: The words apāṁ mitram, “just like water,” can also be read as aghān mitram, which means that a saintly person purifies all living entities by accepting them as mitram, or his personal friends, and saves them from their sinful reactions (aghāt). The conditioned living entity falsely identifies with his gross material body and subtle mind and thus falls from the platform of spiritual knowledge. A conditioned living being is always lusty for material sense gratification, and if he does not acquire it, he becomes angry. Sometimes he is so obsessed with fear of losing his material gratification that he enters a stage approaching madness.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A saintly person, however, is like pure water, free from all contamination and capable of purifying all things. Just as pure water is transparent, a saintly person transparently manifests the Personality of Godhead within his heart. Such love of Godhead is the reservoir of all happiness. Water makes a most pleasing vibration as it flows and cascades, and similarly the sound vibration of the Lord’s pure devotee, who is saturated with the glories of the Lord, is most charming and beautiful. Thus, by studying the nature of water one can understand the symptoms of a pure devotee of the Lord.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Looking at the marks of water: by nature very pure, by its nature soft, wholly sweet to all.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: लक्षणें पाहतां जळ । स्वभावें अतिनिर्मळ । प्रकृतीस्तव कोमळ । मधुर केवळ सर्वांसी

statements.statement: To purify living beings, water has the nature of a sacred ford in the holy places; all these marks should be in the yogī day and night.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पवित्र व्हावया प्राणियांसी । तीर्थीं तीर्थत्व उदकासी । इतुकीं लक्षणें योगीयासी । अहर्निशीं असावीं

statements.statement: Those who enter the water with dirt, it makes clean by its nature; yet it holds no pride of strength: 'I have washed away these impurities.'

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: उदकीं रिघाले जे समैळ । ते स्वभावें करी निर्मळ । परी न धरी अहंबळ । जे म्यां हे मळ क्षाळिले

statements.statement: So, for those who are devoted to worship and wholly sincere in feeling, the yogī removes the dirt of Kali from them, yet holds no pride of guruhood.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसें योगियासी भजनशीळ । भावें भाविक जे केवळ । त्यांचे निरसूनि कळिमळ । न धरी बळ गुरुत्वें

statements.statement: Even if life departs, no hardness arises in his mind toward living beings; to whomever he meets, how gentle is his conduct.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: प्राणु गेला तरी प्राणियांसी । कठिणत्व उपजेना मानसीं । जें जें भेटे तयासी । मृदुता कैसी वर्तत

statements.statement: As moonbeams to the cakora birds, as the wing's shelter to the chicks, as water to living beings, so is the yogī's gentleness to all.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जेवीं चंद्रकिरण चकोरांसी । पांखोवा जेवीं पिलियांसी । जीवन जैसें कां जीवांसी । तेवीं सर्वांसी मृदुत्व

statements.statement: Water washes away dirt on the surface; the yogī makes one clean inside and out; water gives happiness once; the yogī is the giver of happiness at all times.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जळ वरिवरी क्षाळी मळ । योगिया सबाह्य करी निर्मळ । उदक सुखी करी एक वेळ । योगी सर्वकाळ सुखदाता

statements.statement: How much is the happiness of water? In a moment they are thirsty again; the yogī gives the satisfaction of Self-bliss; in that happiness there is no change at all.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: उदकाचें सुख तें किती । सवेंचि क्षणें तृषितें होती । योगिया दे स्वानंदतृप्ती । सुखासी विकृती पैं नाहीं

statements.statement: Likewise the yogī's coming down, his taking birth in this world: he cools the people by hearing and kīrtana, and uplifts them by his own knowledge.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसें योगियासी खालुतें येणें । जे इहलोकीं जन्म पावणें । जन निववी श्रवणकीर्तनें । निजज्ञानें उद्धरी

statements.statement: Such is the sight of a yogī: it does not come without good fortune; whoever has seen his feet, he frees from the disease of worldly existence.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसें योगियाचें दर्शन । भाग्येंवीण नव्हे जाण । ज्याने देखिले त्याचे चरण । करी मोचन भवरोगा

statements.statement: If sight and touch cannot happen, then one should remember his name; by that alone, that name cuts the root of worldly existence.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: न घडे दर्शन स्पर्शन । तरी करावें त्याचें नामस्मरण । इतुकेनि भवमूळ जाण । करी छेदन तें नाम

statements.statement: He who is without beginning or end, the Lord Śrī Datta, says: O king, one should always be clear [pure] like water.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो आद्यन्तरहित। तो भगवान् श्रीदत्त। म्हणे राया सतत। स्वच्छ असावें उदकापरी

statements.statement: In this world one should always keep affection for all, day and night. One should not be bitter to anyone; such should be one's conduct.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नित्य या जगीं सर्वाशीं। स्नेह ठेवावा दिवानिशीं। कडू न व्हावें कोणासी। रहाटी अशी असावी

statements.statement: Speech that is like nectar one should speak in measure; keeping sweetness toward all, one should live from day to day.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जे अमृतासम भाषण। तें परिमित बोलून। सर्वाशीं गोडी ठेवून। अनुदिन वागावें

statements.statement: When one speaks sweetly, like nectar, all are truly drawn. By making water one's guru, this quality comes to hand.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: अमृतप्राय गोड बोलतां। सर्व वळती तत्वतां। उदकाला गुरु करितां। ये हातां हा गुण

statements.statement: As sweet, clear water is naturally pure, therefore all people run when they see water.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जसें मधुर स्वच्छ जळ। स्वभावें असे निर्मळ। म्हणोनी लोक सकळ। पाहतां जळ धांवती

statements.statement: In the same way a man should have sweet speech, keep affection for all, and wear himself out for all, constantly, like water.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नरें तेवीं गोड भाषण। सर्वाशीं स्नेह ठेवून। सर्वात जावें खपून। उदकासमान निरंतर

statements.statement: Sprinkled on the body, drunk, taken as a sip for rinsing the mouth, or even looked at, or bathed in, water purifies.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जळ अंगी प्रोक्षितां। पितां आचमन करितां। किंवा दृष्टीनें पाहतां। स्नान करितां पवित्र करी

statements.statement: People do all their work with water again and again, yet it truly does not tire of it; a man should keep such conduct.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सर्व धंदे जळावर। लोक करिती वारंवार। परी तें न विटे साचार। तसा आचार नरें ठेवावा

statements.statement: A man who always stays clean, by his mere sight a being becomes pure. Such is the character of cleanliness.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सतत स्वच्छ राहे नर। त्याचें होतां दर्शनमात्र। प्राणी होई पवित्र। असे चरित्र स्वच्छतेचें

statements.statement: One who bows to him or serves him, the clean man carries across, constantly, like the water of a sacred place.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो नमः (स्)कार करी। किंवा सेवा करी। तयातें स्वच्छ नर तारी। तीर्थजळापरी निरंतर

statements.statement: A man should hold on to excellence and live like water: being pure himself, he should make others pure.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नरें प्रशस्तपणा धरून। जलाप्रमाणें राहून। स्वयें पवित्र असून। इतरां पवित्र करावें

statements.statement: This is its special quality: water keeps the dirt in its belly, yet is clean outside, and washes away the dirt of others.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हाच विशेष गुण। जळ पोटीं मळ ठेवून। बाहेर स्वच्छ असून। करी मळ क्षालन इतरांचें

statements.statement: Without doubt this body is the house of filth, urine and phlegm, a collection of the five elements; why have attachment to it?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो निःशंकपणें हा देह। मळमूत्रकफांचें गेह। पंच भूतांचा समूह। तयाचा मोह कासया

statements.statement: The wise man, never holding attachment, gains with this very body the wealth of knowledge that destroys worldly existence.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सुमति जो मानव। तो मोह न धरितां सदैव। ह्याच देहें ज्ञानवैभव। मिळवी भवनाशक

statements.statement: When knowledge comes to hand, fulfilment comes to him; yet he does not cast off the body; he keeps it in order to save people.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ज्ञान येतां हातासी। कृतार्थता ये तयासी। तरी न टाकी देहासी। राखी लोकांसी तारावया

statements.statement: Burning the accumulated karma, avoiding the karma now being made, and taking only prārabdha [the destiny already in motion], he lives on to purify people.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: कर्म संचित जाळून। क्रियमाण टाळून। प्रारब्धमात्र घेऊन। राहे पावन कराया लोकां

statements.statement: Moving over the earth at will, giving his darśana and touch, he purifies people, becoming like water.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: स्वेच्छें भूमीवरी फिरून। दर्शन स्पर्शन देऊन। करी लोकांतें पावन। उदकासमान होऊनी

statements.statement: Going its own way, water leaves the high ground; it uproots the lofty tree and saves the humble reed.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: स्वगति करिता जळ। सोडूनी दे उच्चस्थळ। उन्नत वृक्षा पाडी समूळ। तारी नम्र लव्हाळ्या

statements.statement: Know the liberated man to be so: leaving those stiff with pride, he turns to the humble when he sees them, and drives away their sin.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तसा मुक्त नर जाण। गर्वें ताठरती त्यां टाकून। वळती लीना देखून। घालवून त्याचे पाप

statements.statement: Those hypocrites of evil mind he curses, and they are utterly destroyed; and he always saves the humble.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जे कां पाखंड दुर्मती। शापूनी तयांप्रती। समूळनाशा पावविती। तारिती सदा लीनांतें

statements.statement: Making water my guru, I took this instruction. Know this to be the fourth guru; I now tell the quality of the fifth.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जळास गुरू करून। घेतलें म्यां हें शिक्षण। हा चवथा गुरु जाण। पांचव्याचा गुण सांगतों

statements.statement: Saintly persons become powerful by execution of austerities. Their consciousness is unshakable because they do not try to enjoy anything within the material world. Such naturally liberated sages accept foodstuffs that are offered to them by destiny, and if by chance they happen to eat contaminated food, they are not affected, just like fire, which burns up contaminated substances that are offered to it.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
तेजस्वी तपसा दीप्तो दुर्धर्षोदरभाजन: ।
सर्वभक्ष्योऽपि युक्तात्मा नादत्ते मलमग्निवत् ॥ ४५ ॥
original.transliteration:
tejasvī tapasā dīpto
durdharṣodara-bhājanaḥ
sarva-bhakṣyo ’pi yuktātmā
nādatte malam agni-vat
original.word_for_word: tejasvī — brilliantly luminous; tapasā — by his austerity; dīptaḥ — glowing; durdharṣa — unshakable; udara-bhājanaḥ — eating only that needed by his stomach; sarva — everything; bhakṣyaḥ — eating; api — even though; yukta-ātmā — one who is fixed in spiritual life; na ādatte — does not assume; malam — contamination; agni-vat — like the fire.

statements.statement: The word udara-bhājana indicates that a saintly person eats only to keep body and soul together and not for sense gratification. One should eat palatable foodstuffs to maintain one’s mind in a cheerful mood; however, one should not eat luxuriously, because this will cause sex desire and laziness. A saintly person is always a perfect gentleman and is never greedy or lusty. Although māyā tries to defeat him by offering different material allurements, ultimately these attractive material features are themselves defeated by the spiritual power of a saintly person. Thus, one should never disrespect a spiritually advanced personality but should worship him reverentially. To carelessly approach a Kṛṣṇa conscious personality is just like carelessly approaching fire, which immediately burns if not handled properly. The Lord does not excuse mistreatment of a pure devotee.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A saintly person, just like fire, sometimes appears in a concealed form and at other times reveals himself. For the welfare of the conditioned souls who desire real happiness, a saintly person may accept the worshipable position of spiritual master, and thus like fire he burns to ashes all the past and future sinful reactions of his worshipers by mercifully accepting their offerings.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
क्व‍‍चिच्छन्न: क्व‍‍चित् स्पष्ट उपास्य: श्रेय इच्छताम् ।
भुङ्क्ते सर्वत्र दातृणां दहन् प्रागुत्तराशुभम् ॥ ४६ ॥
original.transliteration:
kvacic channaḥ kvacit spaṣṭa
upāsyaḥ śreya icchatām
bhuṅkte sarvatra dātṝṇāṁ
dahan prāg-uttarāśubham
original.word_for_word: kvacit — sometimes; channaḥ — concealed; kvacit — sometimes; spaṣṭaḥ — manifest; upāsyaḥ — worshipable; śreyaḥ — the highest good; icchatām — by those desiring; bhuṅkte — he devours; sarvatra — on all sides; dātṝṇām — of those making offerings to him; dahan — burning; prāk — previous; uttara — and future; aśubham — sinful reactions.

statements.statement: A saintly person prefers to conceal his exalted spiritual position, but to instruct the suffering people of the world he sometimes reveals his own greatness. This is compared to a fire that sometimes burns unnoticed beneath ashes and sometimes blazes openly. Just as fire devours the ghee and other offerings given by the performers of sacrifice, similarly a saintly person accepts the praise offered by his conditioned followers, knowing that in fact all praise is meant for the Supreme Lord, Kṛṣṇa. Although an ordinary person immediately becomes puffed up and foolish when he is praised, such inauspicious tendencies within a saintly person are burned to ashes by his attachment to the Absolute Truth. In this way, he is just like fire.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Just as fire manifests differently in pieces of wood of different sizes and qualities, the omnipotent Supreme Soul, having entered the bodies of higher and lower life forms created by His own potency, appears to assume the identity of each.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
स्वमायया सृष्टमिदं सदसल्ल‍क्षणं विभु: ।
प्रविष्ट ईयते तत्तत्स्वरूपोऽग्निरिवैधसि ॥ ४७ ॥
original.transliteration:
sva-māyayā sṛṣṭam idaṁ
sad-asal-lakṣaṇaṁ vibhuḥ
praviṣṭa īyate tat-tat-
svarūpo ’gnir ivaidhasi
original.word_for_word: sva-māyayā — by His own material energy; sṛṣṭam — created; idam — this (body of the individual jīva); sat-asat — as demigod, animal, and so on; lakṣaṇam — characterized; vibhuḥ — the Almighty; praviṣṭaḥ — having entered; īyate — appears; tat-tat — of each different form; svarūpaḥ — assuming the identity; agniḥ — fire; iva — as; edhasi — in firewood.

statements.statement: Although the Supreme Lord is within everything, everything is not the Lord. By the mode of goodness the Lord creates the exalted material bodies of demigods and brāhmaṇas, and by expanding the mode of ignorance He similarly creates the bodies of animals, śūdras and other lower forms of life. The Lord enters all of these superior and inferior creations, but He remains vibhu, the all-powerful Personality of Godhead. Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura explains that although fire is present within smoldering wood, it blazes forth when we stir the wood around. Similarly, although the Personality of Godhead is indirectly present everywhere, when we chant and hear His glories with love and devotion the Lord is stirred into manifestation and directly appears before His devotees.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The foolish conditioned souls ignore the spectacular presence of the Lord within everything and instead absorb their mediocre consciousness in their own temporary material coverings, thinking, “I am a strong man,” “I am a beautiful woman,” “I am the richest man in this city,” “I am a Ph.D.,” and so on. One should cut off such useless entanglement and accept the fact that one is pure spirit soul, the eternal, blissful servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Fire shines by its own brilliance; know that it cannot be held in the hand directly; it stores everything only in its belly; it devours everything by its own brilliance.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अग्नि निजतेजें देदीप्यमान । साक्षात हातीं न धरवे जाण । उदरमात्रीं सांठवण । सर्व भक्षण निजतेजें

statements.statement: So too the yogī: he shines with the feeling of God; the strength to seize him is not in gods or men.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसाचि योगियाही जाण । भगवद्‌भावें देदीप्यमान । त्यासी धरावया आंगवण । नव्हे जाण सुरनरां

statements.statement: As a burning khadira ember cannot be held in the hand, so the yogī is very hard to hold; the dealings of Māyā with her qualities cannot overpower him.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: हातीं न धरवे खदिरांगारु । तैसा योगिया अतिदुर्धरु । तयासी न शके आवरूं । मायाव्यवहारु गुणेंसीं

statements.statement: Whatever fire takes in, it burns and makes like itself; thus it eats everything, yet does not touch impurity.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अग्नीनें जें जें सेवणें । तें जाळूनि आपुल्या‌ऐसें करणें । यापरी सर्व भक्षणें । नाहीं स्पर्शणें मळासी

statements.statement: So the yogī: whatever he accepts, he decides by the vision of the Self; driving the faults far away, he then accepts it with his own knowledge.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसा योगी जें अंगीकारी । तें आत्मदृष्टीं निर्धारी । दोष दवडूनियां दूरी । मग स्वीकारी निजबोधें

statements.statement: Whatever impure thing falls into fire becomes pure through the fire's mouth; whatever little the yogī takes becomes supremely auspicious.
