source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अग्नींत पडिलें जें समळ । तें अग्निमुखें होय निर्मळ । योगिया जें सेवी अळुमाळ । परम मंगळ तें होय

statements.statement: Sacrifice is performed in the mouth of the fire; by its unseen result one obtains heaven; whatever falls into the mouth of the yogī, by that one obtains one's own state.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अग्निमुखीं यागु घडे । तेणें अदृष्टें स्वर्ग जोडे । योगियाचे मुखीं जें पडे । तेणें जोडे निजपद

statements.statement: Fire is by nature formless; to it, according to the wood, forms come - long, circular, large; it appears in many shapes.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अग्नि सहजें निराकार । त्यासी काष्ठानुरूपें आकार । दीर्घ चक्र वर्तुल थोर । नानाकार भासतु

statements.statement: As the one water of the Gaṅgā appears as whirlpools, ripples and waves, so the Soul of the world appears as the whole world, in the form of the universe.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जैसें गंगेचें एक जळ । भासे भंवरे लहरी कल्लोळ । तैसा जगदाकारें अखिल । भासे सकळ जगदात्मा

statements.statement: Such is the state of the yogī: though he sees beings of many shapes, he sees himself with an equal mind; for him there is no delusion of difference.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैशी योगियाची स्थिती । पाहता नानाकार व्यक्ती । आपणियातें देखे समवृत्ती । भेदभ्रांति त्या नाहीं

statements.statement: One should be radiant through austerity and should appear blazing to people; one may eat what is needed anywhere, but should not touch fault.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तपें तेजस्वी असावें। लोकां प्रदीप्त दिसावें। पाहिजे तिकडे खावें। परी न शिवावें दोषासी

statements.statement: While living among people one should remain hidden; at times, taking on visibility, one should behave openly.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जनांत वागतां आपण। राहावें गुप्तपणा धरून। केव्हां केव्हां प्रगटपण। धरून राहटी करावी

statements.statement: Whoever worships him, one should fulfil that person's wishes; and one should utterly destroy the sins of those who worship.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: भजतो जो आपणासी। पुरवावें त्याच्या कामासी। भजकांच्या पापासी। नाश करावें समूळ

statements.statement: Though moving about on the earth, if one gets something to eat one should not store it. This is understood by making fire one's guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जरी भूमीवरी फिरतां। कांहीं मिळे खाण्याकरितां। त्याचा न करावा सांठा। अग्नि गुरु करितां कळें हें

statements.statement: He who is radiant by himself shows his brightness to people; with heat he drives off cold, and with light he drives away darkness.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो स्वयमेव तेजस्वी। लोकां आपुली दीप्ती दावी। तापें शीत पळवी। प्रकाशें घालवी अंधकारा

statements.statement: Fire moves here and there, eats what it wants, yet remains pure again, and behaves alike toward all.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: अग्नि इकडे तिकडे फिरून। पाहिजे तें खाऊन। पुनः सोंवळा राहून। सर्वासमान वागतसे

statements.statement: Fire, becoming the foremost, eats what it wants, takes not even a trace of fault, and does not spoil its purity.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: अग्नि वरिष्ठ होऊन। पाहिजे तें खाऊन। दोषाचा लेषही न घेऊन। शुद्धपणा न विटवी

statements.statement: He whose radiance is astonishing, who feels disgust nowhere: this instruction the seeker should take firmly.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ज्याचा तेजस्वीपणा अचाट। कोठेंही जया नये वीट। हें शिक्षण नीट। साधकें धीटपणें घ्यावें

statements.statement: Keeping fire in the hearth-pit and kindling it with wood, the agnihotrīs perform the oblation; that fire purifies them.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: कुंडांत अग्नीस ठेवून। काष्ठानें प्रदीप्त करून। अग्निहोत्री करिती हवन। तया पावन करी तो

statements.statement: Fire stays always at the disposal of the sacrificer, accepts his daily service, and always purifies him.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तया यजमानाचे स्वाधीन। अग्नी सदा राहून। नित्य सेवा घेऊन। करी पावन तयासी सदा

statements.statement: As is a person's worship, so does fire fulfil his wish; the oblations offered to the gods, it delivers to them.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जशी उपासना जयाची। तशी इच्छा पुरवी तयाची। आहुती ज्या देवांची। देती तयां ती पोंचवी

statements.statement: Fire does not hoard either; if it gets wood and the like, it burns it and makes it ash. In this way a man should behave.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: अग्नी संग्रहही न करी। त्याला काष्ठादि मिळे तरी। जाळूनी त्याची राख करी। यापरी नरें वागावें

statements.statement: Know the all-pervading Supreme Self to have no form; the form that is seen, know it to be false, as with fire.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो विभू परमात्मा जाण। तया आकार नसून। आकार ये दिसून। तो मिथ्या जाण अग्नीपरी

statements.statement: Entering whatever it meets, burning each piece of wood, though itself formless, fire appears in that shape.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मिळे त्यांत प्रवेशून। त्या त्या काष्ठा जाळून। स्वयें निराकार असून। तसा दिसून ये अग्नी

statements.statement: In a big piece of wood it blazes and appears big; through a small one it appears small; it appears long, broad, round.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जें थोर काष्ठ असे। तया झळकूनी थोर दिसे। लहानाच्या योगें लहान दिसे। लांब चवडा वाटोळा

statements.statement: All living beings are 'vimatāḥ' [disputed, of differing views]; devoid of any fixed form, whatever gradation there is among them is like that of fire resting in wood. [Sanskrit verse; the first half is hard to construe, so this is a literal rendering.]

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: विमताः सकला जीवाः । ध्रौव्यादाकारवर्जिताः यत्तारतम्यं तेषां तु तत्काष्ठाश्रितवह्निवत्

statements.statement: Fire is formless; when it gets wood it takes that form; as it appears, so the ātman appears with form through connection with various bodies.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: अग्नी असे निराकार। काष्ठ मिळतां तदाकार। दिसे तसा हा साकार। नानाशरीरयोगें आत्मा

statements.statement: The man who is exclusively devoted, by the strength of knowledge quickly casts off the perishable adjuncts and becomes the formless Parabrahman.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: अनन्य शरण जो नर। तो ज्ञानबळें सत्वर। टाकी उपाधी नश्वर। होई निराकार परब्रह्म

statements.statement: Karma is the root of the body; he burns it, root and all, with knowledge; then, free of adjuncts, he becomes the pure, spotless Parabrahman.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: कर्म देहाचे मूळ। ते ज्ञानें जाळी समूळ। मग निरुपाधिक केवळ। होयी विमळ परब्रह्म

statements.statement: Fire grows along with the wood and shows a form like the wood's; having quickly made it ash, it drops the form; so too the ātman.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: अग्नी वाढूनी काष्ठाबरोबर। दावी काष्ठासारिखा आकार। राख करूनी सत्वर। आकार टाकी तसा आत्मा

statements.statement: 'He who is manifold, of many forms, a counter-form in every form': this is the Veda's utterance. Then [in truth] the ātman is without form.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो बहुधा बहुरुप। रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूप। हा वेदाचा आलाप। तेव्हां रूपरहित आत्मा

statements.statement: So that this may be understood without doubt, I made fire my guru, gave up identification with the body, and stay put here.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हें निःसंदेह कळावें म्हणून। अग्नीस गुरू करून। देहाभिमान सोडून। राहे पडून ये स्थळीं

statements.statement: The body's momentary perishability, when known, brings true dispassion; to learn this too, one should become the disciple of the fire's flame.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: क्षणभग्नत्व देहाचें। जाणतां वैराग्य बाणे साचें। हेंही जाणाया अग्नीचें। ज्वाळेचें शिष्यत्व कीजे

statements.statement: If one reflects well, moment after moment the elements connected with the body arise and die, every day.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: बरवा विचार करून पाहतां क्षणोक्षण। देहसंबंधीं भुतें उपजोन। जाती मरोन प्रत्यहीं

statements.statement: As flames, every time, arise and come to destruction, such is the state of the elements connected with the body; this subtle state is to be understood.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ज्वाळा दरवेळीं जशा। उपजूनी पावती नाशा। देहासंबंधी भुतांची ती दशा। सूक्ष्मदशा कळे ही

statements.statement: The man who accepts this, regarding the body as perishable, with dispassion and respect crosses the ocean of worldly existence.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हें मान्य करी जो नर। तो देहा क्षमभंगुर। मानुनी वैराग्ये सादर। भवसागर उलंडी

statements.statement: This is a great generosity: to give up quickly one's attachment to the body. This lesson I took from the fifth guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हे उदारत्व थोर। सोडावें देहाचें ममत्व सत्वर। हा बोध घेतला सादर। पांचव्या गुरुपासून

statements.statement: The various phases of one’s material life, beginning with birth and culminating in death, are all properties of the body and do not affect the soul, just as the apparent waxing and waning of the moon does not affect the moon itself. Such changes are enforced by the imperceptible movements of time.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
विसर्गाद्या: श्मशानान्ता भावा देहस्य नात्मन: ।
कलानामिव चन्द्रस्य कालेनाव्यक्तवर्त्मना ॥ ४८ ॥
original.transliteration:
visargādyāḥ śmaśānāntā
bhāvā dehasya nātmanaḥ
kalānām iva candrasya
kālenāvyakta-vartmanā
original.word_for_word: visarga — birth; ādyāḥ — beginning with; śmaśāna — the time of death, when the body is burned to ashes; antāḥ — ending with; bhāvāḥ — the states; dehasya — of the body; na — not; ātmanaḥ — of the soul; kalānām — of the different phases; iva — as; candrasya — of the moon; kālena — by time; avyakta — imperceptible; vartmanā — whose movement.

statements.statement: The body undergoes six changes: birth, growth, maintenance, production of by-products, dwindling and death. Similarly, the moon appears to grow, diminish and finally disappear. Since moonlight is a lunar reflection of sunlight, it is understood that the moon itself does not grow or diminish; rather, we perceive the reflection of the moon in various phases. Similarly, the eternal soul is not born, nor does it die, as confirmed in Bhagavad-gītā (2.20): na jāyate mriyate vā kadācit. We perceive the reflection of the soul in the form of the gross material body and the subtle mind, which undergo various material changes.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: According to Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī, the sun is a fiery planet and the moon is a watery planet. This is also confirmed by Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī and further illustrates the ignorance of modern science about the actual nature of the moon planet.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The flames of a fire appear and disappear at every moment, and yet this creation and destruction is not noticed by the ordinary observer. Similarly, the mighty waves of time flow constantly, like the powerful currents of a river, and imperceptibly cause the birth, growth and death of innumerable material bodies. And yet the soul, who is thus constantly forced to change his position, cannot perceive the actions of time.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
कालेन ह्योघवेगेन भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययौ ।
नित्यावपि न द‍ृश्येते आत्मनोऽग्नेर्यथार्चिषाम् ॥ ४९ ॥
original.transliteration:
kālena hy ogha-vegena
bhūtānāṁ prabhavāpyayau
nityāv api na dṛśyete
ātmano ’gner yathārciṣām
original.word_for_word: kālena — by time; hi — indeed; ogha — like a flood; vegena — whose speed; bhūtānām — of created bodies; prabhava — the birth; apyayau — and demise; nityau — constant; api — although; na dṛśyete — are not seen; ātmanaḥ — related to the spirit soul; agneḥ — of fire; yathā — just as; arciṣām — of the flames.

statements.statement: The brāhmaṇa avadhūta instructing King Yadu again gives the example of fire after having already proceeded to the example of the moon. This analytic method is called siṁhāvalokana, or “the lion’s glance,” by which one simultaneously proceeds forward and casts backward glances to see if anything has been overlooked. Thus the sage proceeds with his analysis but returns to the example of fire to illustrate the need for renunciation. The material body is certainly an ephemeral and phantasmagorical manifestation of the Lord’s external potency. The flames of a fire constantly take birth and disappear, yet we perceive the fire as a continuous reality. Similarly, the soul is a continuous reality, although his material bodies appear and disappear constantly, by the influence of time. It is said that the most astonishing thing is that no one thinks that they will die. Because the soul is eternal, the living entity is prone to accept any fleeting situation as permanent, forgetting that his eternal nature can be truly experienced only in the eternal atmosphere of the spiritual sky. If one is convinced of this fact, he develops the quality of vairāgya, or detachment from material illusion.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The waxing and waning of the moon's phases in the bright and dark fortnights - that pull is not in the moon itself; so it is, directly, with yogīs.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: शुक्लकृष्णपक्षपाडी । चंद्रकळांची वाढीमोडी । ते निजचंद्रीं नाहीं वोढी । तैशी रोकडी योगियां

statements.statement: The six modifications beginning with birth and destruction belong truly to the body alone; the Self is imperishable and unmodified, infinite and boundless in its nature.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जन्मनाशादि षड्‌विकार । हे देहासीच साचार । आत्मा अविनाशी निर्विकार । अनंत अपार स्वरूपत्वें

statements.statement: The pot is by nature perishable; in it the moon is reflected; the imperishable appears in the perishable; it is not tainted by modification or fault.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: घटु स्वभावें नाशवंतु असे । त्यामाजीं चंद्रमा बिंबलासे । नश्वरीं अनश्वर दिसे । विकारदोषें लिंपेना

statements.statement: With the pot there is no origin for the moon, and with its destruction no destruction; the moon, in its own natural state, is without destruction and origin.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: घटासवें चंद्रासी उत्पत्ती । नाहीं नाशासवें नाशप्राप्ती । चंद्रमा आपुले सहजस्थितीं । नाश‌उ त्पत्तिरहितु

statements.statement: So the yogī, in his own true nature, does not come into being with the body; when the body perishes he does not perish; he is full, without a break.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसा योगिया निजरूपपणें । देहासवें नाहीं होणें । देह निमाल्या नाहीं निमणें । अखंडपणें परिपूर्ण

statements.statement: The unseen course of Time shows destruction and origin; that authority of Time is over the body; it does not touch the state of the Self.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: काळाची अलक्ष्य गती । दाखवी नाश आणि उत्पत्ति । ते काळसत्ता देहाप्रती । आत्मस्थिती नातळे

statements.statement: People say 'this is the same lamp', but the flame passes away moment by moment; that subtle movement is not noticed; at the end they say 'it has gone out'.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: दीपू तोचि तो हा म्हणती । परी शिखा क्षणक्षणा जाती । ते लक्षेना सूक्ष्मगती । अंतीं म्हणती विझाला

statements.statement: People see the water of the Gaṅgā flowing before their eyes, yet they say 'that is the water of that time' - they babble; so the course of Time is unfathomable; no one knows it.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: प्रत्यक्ष प्रवाहे गंगाजळ । ते काळींचे म्हणती बरळ । तैशी काळगती अकळ । लोक सकळ नेणती

statements.statement: Looking directly at the body, Time swallows its ages; childhood, boyhood and youth - they do not see Time near.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: प्रत्यक्ष पाहतां देहासी । काळ वयसेतें ग्रासी । बाल्य-कौमार-तारुण्यांसी । निकट काळासी न देखती

statements.statement: The many changes that appear are on the body only. The ātman, who is beyond, neither undergoes them nor grows. This the moon-guru tells.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जे बहु विकार। भासती ते शरीरावर। न घडे न वाढे आत्मा पर। हे निशाकर गुरु सांगे

statements.statement: Not knowing the cause and looking only at the effect, those people who are deluded are cheated by fallacious arguments.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: कारणांतें न जाणून। केवळ कार्या पाहून। जे जन जाती भुलून। ते कुतर्क करून फसती

statements.statement: As, though the moon's phases come and go, there is no change in the moon-disc, and what the eye sees is a vain appearance.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जेवीं येतां जातां कळा। विकार नसे चंद्रमंडळा। जरी दिसला डोळा। तरी तो व्यर्थ भास होय

statements.statement: The ātman is not born, does not grow, does not die; all these changes, O king, know to be on the body, like the phases on the moon-disc.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: आत्मा न होयी न वाढे न मरे। हे विकार सारे। भूपा जाण देहावर रे। चंद्रमंडळीं कळा जशा

statements.statement: As the moon appears in the sky like a second luminous disc, by the sun's power it likewise drives away darkness.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: चंद्र द्वितीय मंडळापरीं। भासतां आकाशांतरी। सूर्यसत्तेंनें त्याचे परी। निवारी अंधकारातें

statements.statement: The moon-disc is itself water, and therefore it appears cool; in the same way, by the power of the ātman alone, the whole body is animated.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: स्वयें चन्द्रमंडळ जळ। म्हणोनीं भासे शीतळ। यापरी आत्मसत्तेनें केवळ। देह सकळ चेतनसे

statements.statement: As water is in the moon-disc, so the inner organ is in the body; in it the ātman is reflected, and thereby it seems that sense-objects pass.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जळ चन्द्रमंडळीं जसें। देहीं अंतःकरण तसें। त्यांत आत्मा बिंबितसे। तेणें भासे विषय जात

statements.statement: This witness-ātman does not perish. I took this knowledge from the moon. Now listen to the seventh guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हा साक्षिभूत आत्मा न नासे। हें चंद्रापासून असें। ज्ञान घेतलें असें। सातवा परिसे गुरु आता

statements.statement: That the ātman is wholly within the body, though this has become the experience, yet he himself is free of difference, as was said in the case of the sky.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: आत्मा संपूर्ण देहगत। असा झाला प्रतीत। तरी तो भेदशून्य स्वतः। आकाशापरी कथिला

statements.statement: As to the individual, the elements, the body and the other adjuncts, this notion of ours that the Self resides in them is to be known as a wrong notion, by the logic of the sun's reflection.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: व्यक्ती भूत देहाद्युपाधी। तद्गत आम्हां ही बुद्धी। जाणावी कुबुद्धी। सूर्यप्रतिबिंबन्यायानें

statements.statement: To fix this in the mind, I give an example: fill a pot with water and move it beneath the disc of the sun.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हे मतिंत भरावें म्हणून। सांगतों उदाहरण। घटीं जळ भरून। सूर्यमंडळाखालून फिरवावें

statements.statement: When the vessel moves, the reflection moves; when the vessel shakes, it shakes well; all see it so; but is that true?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: पात्रच फिरतां प्रतिबिंब फिरे। पात्र हालतां हाले बरें। असें पाहती सारे । परी तें खरे काय असे

statements.statement: Whatever changes there are on the water, those appear on the reflection; they seem to be on the sun too, but they are not; keep this reverently in mind.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जे जे विकार जळावर। ते ते प्रतिबिंबावर। भासती ते सूर्यावर। नसती हें सादर आण मनीं

statements.statement: Whatever various changes there are, they are on the adjunct; they are not on the ātman; he is the witness, beyond the adjunct.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जे जे नाना विकार। ते ते उपाधीवर। ते नसती आत्म्यावर। तो साक्षी पर उपाधीहूनी

statements.statement: Just as the sun evaporates large quantities of water by its potent rays and later returns the water to the earth in the form of rain, similarly, a saintly person accepts all types of material objects with his material senses, and at the appropriate time, when the proper person has approached him to request them, he returns such material objects. Thus, both in accepting and giving up the objects of the senses, he is not entangled.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
गुणैर्गुणानुपादत्ते यथाकालं विमुञ्चति ।
न तेषु युज्यते योगी गोभिर्गा इव गोपति: ॥ ५० ॥
original.transliteration:
guṇair guṇān upādatte
yathā-kālaṁ vimuñcati
na teṣu yujyate yogī
gobhir gā iva go-patiḥ
original.word_for_word: guṇaiḥ — by his senses; guṇān — material sense objects; upādatte — accepts; yathā-kālam — at the proper time; vimuñcati — gives them up; na — he does not; teṣu — in them; yujyate — become entangled; yogī — a self-realized sage; gobhiḥ — by his rays; gāḥ — bodies of water; iva — as; go-patiḥ — the sun.

statements.statement: A Kṛṣṇa conscious person never feels proprietorship over the opulences entrusted to him by Lord Kṛṣṇa for spreading the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. The devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa should not merely accumulate material wealth, but should distribute the opulences of Lord Kṛṣṇa in such a way that the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement spreads unlimitedly. This is a lesson to be learned from the sun.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Even when reflected in various objects, the sun is never divided, nor does it merge into its reflection. Only those with dull brains would consider the sun in this way. Similarly, although the soul is reflected through different material bodies, the soul remains undivided and nonmaterial.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
बुध्यते स्वे न भेदेन व्यक्तिस्थ इव तद्गत: ।
लक्ष्यते स्थूलमतिभिरात्मा चावस्थितोऽर्कवत् ॥ ५१ ॥
original.transliteration:
budhyate sve na bhedena
vyakti-stha iva tad-gataḥ
lakṣyate sthūla-matibhir
ātmā cāvasthito ’rka-vat
original.word_for_word: budhyate — is thought of; sve — in his original form; na — not; bhedena — in terms of diversity; vyakti — on separate reflecting objects; sthaḥ — situated; iva — apparently; tat-gataḥ — actually having entered within them; lakṣyate — seems; sthūla-matibhiḥ — to those whose intelligence is dull; ātmā — the self; ca — also; avasthitaḥ — situated; arkavat — like the sun.

statements.statement: The sun is reflected in many objects, such as windows, mirrors, shiny metal, oil, water, and so on, yet the sun remains one and indivisible. Similarly, the eternal spirit soul within the body is reflected through the screen of the material body. Thus the soul appears to be old or young, fat or skinny, happy or sad. The soul may appear to be American, Russian, African, Hindu or Christian; however, the eternal soul in its natural position is free of any material designation.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The word sthūla-matibhiḥ in this verse indicates those whose intelligence is gross and dull. We have practical experience of a dog urinating on a valuable painting at an outdoor art show. Due to its dull intelligence, the dog could not appreciate the actual value of the painting. Similarly, unless one takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, one is grossly misusing the invaluable opportunity of human life. Human life is meant for self-realization, and we should not waste time bickering over material designations such as capitalist, communist, American, Russian, and so on. Instead, all people should take to the loving devotional service of God and realize their eternal, pure identity. One should understand the sun by observing its direct manifestation and not its distorted reflection on material objects. Similarly, one should consider every living being in terms of his pure spiritual identity beyond the distorted manifestation of material designations.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The word ātmā in this verse also refers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Just as we tend to observe ordinary jīva souls through the reflection of the material body, we tend to observe the Personality of Godhead through the distorting screen of our material mind. Thus, we imagine God to be impersonal or material or unknowable. When the sky is overcast, sunlight is the highest possible perception of the sun, which is covered by clouds. Similarly, when one’s mind is fogged over with mental speculation one may take the light emanating from the transcendental body of God to be the highest spiritual truth. However, when the mind is spotlessly clear like a cloudless blue sky, one can see the actual form of the Personality of Godhead, Lord Kṛṣṇa. The Absolute Truth cannot be perfectly understood by the covered mind of the conditioned soul; rather, one must see the Lord through the clear blue sky of pure Kṛṣṇa consciousness, which is free from fruitive desires and mental speculation. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura sings:

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement:
jīvera kalyāṇa-sādhana-kāma
jagate āsi’ e madhura nāma
avidyā-timira-tāpana-rūpe
hṛd-gagane virāje

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: “The holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa descends into the darkness of the material world just to benedict the conditioned souls. The holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa is just like the sun that rises in the clear sky of the heart of the devotees.” Such brilliant knowledge cannot be understood by those who are trying, in the name of either piety or atheism, to exploit the material creation of the Lord. One must become a pure devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa, and then his knowledge will illuminate everything in all directions: kasmin nu bhagavo vijñāte sarvam idaṁ vijñātaṁ bhavatīti (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 1.3).

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The sun, in its season, draws up water with its essence by its own rays; the same, in the rainy season, raining, cools the people a thousandfold.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सूर्य काळें निजकिरणीं । रसेंसहित शोषी पाणी । तोचि वर्षाकाळीं वर्षोनी । निववी जनीं सहस्त्रधा

statements.statement: He draws in everything by his rays, and nobody knows the mark of that drawing; when he gives back through the cloud's mouth by raining, he cools the earth with its people.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सर्व शोषूनि घे किरणीं । तें शोषितें लक्षण नेणे कोणी । देतां मेघमुखें वरुषोनी । निववी अवनी जनेंसीं

statements.statement: Such is the yogī's way: of him whose little he accepts, he fulfils the wishes in a thousand ways, for his good.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसीचि योगियाची परीं । अल्प ज्याचें अंगीकारी । त्याचे मनोरथ पूर्ण करी । सहस्र प्रकारी हितत्वें

statements.statement: Whether giving or taking objects, they have no attachment at all; drawing the essence and giving it, they are unattached like the sun.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: त्यांसी विषयो देतां कां घेतां । आसक्ति नाहीं सर्वथा । रसु चोखूनि घेतां देतां । अलिप्त सविता तैसे ते

statements.statement: The sun is reflected in a puddle; fools say 'he is drowned in the puddle'; by its trembling they think he trembled; by its muddiness they say he was muddied.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सूर्यो थिल्लरामाजीं बिंबला । मूढ म्हणती थिल्लरीं बुडाला । त्याचेनि कंपें कंपु मानिला । डहुळें डहुळला म्हणती तो

statements.statement: Not touching that puddle, the sun stays unattached in the sky; such is the yogī's fitness: beyond the body, even in the body's actions.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: त्या थिल्लरातें नातळतां । गगनीं अलिप्त जेवीं सविता । तैसीच योगियांची योग्यता । देहातीतता देहकर्मीं

statements.statement: They do not understand that the sense of the body is sublated - that secret knowledge of his; who was ever bitten and killed by a rope that is taken for a snake?

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: त्यासी देहाचें बाधितभान । हें न कळें त्याचें गुह्यज्ञान । दोराचेनि सापें जाण । डसोनि कोण मारिला

statements.statement: He sees himself reflected in the water, but does not say 'I am drowned in the water'; so the one who has become beyond the body, having gained knowledge, is not afraid of the body's actions.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देखे आपणातें जळीं बिंबला । परी न म्हणे मी जळीं बुडाला । तैसा देहातीतु बोधु झाला । नाहीं भ्याला देहकर्मा

statements.statement: In the moving and unmoving world, whatever is seen to be useful, one should keep safe, without becoming attached oneself.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: चराचर जगांत। जें दिसेल उपयुक्त। तें ठेवावें सुरक्षित। आपण आसक्त न होतां

statements.statement: Later, seeing the proper time, one should release all of it into suitable recipients, with a mind to help others.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: पुढें यथायोग्य काळ। पाहूनी मग तें सकळ। पात्रीं सोडावें केवळ। परोपकारमतीनें

statements.statement: Even if everything is exhausted, one should not feel grief within; and when it is got again in due course, one should not rejoice within.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: समस्त संपले तरी। खेद न धरावा अंतरीं। पुढें तसें काळांतरीं। मिळतां अंतरीं न हर्षावें

statements.statement: Leaving attachment and aversion, gathering wealth without strain, and giving it up to the proper recipient at the proper time, one should remain unattached.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: राग द्वेष सोडून। अनायासें अर्थ जोडून। यथाकाळीं पात्रीं सोडून। अलिप्त होऊन रहावें

statements.statement: With no sense of merit and fault in it, one should carry on this dealing; then bondage should not arise. This I learned from the sun.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: गुण दोषबुद्धी नसून। हा व्यवहार करून। असतां नये बंधन। हें सूर्यापासून शिकलों

statements.statement: The sun, knowing the future, stores up water with its rays [lit. 'hands']; it lets it go at the proper time, but does not take pride in it.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सूर्य भविष्य जाणून। जळ ठेवी करीं सांठवून। तें यथाकाळीं दे सोडून। परी अभिमान न करी

statements.statement: One should never indulge in excessive affection or concern for anyone or anything; otherwise one will have to experience great suffering, just like the foolish pigeon.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
नातिस्‍नेह: प्रसङ्गो वा कर्तव्य: क्व‍ापि केनचित् ।
कुर्वन् विन्देत सन्तापं कपोत इव दीनधी: ॥ ५२ ॥
original.transliteration:
nāti-snehaḥ prasaṅgo vā
kartavyaḥ kvāpi kenacit
kurvan vindeta santāpaṁ
kapota iva dīna-dhīḥ
original.word_for_word: na — not; ati-snehaḥ — excess affection; prasaṅgaḥ — close association; vā — or; kartavyaḥ — one should manifest; kva api — ever; kenacit — with anyone or anything; kurvan — so doing; vindeta — one will experience; santāpam — great distress; kapotaḥ — the pigeon; iva — just as; dīna-dhīḥ — cripple-minded.

statements.statement: The Sanskrit prefix ati, or “excessive,” indicates affection or attachment in which there is no Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Lord Kṛṣṇa says in Bhagavad-gītā (5.29), suhṛdaṁ sarva-bhūtānām: the Lord is the eternal well-wisher of every living being. The Lord is so affectionate that He sits in the heart of every conditioned soul and accompanies him throughout his endless wandering in the kingdom of māyā, patiently waiting for the conditioned soul to come back home, back to Godhead. Thus the Lord makes all arrangements for the eternal happiness of every living entity. The best way for anyone to show compassion and affection for all living beings is to become a preacher on behalf of Lord Kṛṣṇa and assist the Lord in reclaiming the fallen souls. If our affection or attachment for others is based on bodily sense gratification, in the name of society, friendship and love, that excessive, unwanted affection (ati-sneha) will cause burning pain at the time of the breaking or destruction of the relationship. Now the story of the foolish pigeon will be narrated. A similar story is described in the Seventh Canto, Second Chapter of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, told by Yamarāja to the mourning widows of King Suyajña.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: There once was a pigeon who lived in the forest along with his wife. He had built a nest within a tree and lived there for several years in her company.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The two pigeons were very much devoted to their household duties. Their hearts being tied together by sentimental affection, they were each attracted by the other’s glances, bodily features and states of mind. Thus, they completely bound each other in affection.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

hṛdayau gṛha-dharmiṇau

original.word_for_word: kapotau — the two pigeons; sneha — by affection; guṇita — tied together as if by ropes; hṛdayau — their hearts; gṛha-dharmiṇau — attached householders; dṛṣṭim — glance; dṛṣṭyā — by glance; aṅgam — physical body; aṅgena — by the other’s body; buddhim — mind; buddhyā — by the other’s mind; babandhatuḥ — they bound each other.

statements.statement: The male and female pigeon were so attracted to each other that they could not tolerate even a moment’s separation from one another. This is called bhagavad-vismṛti, or forgetfulness of the Supreme Lord and attachment to dead matter. The living entity has an eternal love for the Lord, but when perverted, that love is manifested as false material affection. A pale reflection of actual pleasure thus becomes the foundation of a false life based on forgetfulness of the Absolute Truth.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Naively trusting in the future, they carried out their acts of resting, sitting, walking, standing, conversing, playing, eating and so forth as a loving couple among the trees of the forest.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Whenever she desired anything, O King, the she-pigeon would flatteringly cajole her husband, and he in turn would gratify her by faithfully doing whatever she wanted, even with great personal difficulty. Thus, he could not control his senses in her association.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The word tarpayantī indicates that the lady pigeon was quite expert in seducing her husband through smiling glances and loving talks. Thus appealing to his noble sentiments, she efficiently engaged him as her faithful servant. The poor pigeon was ajitendriya, or one who cannot control his senses and whose heart is easily melted by the beauty of a woman. The brāhmaṇa avadhūta is giving valuable instructions by narrating this story of the two pigeons and the terrible distress they suffered by inevitable separation. If one’s intelligence is not dedicated to serving Hṛṣīkeśa, the Supreme Lord of sense activity, undoubtedly one will plunge into the nescience of bodily gratification. Then one becomes no better than a foolish pigeon.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Then the female pigeon experienced her first pregnancy. When the time arrived, the chaste lady delivered a number of eggs within the nest in the presence of her husband.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The two pigeons became most affectionate to their children and took great pleasure in listening to their awkward chirping, which sounded very sweet to the parents. Thus with love they began to raise the little birds who were born of them.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Seeing his own children, who were more dear to him than life itself, fatally bound in the hunter’s net along with his dearmost wife, whom he considered equal in every way to himself, the poor male pigeon began to lament wretchedly.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The male pigeon said: Alas, just see how I am now destroyed! I am obviously a great fool, for I did not properly execute pious activities. I could not satisfy myself, nor could I fulfill the purpose of life. My dear family, which was the basis of my religiosity, economic development and sense gratification, is now hopelessly ruined.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī explains that the word atṛptasya indicates that the pigeon was not satisfied with the sense gratification he had achieved. Although he was completely attached to his wife, children and nest, he could not sufficiently enjoy them since there is ultimately no satisfaction in such things. Akṛtārthasya indicates that his hopes and dreams for future expansion of his sense gratification were now also ruined. People commonly refer to their “home, sweet home” as their nest, and money put aside for future sense gratification is called a nest egg. Therefore, all of the love birds of the material world should clearly note how their so-called wife, children and fortune will all be dragged away in the hunter’s net. In other words, death will finish everything.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: My wife and I were an ideal match. She always faithfully obeyed me and in fact accepted me as her worshipable deity. But now, seeing her children lost and her home empty, she has left me behind and gone to heaven with our saintly children.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.word_for_word: anurūpā — suitable; anukūlā — faithful; ca — and; yasya — of whom; me — of me; pati-devatā — she who accepted her husband as a worshipable deity; śūnye — empty; gṛhe — in the home; mām — me; santyajya — leaving behind; putraiḥ — along with her sons; svaḥ — to heaven; yāti — is going; sādhubhiḥ — saintly.

statements.statement: Now I am a wretched person living in an empty home. My wife is dead; my children are dead. Why should I possibly want to live? My heart is so pained by separation from my family that life itself has become simply suffering.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:

जिजीविषे किमर्थं वा विधुरो दु:खजीवित: ॥ ७० ॥
original.transliteration:
so ’haṁ śūnye gṛhe dīno
mṛta-dāro mṛta-prajaḥ

vidhuro duḥkha-jīvitaḥ

statements.statement: As the father pigeon wretchedly stared at his poor children trapped in the net and on the verge of death, pathetically struggling to free themselves, his mind went blank, and thus he himself fell into the hunter’s net.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
तांस्तथैवावृतान् शिग्भिर्मृत्युग्रस्तान् विचेष्टत: ।

tāṁs tathaivāvṛtān śigbhir

statements.statement: The cruel hunter, having fulfilled his desire by capturing the head pigeon, his wife and all of their children, set off for his own home.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
तं लब्ध्वा लुब्धक: क्रूर: कपोतं गृहमेधिनम् ।

original.transliteration:
taṁ labdhvā lubdhakaḥ krūraḥ
kapotaṁ gṛha-medhinam
kapotakān kapotīṁ ca
siddhārthaḥ prayayau gṛham

statements.statement: In this way, one who is too attached to family life becomes disturbed at heart. Like the pigeon, he tries to find pleasure in mundane sex attraction. Busily engaged in maintaining his own family, the miserly person is fated to suffer greatly, along with all his family members.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
एवं कुटुम्ब्यशान्तात्मा द्वन्द्वाराम: पतत्रिवत् ।
पुष्णन् कुटुम्बं कृपण: सानुबन्धोऽवसीदति ॥ ७३ ॥
original.transliteration:
evaṁ kuṭumby aśāntātmā

puṣṇan kuṭumbaṁ kṛpaṇaḥ
sānubandho ’vasīdati

statements.statement: The doors of liberation are opened wide to one who has achieved human life. But if a human being simply devotes himself to family life like the foolish bird in this story, then he is to be considered as one who has climbed to a high place only to trip and fall down.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
य: प्राप्य मानुषं लोकं मुक्तिद्वारमपावृतम् ।

statements.statement: Thus end the purports of the humble servants of His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda to the Eleventh Canto, Seventh Chapter, of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, entitled “Lord Kṛṣṇa Instructs Uddhava.”

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The root of worldly sorrow, know, is solely attachment to woman; where the force of greed for woman is mighty, all sorrow is beside it.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: संसारदुःखाचें मूळ । स्त्री‌आसक्तीच जाण केवळ । स्त्रीलोभाचें जेथ प्रबळ बळ । दुःख सकळ त्यापासीं

statements.statement: From attachment and the thread of affection - from these two comes strange sorrow; at every step men suffer it, having become unfree.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: आसक्ति आणि स्नेहसूत्र । या दोन्हीपासाव दुःख विचित्र । पदोपदीं भोगिती नर । अस्वतंत्र हो‌ऊनि

statements.statement: Therefore, in whatever place, attachment and affection should not be made; those by whom excessive affection is set up suffer sorrow themselves.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: यालागीं भलतेनि भलते ठायीं । आसक्ति स्नेहो न करावा पाहीं । अतिस्नेहो मांडिजे जिंहीं । दुःख तिंही भोगिजे

statements.statement: As a fly sitting on sugar does not fly off even when struck, so, enjoying objects, he does not remember old age and death.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: बैसली साकरेवरी माशी । मारितांही नुडे जैशी । तैसा भोगितां विषयांसी । जरामरणासी नाठवी

statements.statement: The delusion of wife and sons is deep; to nourish them, worried and very wretched, he wanders for food.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: स्त्रीपुत्रांचा मोह गहन । त्यांचें करावया पोषण । चिंतातुर अतिदीन । करी भ्रमण अन्नार्थ

statements.statement: Attachment to the pleasure of woman is itself the source of growing sorrow; how much shall I tell of the sorrow obtained through the company of woman - it is irresistible.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: स्त्रीसुखाची आसक्ती । तेचि वाढत्या दुःखाची सूती । स्त्रीसंगें दुःखप्राप्ती । सांगों किती अनिवार

statements.statement: How she was deluded by the delusion of Māyā: where she sees her son bound, into that very net she throws herself; by delusion she was made mad.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मायामोहें भुलली कैशी । जेथ बांधलें देखे पुत्रासी । ते जाळीं घाली आपणासी । मोहें पिशी ते केली

statements.statement: To die after the one who has died - this is what we see everyone doing; but to put an end to birth and death - this self-interest no one holds.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मेल्या मागें मरणें । देखों हेंचि सर्वांसी करणें । परी जन्ममृत्यु निवारणें । हा स्वार्थु कवणें न धरिजे

statements.statement: See: for the sake of wife and sons even one's own life is given; but to attain the state of Bhagavān - this the mind never agrees to.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पहा पां स्त्रीपुत्राकरणें । आपुलाही जीवु देणें । परी भगवत्पदवी साधणें । हें न मने मनें सर्वथा

statements.statement: Such a householder, attached to maintaining the family, restless with desire for objects, meets destruction together with his family.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: यो नाश्नुते निजानंदं स्वाधीनं सुलभं परं। स्त्रीपुत्रादिभवं सौख्यं। भुक्त्वापि स न तुष्यति

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)
