original.text: त्यावर जाळीं घालून। भोयी घेई धरून। तंव माता येऊन त्यां पाहून। ती मोहे बंधनगत झाली

statements.statement: Seeing his own golden [hiraṇmaya] home empty, who would live on, bereft in separation? Thinking so, the pigeon himself fell into bondage.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हिरण्मय स्वगृह शून्य पाहून। विरहें विधुर होऊन राहे कोण। असें तो कवडा मानून। स्वयें बंधनगत झाला

statements.statement: Those who, with sense-pleasures unquenched, stay at home delighting in the family: like the pigeon, Death suddenly comes and carries them off together with the family.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: विषयें जे शांत न होऊन। घरीं राहती परिवारीं रमून। कवड्यापरी सहसा काळ येऊन। परिवारासह मारून ने तयां

statements.statement: [The opening words 'ase nase' are unclear in the print; the sense is:] this rare human body is the open door of liberation; if it slips away, terrible suffering comes again. This I came to know by making the pigeon my guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: असे नसे मोकळें मुक्तिद्वार। तें हें दुर्लभ नरशरीर। सुटतां ये पुनः दुःख घोर। हें कवडा गुरु करूनी जाणिलें

statements.statement: The saintly brāhmaṇa said: O King, the embodied living entity automatically experiences unhappiness in heaven or hell. Similarly, happiness will also be experienced, even without one’s seeking it. Therefore a person of intelligent discrimination does not make any endeavor to obtain such material happiness.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
श्रीब्राह्मण उवाच
सुखमैन्द्रियकं राजन् स्वर्गे नरक एव च ।
देहिनां यद् यथा दु:खं तस्मान्नेच्छेत तद् बुध: ॥ १ ॥
original.transliteration:
śrī-brāhmaṇa uvāca
sukham aindriyakaṁ rājan
svarge naraka eva ca
dehināṁ yad yathā duḥkhaṁ
tasmān neccheta tad-budhaḥ
original.word_for_word: śrī-brāhmaṇaḥ uvāca — the saintly brāhmaṇa said; sukham — happiness; aindriyakam — generated from the material senses; rājan — O King; svarge — in material heaven; narake — in hell; eva — certainly; ca — also; dehinām — of the embodied living beings; yat — since; yathā — just as; duḥkham — unhappiness; tasmāt — therefore; na — not; iccheta — should desire; tat — that; budhaḥ — one who knows.

statements.statement: One should not uselessly waste his life pursuing material sense gratification, because a specific quantity of material happiness will automatically come to one as a result of one’s past and present fruitive activities. This lesson is learned from the ajagara, or python, who lies down and accepts for his maintenance whatever comes of its own accord. Remarkably, in both material heaven and hell happiness and unhappiness come automatically, due to our previous activities, although the proportions of happiness and unhappiness certainly vary. Either in heaven or in hell one may eat, drink, sleep and have sex life, but these activities, being based on the material body, are temporary and inconsequential. An intelligent person should see that even the best material situation is actually a punishment for previous unlawful activities executed outside the scope of loving devotional service to God. A conditioned soul undergoes great trouble to obtain a little happiness. After struggling in material life, which is full of hardship and hypocrisy, one may receive a little sense gratification, but this illusory pleasure in no way offsets the burden of suffering one must bear to obtain it. After all, a pretty hat is no cure for a homely face. If one really wants to solve life’s problems, one should live simply and reserve the major portion of one’s life for loving service to Kṛṣṇa. Even those who do not serve God receive a certain standard of maintenance from Him; therefore we can just imagine the security the Lord affords to those who dedicate their lives to His devotional service.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Unrefined fruitive workers foolishly worry only about the present life, whereas more pious karmīs imprudently make elaborate arrangements for future material sense gratification, unaware that all such enjoyment is temporary. The real solution, however, is to understand that by pleasing the Personality of Godhead, who is the master of all senses and all desires, one can attain permanent happiness. Such knowledge easily solves the problems of life.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Following the example of the python, one should give up material endeavors and accept for one’s maintenance food that comes of its own accord, whether such food be delicious or tasteless, ample or meager.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
ग्रासं सुमृष्टं विरसं महान्तं स्तोकमेव वा ।
यद‍ृच्छयैवापतितं ग्रसेदाजगरोऽक्रिय: ॥ २ ॥
original.transliteration:
grāsaṁ su-mṛṣṭaṁ virasaṁ
mahāntaṁ stokam eva vā
yadṛcchayaivāpatitaṁ
grased ājagaro ’kriyaḥ
original.word_for_word: grāsam — food; su-mṛṣṭam — clean and delicious; virasam — tasteless; mahāntam — a large quantity; stokam — a small quantity; eva — certainly; vā — either; yadṛcchayā — without personal endeavor; eva — indeed; āpatitam — obtained; graset — one should eat; ājagaraḥ — like the python; akriyaḥ — remaining neutral without endeavor.

statements.statement: If at any time food does not come, then a saintly person should fast for many days without making endeavor. He should understand that by God’s arrangement he must fast. Thus, following the example of the python, he should remain peaceful and patient.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
शयीताहानि भूरीणि निराहारोऽनुपक्रम: ।
यदि नोपनयेद् ग्रासो महाहिरिव दिष्टभुक् ॥ ३ ॥
original.transliteration:
śayītāhāni bhūrīṇi
nirāhāro ’nupakramaḥ
yadi nopanayed grāso
mahāhir iva diṣṭa-bhuk
original.word_for_word: śayīta — he should remain peacefully; ahāni — days; bhūrīṇi — for many; nirāhāraḥ — fasting; anupakramaḥ — without endeavor; yadi — if; na upanayet — does not come; grāsaḥ — food; mahā-ahiḥ — the great python; iva — like; diṣṭa — whatever is provided by providence; bhuk — eating.

statements.statement: If by God’s arrangement one is forced to suffer material hardship, then one should think, “Due to my past sinful activity I am now being punished. In this way, God is mercifully making me humble.” The word śayīta means one should remain peaceful and patient without mental agitation. Diṣṭa-bhuk means one must accept the Personality of Godhead as the supreme controller and not foolishly give up one’s faith due to material inconvenience. Tat te ’nukampāṁ su-samīkṣamāṇo bhuñjāna evātma-kṛtaṁ vipākam (Bhāg. 10.14.8). A devotee of the Lord always accepts material hardship as the mercy of Lord Kṛṣṇa; thus he becomes eligible for supreme liberation.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A saintly person should remain peaceful and materially inactive, maintaining his body without much endeavor. Even though possessed of full sensual, mental and physical strength, a saintly person should not become active for material gain but rather should always remain alert to his actual self-interest.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
ओज:सहोबलयुतं बिभ्रद् देहमकर्मकम् ।
शयानो वीतनिद्रश्च नेहेतेन्द्रियवानपि ॥ ४ ॥
original.transliteration:
ojaḥ-saho-bala-yutaṁ
bibhrad deham akarmakam
śayāno vīta-nidraś ca
nehetendriyavān api
original.word_for_word: ojaḥ — sensual strength; sahaḥ — mental strength; bala — physical strength; yutam — endowed with; bibhrat — maintaining; deham — the body; akarmakam — without endeavor; śayānaḥ — remaining peacefully; vīta — freed; nidraḥ — from nescience; ca — and; na — not; īheta — should endeavor; indriya-vān — possessing full bodily, mental and sensual strength; api — even though.

statements.statement: The word vīta-nidraḥ in this verse is very significant. Nidrā means “sleep” or “ignorance,” and vīta means “freed from.” In other words, a transcendentalist should always be awake to his eternal relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead and should carefully cultivate Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Being confident of his relationship with the Lord, he should not endeavor for his personal maintenance, knowing that the Lord is protecting him in all respects. Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura states that the example of the python is given so that one will not uselessly waste his time in bodily maintenance.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: One should not think, however, that the purpose of life is to lie on the ground like a python or to make a show of starving the body. The example of the python should not encourage one to become completely inactive. One should rather become active in spiritual advancement and inactive in material sense gratification. If one becomes completely inactive, that is certainly nidrā, or the darkness of ignorance, in which one remains asleep to his identity as an eternal servant of the Personality of Godhead.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A transcendentalist is eager to execute his service to the Lord, and therefore he is grateful when the Lord provides material facilities for such service. Mere renunciation of the material world is phalgu-vairāgya, or an immature stage of spiritual understanding. One must come to the stage of yukta-vairāgya, engaging everything in the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa. It is our practical experience that a devotee absorbed in spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness automatically receives all facilities for his personal maintenance.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The brāhmaṇa said: 'King, listen carefully: the enjoyment of sense-pleasure is the same in heaven and in hell; there is no doubt in this matter.'

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तो म्हणे राया सावधान । विषयसुखाचें जें सेवन । तें स्वर्गनरकीं गा समान । नाहीं अनुमान ये अर्थी

statements.statement: The pleasure Indra has in heaven enjoying Urvaśī - that same pleasure, for certain, the swine has in the filth with the sow.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: भोगितां उर्वशीसी । जें सुख स्वर्गीं इंद्रासी । तेंचि विष्ठेमाजीं सूकरासी । सूकरीपासीं निश्चित

statements.statement: Taking a living snake in the hand - this does not arise in a living being's mind; so the sādhus never hold attachment to objects.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जीत सापु धरावा हातीं । हें प्राणियांसी नुपजे चित्तीं । तेवीं विषयांची आसक्ती । साधु न धरिती सर्वथा

statements.statement: As beings obtain sorrow without praying for it, so, without desiring it, destiny makes one necessarily enjoy the pleasure of the senses.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जैसें न प्रार्थितां दुःख । प्राणी पावताति देख । तैसें न इच्छितां इंद्रियसुख । भोगवी आवश्यक अदृष्ट

statements.statement: 'If one becomes wholly devoted to paramārtha, the body cannot remain without food' - for this very certainty I made the python my guru.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: केवळ झालिया परमार्थपर । म्हणसी आहारेंवीण न राहे शरीर । येच निर्धारीं साचार । गुरु ’अजगर’ म्यां केला

statements.statement: Without effort, the python takes food that comes unasked; shaken, he does not abandon his steadiness; his resolve is fearless.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: उद्योगेंवीण आहारु । अयाचित सेवी अजगरु । डंडळोनि न सांडी धीरु । निधडा निर्धारु पैं त्याचा

statements.statement: By nature he opens his mouth; whatever falls in of itself, he does not consider tasty or tasteless; he accepts the food with contentment.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: स्वभावें तो मुख पसरी । सहजें पडे जें भीतरीं । सरस नीरस विचारु न करी । आहार अंगीकारी संतोषें

statements.statement: Such too is the state of the yogīs: they always contemplate the state of the Self; they partake of what comes of itself, giving up attachment to taste.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैशीचि योगियांची गती । सदा भाविती आत्मस्थिती । यदृच्छा आलें तें सेवती । रस‌आसक्ती सांडूनि

statements.statement: 'Little', 'much', 'tasty', 'tasteless' - he has no such saying; whatever comes naturally to the mouth, he eats at leisure.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: थोडें बहु सरसनिरसासी । हें कांहीं म्हणणें नाहीं त्यासी । स्वभावें जें आलें मुखासी । तें सावकाशीं सेवितु

statements.statement: If the python gets no food by chance for a long time, he does not slip from his resolve; he lies rolling in his own place.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अजगरासी बहु काळें । यदृच्छा आहारु न मिळे । तरी धारणेसी न टळे । पडिला लोळे निजस्थानीं

statements.statement: He has no sleep, yet he lies in the Self night and day; he makes no external effort; the body's food is by destiny.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: निद्रा नाहीं तयासी । परी निजे निजीं अहर्निशीं । बाह्य न करी उपायासी । भक्ष्य देहासी अदृष्टें

statements.statement: Whatever is in destiny at the time, that will come at that time; therefore his knowledge is not soiled and his steadiness does not slip, by his own knowledge.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अदृष्टीं असेल जें जें वेळें । तें तें मिळेल तेणें काळें । यालागीं त्याचें ज्ञान न मैळे । धारणा न ढळें निजबोधें

statements.statement: The python has great strength and a body huge in prowess, yet he does not make a rebellion of exertion; he lies with his mouth spread open.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अजगरासी बळ उदंड । देहो पराक्रमें प्रचंड । परी न करी उद्योगाचें बंड । पसरूनि तोंड पडिलासे

statements.statement: One who holds the desire for wife and sons and lives delighting in sense-objects suddenly meets a fall; therefore one should leave the house.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: स्त्रीपुत्रेच्छा धरून। विषयीं राहे रमून। तया अकस्मात ये पतन। म्हणून सोडून द्यावें घर

statements.statement: Whether welfare or ill-fare, it comes about by itself; karma is its cause; then why wander about in vain?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: कल्याण किंवा अकल्याण। तें आपोआप ये घडून। त्याला कर्म कारण। मग वांयां भ्रमण कां करावें

statements.statement: Prārabdha [the destiny already in motion] is the cause for all; by it happiness will surely come, know; just as sorrow comes and presses on one without any effort.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सर्वास प्रारब्ध कारण। तेणें अवश्य सुख मिळे जाण। जसें उद्योगाविण। दुःख येऊन भिडतें

statements.statement: Accepting this as true, not spending one's life in vain effort for the sake of happiness, one should remain lying like the python [ār; footnote: ajagara].

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हें सत्य मानून। व्यर्थ उद्योग करून। सुखार्थ आयुष्य न खर्चून। राहावें पडून आरापरी

statements.statement: Know this to be the secret meaning: whether in heaven or in hell, the pleasure of the senses comes to one; it is subject to prārabdha.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: रहस्यार्थ हाच जाण। स्वर्गी नरकींही असतां जाण। इंद्रियसुख ये मिळून। प्रारब्धाधीन तें असें

statements.statement: Sense-pleasure is dependent on others; see that it is the same for all. There is sorrow everywhere at the beginning and at the end; in the middle there is only the appearance of happiness.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: परतंत्र इंद्रियसुख। सर्वासी समान देख। आदि अंतीं सर्वत्र दुःख। मध्यें हा सुखभासमात्र

statements.statement: This is not the main [real] happiness; yet wherever a being lives, even that comes by destiny. This is understood from the python.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हें तों मुख्य सुख नसे। तथापि जीव जेथें वसे। तेथें दैवें तेंहीं मिळतसे। कळे असें आरापासून

statements.statement: Holding no worry in the mind, the python lies still; so one should live indifferent, always holding the python's way of life.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मनीं खंत न धरून। आर राहे पडून। तसें राहावें उदासीन । नित्य धरून अजगरवृत्ती

statements.statement: Lying constantly, the python keeps faith in destiny; whatever food comes at whatever time, he eats it with contentment.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: संतत पडूनी आर। विश्वास ठेवी दैवावर। जो जेव्हां जसा आहार। संतोषे तसा तो खातसे

statements.statement: Without looking at small or large, he eats whatever he gets; sometimes sweet comes, sometimes tasteless, yet he does not discard it.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: स्वल्पत्व महत्व न पाहून। मिळेल तें घे खावून। कधी ये मिष्ट मिळून। कधीं विरस तरी न टाकी

statements.statement: Having eaten it fully, he stays lying right there; even when no food comes there, holding patience, he lies awake.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तें सम्पूर्ण खाऊन। तेथेंच राहे पडून। न मिळतांही तेथें अन्न। धैर्य धरून पडून जागे

statements.statement: A man too, holding special patience, should lie like the python; whatever slightly sweeter food comes, he should eat and be content.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: विशेष धैर्य नरें धरून। आरापरी राहावें पडून। थोडें अधिक गोड अन्न। मिळे तें जेवून तोषावें

statements.statement: And if even that food does not come, keeping steadfastness in destiny, he should lie without sleeping, fixing his attention on his own nature.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तें अन्न तसेंही न मिळतां। धीरपणा दैवावरता। धरुनी पडावें न निजतां। स्वरूपीं दृष्टी लावुनी

statements.statement: Even while having in the body as much strength as is wanted, one should stay motionless; lying thus, all activities such as seeing fall away.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: अंगी पाहिजे तसें बळ। असतांही राहावें निश्चळ। असा पडतां सकळ। दर्शनादि व्यापार लोपती

statements.statement: Knowing this, I lie here like a python, always full of bliss. Now I tell of the tenth guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हें जाणुन मी येथ। पडलों अजगरवत। सदा आनंदभरित। सांगतो आतां दहावा गुरु

statements.statement: A saintly sage is happy and pleasing in his external behavior, whereas internally he is most grave and thoughtful. Because his knowledge is immeasurable and unlimited he is never disturbed, and thus in all respects he is like the tranquil waters of the unfathomable and unsurpassable ocean.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
मुनि: प्रसन्नगम्भीरो दुर्विगाह्यो दुरत्यय: ।
अनन्तपारो ह्यक्षोभ्य: स्तिमितोद इवार्णव: ॥ ५ ॥
original.transliteration:
muniḥ prasanna-gambhīro
durvigāhyo duratyayaḥ
ananta-pāro hy akṣobhyaḥ
stimitoda ivārṇavaḥ
original.word_for_word: muniḥ — a saintly sage; prasanna — pleasing; gambhīraḥ — very grave; durvigāhyaḥ — unfathomable; duratyayaḥ — unsurpassable; ananta-pāraḥ — unlimited; hi — certainly; akṣobhyaḥ — not to be disturbed; stimita — calm; udaḥ — water; iva — like; arṇavaḥ — the ocean.

statements.statement: Even in the midst of great distress, a self-realized sage does not lose control of himself, nor is his spiritual knowledge lost. Thus he is akṣobhya, or undisturbed. His mind is fixed on the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the reservoir of unlimited spiritual bliss, and having linked his consciousness with the supreme consciousness, his knowledge cannot be measured. A pure devotee, having taken shelter of the Lord’s lotus feet, possesses great spiritual power, and therefore he cannot be surpassed or overwhelmed. In fact, having developed his spiritual body, he is not affected by the deteriorating actions of time. Although outwardly he is friendly and pleasing to everyone, internally his mind is fixed in the Absolute Truth, and no one can understand his actual purpose or plan. Even the most intelligent human being cannot understand the mental activities of a self-realized devotee who has given up material life based on lust and greed and taken shelter at the lotus feet of the Lord. Such a great soul can be compared to the mighty ocean. Innumerable powerful rivers plunge into the ocean, but the ocean remains calm and peaceful. Thus, a saintly person is understood to be, like the ocean, pleasing, unfathomable, grave, unsurpassable, unlimited and unshakable.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: During the rainy season the swollen rivers rush into the ocean, and during the dry summer the rivers, now shallow, severely reduce their supply of water; yet the ocean does not swell up during the rainy season, nor does it dry up in the hot summer. In the same way, a saintly devotee who has accepted the Supreme Personality of Godhead as the goal of his life sometimes will receive by providence great material opulence, and sometimes he will find himself materially destitute. However, such a devotee of the Lord does not rejoice in a flourishing condition, nor is he morose when poverty-stricken.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
समृद्धकामोहीनो वा नारायणपरो मुनि: ।
नोत्सर्पेत न शुष्येत सरिद्भ‍िरिव सागर: ॥ ६ ॥
original.transliteration:
samṛddha-kāmo hīno vā
nārāyaṇa-paro muniḥ
notsarpeta na śuṣyeta
saridbhir iva sāgaraḥ
original.word_for_word: samṛddha — flourishing; kāmaḥ — material opulence; hīnaḥ — destitute; vā — or; nārāyaṇa — the Supreme Personality of Godhead; paraḥ — accepting as supreme; muniḥ — a saintly devotee; na — does not; utsarpeta — swell up; na — does not; śuṣyeta — dry up; saridbhiḥ — by the rivers; iva — like; sāgaraḥ — the ocean.

statements.statement: A sincere devotee of the Lord is always eager to meet the Lord and render Him transcendental service. He wants to remain fixed as an atom at the lotus feet of the Lord because Lord Kṛṣṇa, or Nārāyaṇa, is the reservoir of all pleasure. He rejoices when experiencing pure Kṛṣṇa consciousness and is morose when Kṛṣṇa is not present in his mind. In his dealings with the material world, a devotee cannot be disturbed by ordinary, materialistic people who sometimes insult him and accuse him of neglecting material sense gratification, just as the ocean cannot be disturbed by the innumerable rivers that enter into it. Sometimes lusty women approach a pure devotee, and sometimes speculative philosophers try to argue against the Personality of Godhead, but with all such ordinary people, a pure devotee is detached and undisturbed in his blissful Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The guru to be made, the ocean - hear his marks: depth, fullness, being pure, and so on.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ’समुद्र’ जो गुरु करणें । त्याचीं परिस पां लक्षणें । गंभीरत्व पूर्णपणें । निर्मळ असणें इत्यादि

statements.statement: The ocean is always serene; the yogī is always of serene face; at no time is there turbidity in him, by his own knowledge.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: समुद्र सदा सुप्रसन्न । योगी सदा प्रसन्नवदन । केव्हांही धुसमुशिलेंपण । नव्हें जाण निजबोधें

statements.statement: Though the muddy waters of the merged rivers come in, the very pure ocean is not stirred; so the yogī, while doing all kinds of actions, is always undisturbed.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मीनल्या सरितांचें समळ जळ । समुद्र डहुळेना अतिनिर्मळ । तैसीं नाना कर्में करितां सकळ । सदा अविकळ योगिया

statements.statement: The ocean is deep in its waters; the yogī is deep by his own experience; the ocean does not cross its shore; the lord of yogīs does not cross the guru's command.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जळें गंभीर सागर । योगिया स्वानुभवें गंभीर । वेळा नुल्लंघी सागर । नुल्लंघी योगीश्वर गुरु‌आज्ञा

statements.statement: Dirt does not stay in the ocean; it throws it far off with the waves; so too dirt does not stay within the yogī - by meditation, for certain.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मळु न राहे सागरीं । लाटांसरिसा टाकी दुरी । तैसाचि मळु योगियाभीतरीं । ध्यानें निर्धारीं न राहे

statements.statement: As the water in the ocean is still, without current, so the yogī is wholly unshaken, without fear of death.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: प्रवाहेंवीण जळ । समुद्रीं जेवीं निश्चळ । मृत्युभयेंवीण अचंचळ । असे केवळ योगिया

statements.statement: The ocean is salty to all; the lord of yogīs is not so; to all beings he is sweet; his knowledge is real.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: समुद्र सर्वांप्रति क्षार । तैसा नव्हे योगीश्वर । तो सर्वां जीवांसी मधुर । बोधु साचार पैं त्याचा

statements.statement: In the rainy season all the rivers bring immeasurable water; by that the ocean does not rejoice greatly; the water does not rise in the ocean.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: वर्षाकाळीं सरिता सकळ । घे‌ऊनि आल्या अमूप जळ । तेणें हरुषेजेना प्रबळ । न चढे जळ जळाब्धीं

statements.statement: When summer comes, the floods of the rivers subside; thinking it a sorrow, the lord of waters does not ebb.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ग्रीष्मकाळाचिये प्राप्ती । सरितांचे यावे राहती । ते मानूनियां खंती । अपांपती वोहटेना

statements.statement: So too in the yogī, even if various kinds of prosperity come, he holds no ego in the body; no pride rises in him at all.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसेंचि योगियांच्या ठायीं । नाना समृध्दि आलिया पाहीं । अहंता न धरी देहीं । गर्वु कांहीं चढेना

statements.statement: When prosperity has been spent, there is no regret in the yogī's heart; with his vision set on Nārāyaṇa, he lives in happy contentment.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: समृध्दि वेंचिलिया पाठीं । खंती नाहीं योगिया पोटीं । तो नारायणपरदृष्टीं । सुखसंतुष्टी वर्ततु

statements.statement: Poverty and wealth are both equal to his mind; he has no attachment to worldly affairs; he is truly devoted to Nārāyaṇa, through his own knowledge.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: दरिद्र आणि संपन्नता । दोन्ही समान त्याचिया चित्ता । नाहीं प्रपंचाची आसक्तता । नारायणपर तत्त्वतां निजबोधें

statements.statement: Lying thus constantly, whether enjoyments come or do not come, one should feel neither joy nor sorrow. This is understood by making the ocean one's guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: असा सतत पडतां। भोग मिळतां अथवा न मिळतां। न कीजे हर्षविषादता। समुद्रा गुरु करितां हें कळे

statements.statement: He is ever full; when the rivers come in the rainy season and meet him, he does not burst, and in joy he does not leave his shore to flow out.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तो नित्य पूर्ण असून। वर्षाकाळीं नद्या येऊन। मिळतां न जाय फुटून। हर्षें वेळा सोडून बाहेर

statements.statement: The various rivers dry up in summer and do not meet the ocean; yet the lord of rivers does not dry up from grief. That way should be learned.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: विविध नद्या त्या ग्रीष्मीं वाळती। समुद्रा न मिळती। तरी दुःखें न वाळे सरित्पती। ती रीती घ्यावी

statements.statement: One should remain subject to one's own dharma; when enjoyments come one should not be elated; when they do not come one should not be dejected; one should be of one form.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: स्वधर्माधीन राहावें। भोग मिळतां हृष्ट न व्हावें। न मिळतांही दीन न व्हावें। असावें एकरूप

statements.statement: Though effort is made, the bottom of the ocean is not found: how many jewels are within, how long and broad it is.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जरी यत्न केला तरी। ठाव न लागे समुद्रीं। रत्नें किती अंतरीं। हा लांब रुंद किती असे

statements.statement: Making this a firm resolve, as it cannot be fathomed, so, becoming a worthy man, one should be at ease day after day.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हेची दृढ निश्चय करून। जसें न ये कळून। तसें योग्यानें होऊन। अनुदिन स्वस्थ असावें

statements.statement: 'This man is distinguished, or this one is inferior': when people reflect so, one should not let them find one's end or limit; one should be hard to get across [duratyaya; the editor's note: 'one should go beyond sorrow'].

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: विशिष्ट किंवा हा निकृष्ट नर। असा लोकीं करितां विचार। न लावूं द्यावा अंतपार। दुरत्यय असावें

statements.statement: 'How many qualities are here?': one should not let this count be made; holding a state free of change, one should remain unmoving.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: गुण येथें किती असती। न करूं द्यावी ही गणती। निर्विकारपणें स्थिती। धरूनी राहावें निश्चळ

statements.statement: Like the ever-full ocean, one should show cheerfulness outwardly. Accept this from the ocean; now listen to the eleventh guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सदा पूर्ण समुद्रापरी। प्रसन्नता दावावी बाहेरी। हें समुद्रापासूनी स्वीकारीं। अवधारीं आतां अक्रावा गुरु

statements.statement: One who has failed to control his senses immediately feels attraction upon seeing a woman’s form, which is created by the illusory energy of the Supreme Lord. Indeed, when the woman speaks with enticing words, smiles coquettishly and moves her body sensuously, his mind is immediately captured, and thus he falls blindly into the darkness of material existence, just as the moth maddened by the fire rushes blindly into its flames.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
द‍ृष्ट्वा स्त्रियं देवमायां तद्भ‍ावैरजितेन्द्रिय: ।
प्रलोभित: पतत्यन्धे तमस्यग्नौ पतङ्गवत् ॥ ७ ॥
original.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā striyaṁ deva-māyāṁ
tad-bhāvair ajitendriyaḥ
pralobhitaḥ pataty andhe
tamasy agnau pataṅga-vat
original.word_for_word: dṛṣṭvā — seeing; striyam — a woman; deva-māyām — whose form is created by the illusory energy of the Lord; tat-bhāvaiḥ — by the alluring seductive activities of the woman; ajita — one who has not controlled; indriyaḥ — his senses; pralobhitaḥ — enticed; patati — falls down; andhe — into the blindness of ignorance; tamasi — into the darkness of hell; agnau — in the fire; pataṅga-vat — just like the moth.

statements.statement: Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī explains in this regard that just as a moth is killed by its attraction to the form of fire, similarly a bee can easily be killed by exploiting its attraction to the fragrance of flowers. Furthermore, hunters may trap and kill an elephant by exploiting its sensuous desire to touch a captive female elephant and may also kill a deer by attracting it with the sounds of their horns; and a fish is killed by its desire to taste the bait on a hook. Thus, one who desires to learn detachment from material illusion should accept these five helpless creatures as guru and learn the needful. Certainly one who is lusty to enjoy the illusory form of woman will be quickly buried in material illusion. Of the five types of fatal attraction involving material sense objects, the lesson of rūpa, or form, is illustrated in this verse.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A foolish person with no intelligent discrimination is immediately aroused at the sight of a lusty woman beautifully decorated with golden ornaments, fine clothing and other cosmetic features. Being eager for sense gratification, such a fool loses all intelligence and is destroyed just like the moth who rushes into the blazing fire.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
योषिद्धिरण्याभरणाम्बरादि-
द्रव्येषु मायारचितेषु मूढ: ।
प्रलोभितात्मा ह्युपभोगबुद्ध्या
पतङ्गवन्नश्यति नष्टद‍ृष्टि: ॥ ८ ॥
original.transliteration:
yoṣid-dhiraṇyābharaṇāmbarādi-
dravyeṣu māyā-raciteṣu mūḍhaḥ
pralobhitātmā hy upabhoga-buddhyā
pataṅga-van naśyati naṣṭa-dṛṣṭiḥ
original.word_for_word: yoṣit — of women; hiraṇya — golden; ābharaṇa — ornaments; ambara — clothing; ādi — and so on; dravyeṣu — upon seeing such things; māyā — by the illusory energy of the Lord; raciteṣu — manufactured; mūḍhaḥ — a fool with no discrimination; pralobhita — aroused by lusty desires; ātmā — such a person; hi — certainly; upabhoga — for sense gratification; buddhyā — with the desire; pataṅga-vat — like the moth; naśyati — is destroyed; naṣṭa — is ruined; dṛṣṭiḥ — whose intelligence.

statements.statement: Actually, women have the power to attract men through all of the material senses. Men become lusty by seeing the body of a woman, by smelling her fragrance, by hearing her voice, by tasting her lips and by touching her body. However, the foolish relationship based on material sex attraction begins by seeing, and thus rūpa, or form, is very prominent in the process of ruining one’s intelligence. This fact has been exploited in modern times by huge pornography industries, which prey on unfortunate men and women. The example of the foolish moth rushing into the fire and destroying itself is most appropriate in this regard, for one who becomes addicted to the momentary pleasure of sex indulgence certainly loses his power to understand the spiritual reality behind dull matter.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A lusty person becomes blind and foolish through sex indulgence, and his soul is lost in the fire of sense gratification. This whole disaster can be avoided by taking seriously to the process of chanting the holy names of the Lord: Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare/ Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare. Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His empowered representatives such as Śrīla Prabhupāda have created a movement to save people from the dungeon of material life, and we should all seriously take advantage of this opportunity.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The divine Māyā made of the guṇas - her form with qualities is women; there a temptation arose in beings, to enjoy the pleasure of woman.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: दैवी गुणमयी जे माया । तिचें सगुणस्वरूप त्या स्त्रिया । तेथ प्रलोभ उपजला प्राणियां । भोग भोगावया स्त्रीसुखें

statements.statement: The pleasure of enjoying a woman, know, is nothing but sorrow; like putting sweet poison in the mouth, in its ripening, see, it ends in death.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: स्त्रीभोगाचें जें सुख । तें जाण पां केवळ दुःख । तोंडीं घालितां मधुर विख । परिपाकीं देख प्राणांतु

statements.statement: What pleasure is there for the moth in touching the body of the lamp? Going by force to embrace it, they set out on the road to death.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: दीपाचिया अंगसंगा । कोण सुख आहे पतंगा । वळें आलिंगूं जातां पैं गा । मरणमार्गा लागले

statements.statement: Seeing the moth ahead dead, the ones behind are still excessively attached to the lamp; so some are deceived by lust for woman, and some love her excessively, after the way of the moth.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पुढिला पतंग निमाला देखती । तरी मागिल्या दीपीं अति‌आसक्ती । तेवीं स्त्रीकामें एक ठकती । एकां अतिप्रीती पतंगन्यायें

statements.statement: So, in the fool without discernment, greed arises for the pleasure of woman; death through contact with her is not escaped by people at all.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तेवीं विवेकहीन मूर्खा । लोलुप्य उपजे स्त्रीसुखा । तत्संसर्गें मरण लोकां । न चुके देखा सर्वथा

statements.statement: Through delight in the beauty of the lamp, the moth burns and sinks in the oil; so surely, through the company of woman, a downfall into blind darkness happens at once.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: दीप-रूपाचेनि कोडें । पतंग जळोनि स्नेहीं बुडे । तेवीं स्त्रीसंगे अवश्य घडे । पतन रोकडें अंधतमीं

statements.statement: See: woman and gold, garments, ornaments, gems - created by Māyā to make one fall - are the cause of people's downfall.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पहा पां कांता आणि सोनें । वस्त्रें आभरणें रत्‍ने । मायेनें रचिलीं पडणें । पतनाकारणें जनांच्या

statements.statement: Māyā binds those of uncontrolled senses; she does not face the servants of God at all; for one whose love for Govinda is great, the Ocean of Mercy is the protector.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: माया अजितेंद्रिया बाधी । दासांसंमुख नव्हे त्रिशुद्धी । ज्याची अतिप्रीती गोविंदीं । त्यासी कृपानिधि रक्षिता

statements.statement: Seeing a lovely woman, the sight of discernment is destroyed; those who, tempted, embrace her for enjoyment suffer crores of sorrows.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: वनिता देखोनि गोमटी । विवेकाची होय नष्ट दृष्टी । प्रलोभें उपभोगा देती मिठी । ते दुःखकोटी भोगिती

statements.statement: Seeing the glittering lamp-form, the moth has the thought of enjoyment; leaping in quickly, burned in the fire, they perish.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देखोनि दीपरूपीं झगमगी । उपभोगबुद्धि पतंगी । उडी घालितां वेगीं । जळोनि आगीं नासती

statements.statement: Thus Māyā in the form of woman deludes beings through the thought of enjoyment; those who are averse to Hari's feet - only them does Māyā delude.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एवं योषितारूपें माया । उपभोगबुद्धि भुलवी प्राणियां । जे विमुख हरीच्या पायां । त्यांसीच माया भुलवितु

statements.statement: He who serves the five objects through the five senses goes to death; making these five his gurus and taking instruction, he gives up the sense-objects.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो विषय पांच पंचेंद्रियांनीं। सेवी तो जाय मरूनी। हें पांच गुरु करूनी। शिक्षण घेऊनी विषय सोडी

statements.statement: As one asleep does not perceive the sense-objects though they exist, so, if one is wakeful, who would not be freed from bondage? [Sanskrit verse; literal rendering]

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: स्वपन्नेव न जानाति सतोऽपि विषयान्यथा। तथैव जागरूकश्चेत्को न मुच्येत बंधनात

statements.statement: He who does not bring the senses under control, seeing the charms and beauty of women, goes infatuated and dies like the moth.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो नकरीं इंद्रियें स्वाधीन। स्त्रियांचे विलास लावण्य पाहून। जाई मोहित होऊन। पतंगासमान मरे तो

statements.statement: He who looks with delight at a form is like the moth that sees a lamp, leaps upon it, and then burns up there by himself.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो हर्षें पाहतां रूप। तो पतंग देखोनि दीप। त्यावरी घाली झेप। मग आपोआप जळे तेथें

statements.statement: The man who goes deluded on seeing a new woman, a clever, pleasure-loving young woman, will die in vain.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो जाय नर भुलुनी। पाहतां नवी रमणी। फर्डी विलासिनी तरुणी। तो व्यर्थ मरून जाईल

statements.statement: A saintly person should accept only enough food to keep his body and soul together. He should go from door to door accepting just a little bit of food from each family. Thus he should practice the occupation of the honeybee.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
स्तोकं स्तोकं ग्रसेद् ग्रासं देहो वर्तेत यावता ।
गृहानहिंसन्नातिष्ठेद् वृत्तिं माधुकरीं मुनि: ॥ ९ ॥
original.transliteration:
stokaṁ stokaṁ grased grāsaṁ
deho varteta yāvatā
gṛhān ahiṁsann ātiṣṭhed
vṛttiṁ mādhukarīṁ muniḥ
original.word_for_word: stokam stokam — always, a little bit; graset — one should eat; grāsam — food; dehaḥ — the material body; varteta — that it may live; yāvatā — with that much; gṛhān — the householders; ahiṁsan — not harassing; ātiṣṭhet — one should practice; vṛttim — the occupation; mādhu-karīm — of the honeybee; muniḥ — a saintly person.

statements.statement: Sometimes a honeybee is attracted by the extraordinary aroma of a particular lotus flower and lingers there, neglecting his usual activity of flying from flower to flower. Unfortunately, at sunset the lotus flower closes, and thus the infatuated honeybee is trapped. Similarly, a sannyāsī or brahmacārī may discover that excellent foodstuff is available at a particular house, and therefore, instead of wandering from place to place, he may become a veritable resident of such a well-fed household. Thus he will become bewildered by the illusion of family life and fall down from the platform of renunciation. Also, if a mendicant takes unfair advantage of the Vedic custom of charity and takes too often from a single family, the resentment he causes will disturb the social order. An ideal sage should, like the honeybee, travel from place to place, but he must be careful not to become a chubby bee by going to many houses and eating sumptuously at each house. According to Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, such a chubby bee will undoubtedly become entangled in the network of māyā. No one should be overly attached to the gratification of his tongue, because this will lead to an overstuffed belly and then uncontrollable lust. In conclusion, one should not endeavor very much for material sense gratification but should instead endeavor strenuously to spread the glories of the Supreme Lord, Kṛṣṇa. This is the proper use of human energy.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Just as the honeybee takes nectar from all flowers, big and small, an intelligent human being should take the essence from all religious scriptures.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
अणुभ्यश्च महद्भ्यश्च शास्त्रेभ्य: कुशलो नर: ।
सर्वत: सारमादद्यात् पुष्पेभ्य इव षट्पद: ॥ १० ॥
original.transliteration:
aṇubhyaś ca mahadbhyaś ca
śāstrebhyaḥ kuśalo naraḥ
sarvataḥ sāram ādadyāt
puṣpebhya iva ṣaṭpadaḥ
original.word_for_word: aṇubhyaḥ — from the smallest; ca — and; mahadbhyaḥ — from the greatest; ca — also; śāstrebhyaḥ — from religious scriptures; kuśalaḥ — intelligent; naraḥ — a man; sarvataḥ — from all; sāram — the essence; ādadyāt — should take; puṣpebhyaḥ — from the flowers; iva — like; ṣaṭpadaḥ — the honeybee.

statements.statement: In human society the original knowledge is called Veda, and the essential part of veda, or knowledge, is Kṛṣṇa consciousness. As stated in Bhagavad-gītā (15.15), vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ. From the honeybee, an intelligent human being should learn to take the essence, or nectar, of all knowledge. A honeybee does not waste its time trying to carry away an entire bush or garden, but rather takes the essential nectar. We may thus study the difference between the honeybee and the ass, who carries heavy loads. Education does not mean to become an intellectual ass carrying heavy loads of useless knowledge; rather, one should accept the essential knowledge that leads to an eternal life of bliss and understanding.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: At the present time people generally have a sectarian concept of religion, and yet there is no scientific understanding of the Absolute Truth. Such complacent, dogmatic, sectarian religionists can certainly learn something from the example of the honeybee given in this verse.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A saintly person should not think, “This food I will keep to eat tonight and this other food I can save for tomorrow.” In other words, a saintly person should not store foodstuffs acquired by begging. Rather, he should use his own hands as his plate and eat whatever fits on them. His only storage container should be his belly, and whatever conveniently fits into his belly should be his stock of food. Thus one should not imitate the greedy honeybee who eagerly collects more and more honey.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
सायन्तनं श्वस्तनं वा न सङ्गृह्णीत भिक्षितम् ।
पाणिपात्रोदरामत्रो मक्षिकेव न सङ्ग्रही ॥ ११ ॥
original.transliteration:
sāyantanaṁ śvastanaṁ vā
na saṅgṛhṇīta bhikṣitam
pāṇi-pātrodarāmatro
makṣikeva na saṅgrahī
original.word_for_word: sāyantanam — meant for the night; śvastanam — meant for tomorrow; vā — either; na — not; saṅgṛhṇīta — should accept; bhikṣitam — food in charity; pāṇi — with the hand; pātra — as one’s plate; udara — with the belly; amatraḥ — as the storage container; makṣikā — the bee; iva — like; na — not; saṅgrahī — a collector.

statements.statement: There are two types of honeybees: those who collect nectar from the flowers and those who actually manufacture honey in the beehive. This verse refers to the second class. The greedy honeybee eventually collects so much honey that he is trapped in his hive; and in the same way, a materialistic person becomes trapped under the burden of unnecessary material accumulation. One who is interested in making spiritual progress should avoid such a situation; however, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura points out that for the purpose of spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness one may accumulate an unlimited amount of material opulence. This is called yukta-vairāgya, or using everything in the service of Kṛṣṇa. A saintly person who is unable to work in Lord Caitanya’s mission should practice austerities and collect only what he can hold in his hands and belly. However, one who has given his life to Kṛṣṇa may collect unlimitedly on Lord Kṛṣṇa’s behalf. In fact, without acquiring material opulence, how is it possible to spread the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement all over the world? But if one tries to personally enjoy the funds or facilities acquired for the missionary activities of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, he commits the greatest offense. Therefore, even in the name of Lord Kṛṣṇa, one should collect only what he can immediately engage in practical devotional service; otherwise one will fall down to the platform of ordinary greediness.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A saintly mendicant should not even collect foodstuffs to eat later in the same day or the next day. If he disregards this injunction and like the honeybee collects more and more delicious foodstuffs, that which he has collected will indeed ruin him.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:

मक्षिका इव सङ्गृह्णन् सह तेन विनश्यति ॥ १२ ॥

sāyantanaṁ śvastanaṁ vā
na saṅgṛhṇīta bhikṣukaḥ
makṣikā iva saṅgṛhṇan
saha tena vinaśyati

statements.statement: Bhramara refers to that honeybee who wanders about from flower to flower, and makṣikā is the honeybee who accumulates more and more honey in the beehive with great attachment. A saintly mendicant should be like the bhramara bee because if he imitates the makṣikā bee his spiritual consciousness will be ruined. This point is so important that it is repeated in this verse.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The bee enters within the flower, but does not let the flower be crushed; he accomplishes his own purpose; the bee's mind is pure.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: भ्रमरु रिघोनि पुष्पामधीं । फुल तरी कुचुंबों नेदी । आपुली करी अर्थसिद्धी । चोखट बुद्धि भ्रमराची

statements.statement: Such is the yogī's way: a morsel at each house, he fills his belly by begging alms; he causes no distress to householders.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

statements.statement: Even if a flower is very small, the bee does not neglect it; entering that too, he enjoys its fragrance.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अतिलहान सुमन जें कांहीं । भ्रमरा तेथ उपेक्षा नाहीं । रिघोनि त्याच्याही ठायीं । आमोद पाहीं सेवितु

statements.statement: So too the yogī is neat: in the view of the scriptures very discerning; he makes no argument of small or great; he becomes a taker of the essence.

statements.statement: The śāstras are arrayed in many kinds; one does not get through them by studying for a whole lifetime; one should take their essence. This knowledge the bumblebee gives.

statements.statement: A saintly person should never touch a young girl. In fact, he should not even let his foot touch a wooden doll in the shape of a woman. By bodily contact with a woman he will surely be captured by illusion, just as the elephant is captured by the she-elephant due to his desire to touch her body.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Elephants are captured in the jungle in the following way. A large hole is dug and then covered over with grass, leaves, mud and so on. Then a she-elephant is exhibited in front of the male elephant, who chases after her with lusty desire, falls into the hole and is captured. The lesson to be learned from the elephant is that the desire to relish the touch sensation is certainly the cause of ruining one’s life. An intelligent person, noting the elephant’s great propensity to sport with the she-elephant, will take this excellent example to heart. Therefore, somehow or other one should avoid being cheated by allurement to the sensuous form of woman. One should not allow one’s mind to be lost in lusty dreams of sex pleasure. There are various types of sense gratification to be enjoyed between men and women, including speaking, contemplating, touching, sexual intercourse, etc., and all of these constitute the network of illusion by which one is helplessly bound like an animal. Somehow or other one should remain aloof from sense gratification in the form of sex pleasure; otherwise, there is no possibility of understanding the spiritual world.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A man possessing intelligent discrimination should not under any circumstances try to exploit the beautiful form of a woman for his sense gratification. Just as an elephant trying to enjoy a she-elephant is killed by other bull elephants also enjoying her company, one trying to enjoy a lady’s company can at any moment be killed by her other lovers who are stronger than he.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Just as one is enchanted by the beautiful form of a woman, many other men will also be enchanted, and there is danger that they will be stronger than oneself and may even jealously kill one. Crimes of passion are extremely common. This is another disadvantage of material life.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: See the sixty-year-old elephants of noble breed: before them, how much are men? Yet through contact with the body of a she-elephant they get the bondage of men.
