statements.statement: He who does not bring men into his sight is made subject to men by the she-elephants; at their word he rises and sits; he is struck on the head with the goad.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जो दृष्टीं नाणी मनुष्यांसी । तो स्त्रियां वश केला मानवांसी । त्यांचेनि बोलें उठी बैसी । माथां अंकुशीं मारिजे

statements.statement: So, to conquer worldly existence, those sannyāsīs who are steadfast in their own dharma should, on seeing women, flee at once.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एवं जिणावया संसारासी । जे स्वधर्मनिष्ठ संन्यासी । तिंही देखोनि योषितांसी । लागवेगेंसी पळावें

statements.statement: No meeting with women, no talk with women; the moment a woman is seen with the eyes, one should flee in haste.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: नको स्त्रियांची भेटी । नको स्त्रियांसी गोष्टी । स्त्री देखतांचि दिठीं । उठा‌उठीं पळावें

statements.statement: They call themselves 'men', yet in the end they hold women's feet; how will there be liberation for them? Through company of women, downfall.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ’पुरुष’ आपणया म्हणविती । सेखीं स्त्रियांचे पाय धरिती । त्यांसी कैसेनि हो‌ईल मुक्ती । स्त्रीसंगतीं अधःपात

statements.statement: Thus, for gods, men and beasts, the root of ruin is the company of woman; through that company comes attachment to home; the arising of quarrel has woman as its root.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एवं सुरनरपशूंप्रती । नाशासी मूळ स्त्रीसंगती । तिचेनि संगें गृहासक्ती । कलहप्राप्ती स्त्रीमूळ

statements.statement: By serving women without rest, lust attains madness; one mad with lust is carried wholly to a downfall.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अविश्रम स्त्री सेवितां । कामु पावे उन्मत्तता । उन्मत्त कामें सर्वथा । अधःपाता ने‌इजे

statements.statement: Woman, and the second, wealth: this alone is the dreadful calamity in this world; by this one's own true interest is lost, and in the end it brings the destruction of life.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: स्त्री आणि दुसरा अर्थु । हाचि ये लोकीं घोर अनर्थु । येणें अंतरला निजस्वार्थु । शेखीं करी घातु प्राणाचा

statements.statement: Whether it is a woman of one's own or of another, if one holds affection for her, a firm fetter of love will fall on one.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: स्वसत्तेची किंवा पराची। नारी असो तिची। प्रीति धरितां स्नेहाची। बेडी दृढ पडेल

statements.statement: Even if a beautiful woman is made of wood, if one touches her with the foot one becomes bound; the elephant gives this witness.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जरी रूपवती काष्ठमयी। नारी असो तिला पायीं। स्पर्श करतां बद्ध होई। गज देई साक्ष ही

statements.statement: Then how will a woman of flesh not bind? Tell me, who would hold such a thought within?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मग कसी बरें नारी। मांसमयी असे तरी। न बांधील हें अंतरीं। कोण धरी सांग बा

statements.statement: For her own advantage a woman pushes [one] into the pit of delusion; he who keeps love for her in his belly goes at the end to hell.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: आपुल्या हितासाठीं। नारी मोहगर्ती लोटी। तिचें प्रेम जो पोटीं। ठेवी तो शेवटीं नरकी जाय

statements.statement: Seeing a she-elephant, elephants run to embrace her; there, those who are strong strike the weak.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हत्तीण पाहून हत्ती। आलिंगावया धांवती। तेथें जे बलिष्ठ असती। ते हाणती निर्बळा

statements.statement: So with men: if they run on seeing a woman, the strong quickly come and kill him.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नर तसे जे स्त्री पाहून। जाती जरी धांवून। त्वरें बलिष्ठ येऊन। त्याला मारून टाकिती

statements.statement: He who, like a rutting elephant [footnote: matta hattī], runs at a beautiful woman the moment he sees her, will wallow in hell, O king.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो मत्तेभाचेपरी। पाहतांचि सुंदरी। धाव घे तिजवरी। तो नरकाभीतरी लोळेल भूपा

statements.statement: He alone is supremely pure who, having come of age, does not touch women; know him to be equal to Śiva.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तोचि परम पावन। जो नर वयांत येऊन। स्त्रियांसी न घे शिवून। शिवसमान जाण तो

statements.statement: As Nārāyaṇa was not deluded on seeing the celestial courtesan, holding such steadiness, he is Parabrahman, know.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: स्वर्वेश्यावलोकन करून। जसा न भुलला नारायण। तसें धैर्य धरून। राहे तो जाण परब्रह्म

statements.statement: When the woman, tamisrā [footnote: the night in the form of woman], is seen and the darkness of pleasure spreads, the lust-possessed [lit. 'lust-demons'] feel delight in doing all sorts of antics.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: स्त्री तमिस्रा दिसतां। विलासांधकार पसरतां। हर्ष वाटे कामीभूतां। नानाचेष्टा करावया

statements.statement: The steadfast, clever yogī, on seeing the woman-night, at once sits on the siddhāsana and stays constantly awake.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: धीर यो(ऽ)गी चतुर। स्त्रीतमिस्रा दिसतां सत्वर। बसती सिद्धासनावर। निरंतर जागती

statements.statement: A greedy person accumulates a large quantity of money with great struggle and pain, but the person who has struggled so much to acquire this wealth is not always allowed to enjoy it himself or give it in charity to others. The greedy man is like the bee who struggles to produce a large quantity of honey, which is then stolen by a man who will enjoy it personally or sell it to others. No matter how carefully one hides his hard-earned wealth or tries to protect it, there are those who are expert in detecting the whereabouts of valuable things, and they will steal it.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
न देयं नोपभोग्यं च लुब्धैर्यद् दु:खसञ्चितम् ।
भुङ्क्ते तदपि तच्चान्यो मधुहेवार्थविन्मधु ॥ १५ ॥
original.transliteration:
na deyaṁ nopabhogyaṁ ca
lubdhair yad duḥkha-sañcitam
bhuṅkte tad api tac cānyo
madhu-hevārthavin madhu
original.word_for_word: na — not; deyam — to be given in charity to others; na — not; upabhogyam — to be enjoyed personally; ca — also; lubdhaiḥ — by those who are greedy; yat — that which; duḥkha — with great struggle and pain; sañcitam — is accumulated; bhuṅkte — he enjoys; tat — that; api — nevertheless; tat — that; ca — also; anyaḥ — someone else; madhu-hā — the one who steals the honey from the beehive; iva — like; artha — wealth; vit — one who knows how to recognize; madhu — the honey.

statements.statement: One may argue that a wealthy man may conceal his money so expertly, by investing it in banks, stocks, properties, and so on, that there is no danger of theft. Only foolish people actually hide money by burying it in the ground or placing it under a mattress. But despite the fact that the majority of the world’s wealth has been accumulated in highly developed capitalistic countries, these countries are being severely challenged by many enemies who threaten at any moment to overrun the capitalists and steal their wealth. Similarly, we often find that the children of wealthy people are kidnapped, and then their parents must pay huge ransoms. Sometimes the parents themselves may also be kidnapped. Furthermore, there are so-called investment counselors who are expert in stealing the money of rich people; and in the modern age governments have also become expert in stealing money by taxation. Thus, the word artha-vit indicates one who by hook or by crook is expert in stealing the hard-earned wealth of other people. The bees work frantically to produce honey, but they will not enjoy their honey. As Lord Kṛṣṇa states, mṛtyuḥ sarva-haraś cāham: “I will come as death personified and steal everything.” (Bg. 10.34) Somehow or other one’s hard-earned material opulence will be stolen, and therefore, as mentioned in this verse, one should not work uselessly like the foolish honeybee.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Just as a hunter takes away the honey laboriously produced by the honeybees, similarly, saintly mendicants such as brahmacārīs and sannyāsīs are entitled to enjoy the property painstakingly accumulated by householders dedicated to family enjoyment.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
सुदु:खोपार्जितैर्वित्तैराशासानां गृहाशिष: ।
मधुहेवाग्रतो भुङ्क्ते यतिर्वै गृहमेधिनाम् ॥ १६ ॥
original.transliteration:
su-duḥkhopārjitair vittair
āśāsānāṁ gṛhāśiṣaḥ
madhu-hevāgrato bhuṅkte
yatir vai gṛha-medhinām
original.word_for_word: su-duḥkha — with great struggle; upārjitaiḥ — that which is acquired; vittaiḥ — material opulence; āśāsānām — of those fervently desiring; gṛha — related to domestic enjoyment; āśiṣaḥ — blessings; madhu-hā — the person who steals honey from the bees; iva — like; agrataḥ — first, before others; bhuṅkte — enjoys; yatiḥ — a saintly mendicant; vai — certainly; gṛha-medhinām — of those dedicated to material family life.

statements.statement: The scriptures state: “Saintly mendicants in the sannyāsa order of life and brahmacārīs have first right to enjoy the sumptuous foodstuffs produced by the householders. If the householders enjoy such foodstuffs without first offering them in charity to the mendicants, such neglectful householders must undergo the lunar fast called cāndrāyaṇam.” In family life one must overcome the natural tendency toward selfishness by giving abundant charity. Modern society foolishly does not observe such Vedic injunctions, and as a result the world has become overrun by envious gṛha-medhīs, or persons wholly and solely dedicated to personal gratification in family life. Therefore, the whole world is seized in an uncontrollable spasm of violence and suffering. If one wants to live peacefully one must follow the Vedic injunctions regulating family life. Although the householders work very hard to accumulate money, the saintly sannyāsīs and brahmacārīs have the right to first enjoy the fruits of such labor. The conclusion is that one should give first priority to spiritual advancement in Kṛṣṇa consciousness and thus perfect one’s life. Then even without personal endeavor, one will be supplied all of one’s necessities by the mercy of the Personality of Godhead.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: He does not eat himself, nor does he do dharma; the wretch does not let his household eat; like the honeybee he hoards with toil.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: स्वयें खाये ना धर्मु न करी । घरच्यांसी खा‌ऊं नेदी दरिद्री । मधुमक्षिकेच्या परी । संग्रहो करी कष्टोनि

statements.statement: Bees build the honeycomb with effort; within it lumps of honey are collected; seeing it, the eyes of the world try to take it by the force of means.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: माशा मोहळा बांधिती बळें । माजीं सांचले मधाचे गोळे । तें देखोनि जगाचे डोळे । उपायबळें घेवों पाहाती

statements.statement: So too the miser's hoard, like a yakṣa's wealth: no charity, no protection of dharma; thieves take it, killing him; and the king, punishing even them, takes it.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसेंचि कृपणाचें यक्षधन । नाहीं दान धर्मसंरक्षण । त्यातें तस्कर नेती मारून । त्यांसही दंडून राजा ने

statements.statement: Those who hoard with toil do not get enjoyment; that wealth is enjoyed by those who own nothing; strange is the course of destiny.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जे शिणोनि संग्रह करिती । त्यांसी नव्हे भोगप्राप्ती । ते द्रव्यें अपरिग्रही सेविती । दैवगती विचित्र

statements.statement: The householder has food prepared with effort; the sannyāsī, without toil, goes and takes the meal; on this point destiny is the proof.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: प्रयासें गृहस्थ करवी अन्न । तें संन्यासी न शिणतां जाण । करूनि जाय भोजन । अदृष्ट प्रमाण ये अर्थीं

statements.statement: Therefore one who stays subject to destiny has no longing to hoard; that very destiny is his helper; the miserliness of others is done in vain.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: यालागीं दैवाधीन जो राहे । तो संग्रहाची चाड न वाहे । तें अदृष्टचि साह्य आहे । कृपणता वायें करिताति

statements.statement: As, driving away the bees of the honeycomb, the honey-taker drinks the honey, so it happens to the householder: sannyāsīs carry off the prepared meal.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जैसें दवडून मोहळमाशियांसी । मधुहर्ता मधु प्राशी । तैसें होय गृहस्थासी । नेती संन्यासी सिद्धपाकु

statements.statement: Whether one dwells in meditation-yoga, or is engaged in austerity, or in the study of knowledge, he should not toil for the belly.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जरी वसें ध्यानयोगीं। किंवा गुंतें तपालागीं। किंवा विद्याभ्यासालागीं। तरी पोटालागीं न शिणावें

statements.statement: O king, the means that brings ease: when hunger comes, take the bag in hand and go begging alms.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: भूपा सौख्यकारकसाधन। भूक लागल्या जाण। हाती झोळी घेऊन। भिक्षाटण करावें

statements.statement: The man who is a householder has much toil: wandering in the village, the forest and the shop to get wood, vegetables and grain.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो पुरुष गृहस्थ। त्याला श्रम पडती बहुत। ग्रामीं वनीं दुकानीं हिंडत। काष्ठ भाजी धान्य घ्याया

statements.statement: They cook, bearing the suffering, and do not give even to their children; then the mendicants swoop down, like the honey-thief [madhuhā; footnote: a man who steals honey].

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: दुःख सो(ऽ)सून पाक करिती। पोराबाळांलाही न देती। तंव भिक्षू घाला घालिती। मधुहा जेवीं

statements.statement: The bees, with great toil, wandering in many forests, gathering whatever they get, store up honey.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ज्या महत्तर कष्ट करून। नाना वनीं फिरून। मिळेल तसें संपादून। माश्या सांठवून ठेविती मधु

statements.statement: The bees do great toil and with effort make the honey sweet; they themselves eat not a drop, nor do they give to their young.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: माश्या महत्तर कष्ट करिती। यत्नें मधु मिष्ट करिती। स्वयें बिंदुमात्र न खाती। न देती पोरांलाही

statements.statement: The honey-thief, greatly astonished, goes there with effort, strikes before they have eaten, and takes it away.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सुविस्मित मधुहा होऊन। यत्नें तेथें जाऊन। त्यांच्या खाण्यापूर्वी घाला घालून। तें घेवून जातसें

statements.statement: O king, see: this comes suddenly, without effort; taking this instruction, one should eat happily.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: पार्थिवा पाहें हें उद्योगावांचून। अकस्मात् ये मिळून। हें शिक्षण घेऊन । सुखें जेवून असावें

statements.statement: This device is good, know; who would tend the hearth and the cooking-square, ruin his eyes with the smoke and burn his hands?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हीच युक्ती बरी जाण। चूल चौका करी कोण। धूमानें डोळे फोडून। हात भाजून कोण घेई

statements.statement: Only food already cooked: bring it by begging, eat it without trouble, and digest it by meditation.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: आहारमात्र सिद्धान्न। भिक्षा मागून आणून। अनायासें खाऊन। ध्यान करून जिरवावें

statements.statement: He who, having eaten excess food, does not meditate and stays bloated, will certainly meet a fall.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: खाऊनि जो विशेष अन्न। ध्यानादिक न करून। राहे बोकळून। त्याला पतन येईल खास

statements.statement: The householder's five great sins go from him when he gives alms; if guests are turned away from him, his loss will be great.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: पंच महापापें गृहस्थाचीं। भिक्षा देतां तीं जाती त्याचीं। अतिथी फिरविती तयाची। हानी मोठी होईल

statements.statement: If vaiśvadeva has not been done in the house and a celibate student or an ascetic comes, giving him food brings the fruit of sacrifice; turning him away requires the cāndrāyaṇa expiation.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: घरांत वैश्वदेव न होतां। ब्रह्मचारी यती येतां। यज्ञफळ ये त्याला अन्न देतां। त्या फिरवितां चांद्रायण प्रायश्चित्त

statements.statement: A saintly person dwelling in the forest in the renounced order of life should never listen to songs or music promoting material enjoyment. Rather, a saintly person should carefully study the example of the deer, who is bewildered by the sweet music of the hunter’s horn and is thus captured and killed.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
ग्राम्यगीतं न श‍ृणुयाद् यतिर्वनचर: क्व‍‍चित् ।
शिक्षेत हरिणाद् बद्धान्मृगयोर्गीतमोहितात् ॥ १७ ॥
original.transliteration:
grāmya-gītaṁ na śṛṇuyād
yatir vana-caraḥ kvacit
śikṣeta hariṇād baddhān
mṛgayor gīta-mohitāt
original.word_for_word: grāmya — relating to sense gratification; gītam — songs; na — not; śṛṇuyāt — he should hear; yatiḥ — a saintly mendicant; vana — in the forest; caraḥ — moving; kvacit — ever; śikṣeta — one should learn; hariṇāt — from the deer; baddhāt — bound up; mṛgayoḥ — of the hunter; gīta — by the song; mohitāt — bewildered.

statements.statement: If one becomes attached to the sense gratification of materialistic music and songs, one will develop all the features of material entanglement. One should hear Bhagavad-gītā, or the song sung by the Supreme Lord.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Becoming attracted to the worldly singing, dancing and musical entertainment of beautiful women, even the great sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, the son of a deer, fell totally under their control, just like a pet animal.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
नृत्यवादित्रगीतानि जुषन् ग्राम्याणि योषिताम् ।
आसां क्रीडनको वश्य ऋष्यश‍ृङ्गो मृगीसुत: ॥ १८ ॥
original.transliteration:
nṛtya-vāditra-gītāni
juṣan grāmyāṇi yoṣitām
āsāṁ krīḍanako vaśya
ṛṣyaśṛṅgo mṛgī-sutaḥ
original.word_for_word: nṛtya — dancing; vāditra — musical performance; gītāni — songs; juṣan — cultivating; grāmyāni — related to sense gratification; yoṣitām — of women; āsām — of them; krīḍanakaḥ — a plaything; vaśyaḥ — fully controlled; ṛṣya-śṛṅgaḥ — the sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga; mṛgī-sutaḥ — the son of a deer.

statements.statement: Ṛṣyaśṛṅga was intentionally brought up by his father in an atmosphere of complete innocence. The father thought that if his son were never exposed to the sight of women he would always remain a perfect brahmacārī. But by chance the inhabitants of the neighboring kingdom, who were suffering from a long-term drought, received divine advice that rain would return to their kingdom only after the brāhmaṇa named Ṛṣyaśṛṅga stepped foot in it. Therefore they sent beautiful women to Ṛṣyaśṛṅga’s hermitage to entice him and bring him back with them. Since Ṛṣyaśṛṅga had never even heard about women, he easily fell for their trap.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The name Ṛṣyaśṛṅga indicates that the young sage was born with a deerlike horn growing out of his forehead. If like the deer a ṛṣi becomes attracted to sweet musical sounds promising sense gratification, then like the deer he is quickly vanquished. A thoughtful person should humbly take instruction from the deer, who is doomed by attraction to musical sense gratification.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Whoever truly listens to the talk of village people or the songs of village women gets bound, surely.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ग्राम्यजनवार्ता । कां ग्राम्य स्त्रियांच्या गीता । ऐके जो कां तत्त्वतां । बंधन सर्वथा तो पावे

statements.statement: Looking steadily toward the lamp, maddened by the sound of the bell, the deer forgot to look ahead and falls into the snare completely.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अखंड पाहतां दीपाकडे । घंटानादें झालें वेडें । मृग पाहों विसरला पुढें । फांसीं पडे सर्वथा

statements.statement: He who is called the crown of ascetics, who had no meeting or talk with women - that Ṛṣyaśṛṅga was at once deluded for the sake of women's songs.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जो बोलिजे तापसांचा मुकुटी । ज्यासी स्त्रियांसी नाहीं भेट गोष्टी । तो ऋष्यश्रृंग उठा‌उठी । स्त्रीगीतासाठीं भुलला

statements.statement: That Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, at the sight of the women, at once became subject to them; he ran after the women; he acted according to their talk.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तो ऋष्यश्रृंग स्त्रीदृष्टीं । वश्य जाहला उठा‌उठी । धांवे योषितांचे पाठोवाठीं । त्यांचे गोष्टीमाजी वर्ते

statements.statement: He forgot the labour of austerity; he forgot his father Vibhāṇḍaka; he forgot the resolve of celibacy he had made; he danced to the women's tune.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: विसरला तपाचा खटाटोपु । विसरला विभांडक बापु । विसरला ब्रह्मचर्यकृत संकल्पु । स्त्रियानुरूपु नाचतु

statements.statement: Village songs are forbidden and are not to be listened to - this is true, wholly true; but where there are Hari-kīrtana and kathā, those should be heard, for paramārtha.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: वारिलें ना‌इकावें ग्राम्य गीता । हे सत्य सत्य गा सर्वथा । तेथ हरिकीर्तन कथा । जाहल्या परमार्थतां ऐकावें

statements.statement: What is spoken in the village without the name of Rāma is called 'grāmya-gīta' (village song); that should surely not be listened to; one should not go there out of curiosity.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: रामनामें विवर्जित । ग्रामणीं बोलिजे तें ’ग्राम्यगीत’ । तें ना‌इकावें निश्चित । कवतुकें तेथ न वचावें

statements.statement: Swift and straight they run, their speed like the wind's; the deer that cannot be caught by hand are bound by the sound of song.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: त्वरें थेट सारखे धांवती। वायूपरी ज्यांची गती। जे मृग हातीं न लागती। ते बद्ध होती गीतशब्दें

statements.statement: This great enchantment pierces the mind; it binds the deer without taking even a moment.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हें उदंड मोहन। जाई चित्त वेधून। जें टाकी मृगां बांधून। एक क्षण न लागतांची

statements.statement: Skilled singers go into the forest, play the vīṇā and the sārangī, take various ālāps, and keep singing sweet-voiced.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: वनीं भले गवयी जाऊन। वीणा सारंगी वाजवून। नाना आलाप घेऊन। सुस्वर गाऊन राहती

statements.statement: Hearing that suddenly, the deer, enticed by the song and forgetting everything, all fall upon it.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: अकस्मांत तें ऐकून। त्या गीता लुब्ध होऊन। मृग सर्व विसरून। पडती येऊन त्यावरी सारे

statements.statement: When the deer become absorbed in the sound of the stringed instrument, the hunter [footnote: pāradhī] binds them. From that I took the instruction to give up [the lure of] sound.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मृग तंत्रीस्वरीं होतां लीन। मृगयूत्यांचे करी बंधन। त्यापासून घेतलें शिक्षण। नाद सोडून द्यावया

statements.statement: The sound of song seems sweet; hearing a tender, sweet voice, it pierces the heart; it is a firmer bond.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: गीत शब्द वाटे मधुर। ऐकतां कोमळ सुस्वर। तो वेधीतसे अंतर। हें दृढतर बंधन जो

statements.statement: Women who sing sweetly and take ālāps like the cuckoo: on hearing it, the mind becomes very much enchanted.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ज्या नारी सुस्वर गाती। कोकिळेपरी आलाप घेती। ऐकतांच तें चित्तीं। लागे अति मोहकसें

statements.statement: Those who sing, showing various moods, keeping beat and tempo, making rāgas and rāgiṇīs shine, what they sing should be heard from afar.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नाना रंग दावून। तालकाल साधून। रागरागिणी उजळून। गाती तें दुरून ऐकावें

statements.statement: Where they sing the Sāma [chant] with Oṃkāra first, with devotion, or where the devout sing in praise of the Lord's qualities [continued in the next ovi],

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जेथें ॐकारपूर्वक। साम गाती भक्तिपूर्वक। किंवा गाती भाविक। ईश्वरगुणानुवाद

statements.statement: know that [other singing] to be wailing, though it be sweet-voiced singing, which is without the Lord's qualities; or a jackal's howl.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तें आक्रन्दन जाण। हो कां सुस्वर गायन। जे भगवद्गुणाविण। किंवा कोल्ह्याची ओरड

statements.statement: As the sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, who was born of a doe, was deluded on seeing the dances and the like of women and became bound.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जसा तो ऋष्यश्रृंगमुनी। जो झाला मृगीपासूनी। स्त्रियांचें नृत्यादिक पाहूनी। भुलुनी बद्ध जाहला

statements.statement: So one should not even remember village songs: this is the fifteenth guru's [teaching]. Now I tell of the sixteenth, measured and true.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तेव्हां स्मरणसुद्धां ग्राम्यगीतांचें। न कीजे हें पंध्राव्या गुरूचें। सांगणें आतां सोळाव्याचें। मित साचें सांगतो

statements.statement: Just as a fish, incited by the desire to enjoy his tongue, is fatally trapped on the fisherman’s hook, similarly, a foolish person is bewildered by the extremely disturbing urges of the tongue and thus is ruined.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
जिह्वयातिप्रमाथिन्या जनो रसविमोहित: ।
मृत्युमृच्छत्यसद्बुद्धिर्मीनस्तु बडिशैर्यथा ॥ १९ ॥
original.transliteration:
jihvayāti-pramāthinyā
jano rasa-vimohitaḥ
mṛtyum ṛcchaty asad-buddhir
mīnas tu baḍiśair yathā
original.word_for_word: jihvayā — by the tongue; ati-pramāthinyā — which is extremely disturbing; janaḥ — a person; rasa-vimohitaḥ — bewildered by attraction to taste; mṛtyum — death; ṛcchati — achieves; asat — useless; buddhiḥ — whose intelligence; mīnaḥ — the fish; tu — indeed; baḍiśaiḥ — by the hooks; yathā — just as.

statements.statement: The fisherman places meaty bait on a sharp hook and easily attracts the unintelligent fish, who is greedy to enjoy its tongue. Similarly, people are mad after gratifying their tongues and lose all discrimination in their eating habits. For momentary gratification they construct huge slaughterhouses and kill millions of innocent creatures, and by inflicting such atrocious suffering they prepare a ghastly future for themselves. But even if one eats only the foods authorized in the Vedas, there is still danger. One may eat too sumptuously and then the artificially stuffed belly will create pressure on the sexual organs. Thus one will fall down into the lower modes of nature and commit sinful activities that lead to the death of one’s spiritual life. From the fish one should carefully learn the real dangers involved in gratifying the tongue.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: By fasting, learned men quickly bring all of the senses except the tongue under control, because by abstaining from eating such men are afflicted with an increased desire to gratify the sense of taste.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
इन्द्रियाणि जयन्त्याशु निराहारा मनीषिण: ।
वर्जयित्वा तु रसनं तन्निरन्नस्य वर्धते ॥ २० ॥
original.transliteration:
indriyāṇi jayanty āśu
nirāhārā manīṣiṇaḥ
varjayitvā tu rasanaṁ
tan nirannasya vardhate
original.word_for_word: indriyāṇi — the material senses; jayanti — they conquer; āśu — quickly; nirāhārāḥ — those who restrain the senses from their objects; manīṣiṇaḥ — the learned; varjayitvā — except for; tu — however; rasanam — the tongue; tat — its desire; nirannasya — for one who is fasting; vardhate — increases.

statements.statement: In South America there is a saying that when the belly is full the heart is content. Thus, one who is eating sumptuously is jolly, and if one is deprived of proper food one’s appetite becomes even more voracious. An intelligent person, however, does not fall under the control of the tongue, but rather tries to make progress in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. By accepting the remnants of food offered to the Lord (prasādam), one gradually purifies the heart and automatically becomes simple and austere.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: In this connection, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura states that the business of the tongue is to gratify itself with the varieties of flavor, but by wandering in the twelve holy forests of Vraja-maṇḍala (Vṛndāvana), one can be freed from the twelve flavors of material sense gratification. The five principal divisions of material relationships are neutral admiration, servitude, friendship, parental affection and conjugal love; the seven subordinate features of material relationships are material humor, astonishment, chivalry, compassion, anger, dread and ghastliness. Originally, these twelve rasas, or flavors of relationships, are exchanged between the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the living entity in the spiritual world; and by wandering in the twelve forests of Vṛndāvana one can respiritualize the twelve flavors of personal existence. Thus one will become a liberated soul, free from all material desires. If one artificially tries to give up sense gratification, especially that of the tongue, the attempt will be a failure, and in fact one’s desire for sense gratification will increase as a result of artificial deprivation. Only by experiencing real, spiritual pleasure in relationship with Kṛṣṇa can one give up material desires.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Although one may conquer all of the other senses, as long as the tongue is not conquered it cannot be said that one has controlled his senses. However, if one is able to control the tongue, then one is understood to be in full control of all the senses.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
तावज्जितेन्द्रियो न स्याद् विजितान्येन्द्रिय: पुमान् ।
न जयेद् रसनं यावज्जितं सर्वं जिते रसे ॥ २१ ॥
original.transliteration:
tāvaj jitendriyo na syād
vijitānyendriyaḥ pumān
na jayed rasanaṁ yāvaj
jitaṁ sarvaṁ jite rase
original.word_for_word: tāvat — still; jita-indriyaḥ — one who has conquered the senses; na — not; syāt — can be; vijita-anya-indriyaḥ — one who has conquered all of the other senses; pumān — a human being; na jayet — cannot conquer; rasanam — the tongue; yāvat — as long as; jitam — conquered; sarvam — everything; jite — when conquered; rase — the tongue.

statements.statement: By eating, one gives energy and activity to all of the senses, and thus if the tongue is uncontrolled all of the senses will be dragged down to the material platform of existence. Therefore, by all means one must control the tongue. If one fasts, then all of the other senses become weak and lose their potency. The tongue, however, becomes more greedy to taste delicious preparations, and when one finally indulges the tongue, all of the senses quickly go out of control. Therefore, Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura advises that one accept mahā-prasādam, or the remnants of the Lord’s food, in a moderate proportion. Since the tongue’s function is also to vibrate, one should vibrate the glorious holy name of the Supreme Lord and taste the ecstasy of pure Kṛṣṇa consciousness. As stated in Bhagavad-gītā, rasa-varjaṁ raso ’py asya paraṁ dṛṣṭvā nivartate: only by the higher taste of Kṛṣṇa consciousness can one give up the deadly lower taste that keeps one imprisoned in material bondage.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura states that as long as one’s intelligence is materially covered, one cannot understand the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Trying to enjoy without Kṛṣṇa, the living entity leaves the abode of the Supreme Lord, called Vrajabhūmi, and comes down into the material world, where he quickly loses control of his senses. One becomes particularly victimized by the tongue, belly and genitals, which exert intolerable pressure on the conditioned soul. These desires subside, however, when one reestablishes one’s blissful relationship with the Lord, who is actually the reservoir of all pleasure. One who is attached to the taste of Kṛṣṇa consciousness automatically follows all of the rules and regulations of religious life due to spontaneous attraction to viśuddha-sattva, or the mode of pure goodness. Without such spontaneous attraction, one is certainly bewildered by the pushing of the material senses.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Even the beginning stage of devotional service, called sādhana-bhakti (regulatory practice), is so powerful that it brings one to the platform of anartha-nivṛtti, where one becomes free from unwanted sinful habits and gains relief from the pressure of the tongue, belly and genitals. Thus one is delivered from the bondage of material addiction and can no longer be cheated by the allurements of the material energy. As it is said, all that glitters is not gold. In this regard Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura recommends that we consider the following song written by his father, Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura:

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement:
śarīra avidyā-jāl, jaḍendriya tāhe kāl,
jīve phele viṣaya-sāgare
tā’ra madhye jihvā ati, lobhamay sudurmati,
tā’ke jetā kaṭhina saṁsāre

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement:
kṛṣṇa baḍa dayāmay, karibāre jihvā jay,
sva-prasādānna dila bhāi
sei annāmṛta pāo, rādhā-kṛṣṇa-guṇa gāo,
preme ḍāko caitanya-nitāi

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: “O Lord, this material body is a lump of ignorance, and the senses are a network of paths to death. Somehow, we have fallen into this ocean of material sense enjoyment, and of all the senses the tongue is most voracious and uncontrollable; it is very difficult to conquer the tongue in this world. But You, dear Kṛṣṇa, are very kind to us and have given us such nice prasādam, just to control the tongue. Now we take this prasādam to our full satisfaction and glorify Their Lordships Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and in love call for the help of Lord Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda.”

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: To make the 'fish' a guru - hear those marks too: through greed of the tongue he goes, with life and breath.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ’मीन’ गुरु करणें । तेंही अवधारा लक्षणें । रसनेचेनि लोलुप्यपणें । जीवेंप्राणे जातसे

statements.statement: Through hoarding wealth, killing of life; through attachment to women, downfall; through greed of the tongue, death; various destructions for the soul.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अर्थ-संग्रहें जीवघातु । स्त्रिया-आसक्तीं अधःपातु । रसनालोलुप्यें पावे मृत्यु । विविध घातु जीवासी

statements.statement: One who has deep greed of the tongue has calamity joined to him pair after pair; he suffers crores of sorrows; the sweetness of the tongue is harmful.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ज्यासी रसनालोलुप्यता गाढी । त्यासी अनर्थुचि जोडे जोडी । दुःखाच्या भोगवी कोडी । रसनागोडी बाधक

statements.statement: For the tongue's sweetness of the bait, in greed the fish swallows the ball; at once the hook pierces his palate; then, caught, he writhes.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: रसना आमिषाची गोडी । लोलुप्यें मीनु गिळी उंडी । सवेंचि गळु टाळू फोडी । मग चरफडी अडकलिया

statements.statement: Seen, the taste appears excellent; within, hooks of diseases are hidden; those who partake of taste with attachment writhe with the disease of worldly existence.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पाहतां रस उत्तम दिसत । भीतरीं रोगांचे गळ गुप्त । रस आसक्तीं जे सेवित । ते चडफडित भवरोगें

statements.statement: The power of the senses, grown wild, carries one and throws him into a downfall; if the tongue is not conquered at all, the pain of worldly existence is not avoided.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मातली जे इंद्रियसत्ता । ते ने‌ऊन घाली अधःपाता । रसना न जिणतां सर्वथा । भवव्यथा चुकेना

statements.statement: That the senses have been conquered by going without food - this is a false saying; as soon as food is taken they spring up, alert to their own functions.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: निरन्नें इंद्रियें जिंतली । तीं जिंतलीं हे मिथ्या बोली । अन्न घेतांचि सरसावलीं । सावध जाहलीं निजकर्मी

statements.statement: As long as the tongue has not been conquered, 'jitendriya' is a false word; when the tongue is truly conquered, then the road of the objects is broken.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जंव रसना नाहीं जिंकिली । तंव ’जितेंद्रिय’ मिथ्या बोली । जैं साचार रसना जिंकली । तैं वाट मोडिली विषयांची

statements.statement: There is the Sweet of all sweetnesses; he who stays attached to that sweetness - to him alone the tongue becomes subject; the harms of taste do not afflict him.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सर्वां गोडियांचें गोड आहे । ते गोडीस जो लागला राहे । त्यासीचि रसना वश्य होये । रस-अपाये न बाधिती

statements.statement: The felicitation of one who has conquered the tongue: by it his station is fixed in union with Brahman; he enjoys the festival in supreme bliss - he by whom the tongue has been conquered.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: रसनाजिताचें वाधावणें । तेणें ब्रह्मसायुज्यीं पडे ठाणें । सोहळा परमानंदे भोगणें । रसना जेणें जिंतिली

statements.statement: He whose speed is swift, who runs in the water, who cannot be caught by hand, is bound by the tongue.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सत्वर गति जया असे। जो जळीं धांवतसे। धरितां हाता न येतसे। तो बद्ध होतसे जिव्हेमुळे

statements.statement: Always living in water, he cannot rein in the tongue; therefore they catch that fish, casting a hook [footnote: gaḷa] with flesh on it.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नित्य कृतजळवास। जिव्हा नावरी त्यामुळें खास। धरिती त्या मत्स्यास। सोडूनी बडिश मांसयुक्त

statements.statement: Do not hope for happiness so long as the craving for taste has not left; the fish gives this instruction: give up the craving for taste.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नको तंववरी सुखाशा। जंव न सुटली रसाशा। मासा अशा उपदेशा। देतसे रसाशा टाकावया

statements.statement: When one remembers tastes in the mind, the tongue waters; then who can restrain that man once he takes in the fragrance?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मनीं स्मरतां रसांला। लाळ सुटे जिव्हेला। मग घेतां सुवासाला। त्या नराला कोण आवरी

statements.statement: Those who cannot rein in this tongue wander from country to country and sell cattle, houses and children to satisfy the tongue.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जे ही रसना नावरती। ते देशोदेशी भटकती। गुरें घरें पोरें विकिती। रसनातृप्ती करावया

statements.statement: Those who do great deeds of valour, who conquer even enemies, even they cannot restrain that tongue, which is so enticing [huḷakī; footnote: 'one that holds out a lure'].

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: पराक्रम थोर करिती। जे शत्रूंलाही जिंकिती। तयांलाही नावरे ती। रसना बरी हुळकी जी

statements.statement: Even a thoughtful man who defeats the circle of śāstrīs in the assembly: to him too the tongue is utterly hard to conquer.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जरी तो विचारशीळ। सभेंत जिंकी शास्त्रीमंडळ। तयालाही जिव्हा केवळ। निखळ दुर्जेय हो

statements.statement: This astonishes us: you have a tongue four fingers long; why can you not rein it in? Reflect and tell us the reason.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हा विस्मय वाटे आम्हां। चार आंगुळे जिव्हा तुम्हां। कां नावरे हे आम्हां। कारणा सांगा विचारूनी

statements.statement: Do this now: reduce taste little by little; practise the way of the life-breath [eating only to sustain life]; then you will conquer that tongue.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: असें कृत्य आतां करा। थोडा थोडा रस कमी करा। प्राणवृत्ती परी आचरा। जिंकाल मग रसना ती

statements.statement: You will not be master of the senses until you conquer the tongue; if you conquer taste you will conquer all: 'jitaṃ sarvaṃ jite rase' [all is conquered when taste is conquered].

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तुम्ही तंववरी जितेंद्रिय न व्हाल। जंवर रसना न जिंकाल। रस जिंकतां सर्व जिंकाल। जितं सर्व जिते रसे

statements.statement: Keeping this in memory, conquering taste step by step, victorious everywhere, I remain lying here in happiness.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हेंची स्मरण ठेवून। अनुक्रमें रस जिंकून। सर्वत्र विजयी होऊन। येथें पडून राहिलों सुखें

statements.statement: This is the instruction for restraining the tongue that I truly received from the sixteenth guru; the power of taste should be warded off.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: असें रसना आवरण्याचें। हें सोळाव्या गुरुचें। शिक्षण लाधलें साचें। रसाचें प्राबल्य निवारिजे

statements.statement: O son of kings, previously in the city of Videha there dwelled a prostitute named Piṅgalā. Now please hear what I have learned from that lady.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
पिङ्गला नाम वेश्यासीद् विदेहनगरे पुरा ।
तस्या मे शिक्षितं किञ्चिन्निबोध नृपनन्दन ॥ २२ ॥
original.transliteration:
piṅgalā nāma veśyāsīd
videha-nagare purā
tasyā me śikṣitaṁ kiñcin
nibodha nṛpa-nandana
original.word_for_word: piṅgalā nāma — of the name Piṅgalā; veśyā — a prostitute; āsīt — there was; videha-nagare — in the city named Videha; purā — in the past; tasyāḥ — from her; me — by me; śikṣitaṁ — what was learned; kiñcit — something; nibodha — now you learn; nṛpa-nandana — O son of kings.

statements.statement: Once that prostitute, desiring to bring a lover into her house, stood outside in the doorway at night showing her beautiful form.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
सा स्वैरिण्येकदा कान्तं सङ्केत उपनेष्यती ।
अभूत् काले बहिर्द्वारे बिभ्रती रूपमुत्तमम् ॥ २३ ॥
original.transliteration:
sā svairiṇy ekadā kāntaṁ
saṅketa upaneṣyatī
abhūt kāle bahir dvāre
bibhratī rūpam uttamam
original.word_for_word: sā — she; svairiṇī — the prostitute; ekadā — once; kāntam — a paying lover or a customer; saṅkete — into her house of sex; upaneṣyatī — to bring; abhūt — she stood; kāle — at night; bahiḥ — outside; dvāre — in the doorway; bibhratī — holding up; rūpam — her form; uttamam — most beautiful.

statements.statement: O best among men, this prostitute was very anxious to get money, and as she stood on the street at night she studied all the men who were passing by, thinking, “Oh, this one surely has money. I know he can pay the price, and I am sure he would enjoy my company very much.” Thus she thought about all the men on the street.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
मार्ग आगच्छतो वीक्ष्य पुरुषान् पुरुषर्षभ ।
तान् शुल्कदान् वित्तवत: कान्तान् मेनेऽर्थकामुकी ॥ २४ ॥
original.transliteration:
mārga āgacchato vīkṣya
puruṣān puruṣarṣabha
tān śulka-dān vittavataḥ
kāntān mene ’rtha-kāmukī
original.word_for_word: mārge — in that street; āgacchataḥ — those who were coming; vīkṣya — seeing; puruṣān — men; puruṣa-ṛṣabha — O best among men; tān — them; śulka-dān — who could pay the price; vitta-vataḥ — possessing money; kāntān — lovers or customers; mene — she considered; artha-kāmukī — desiring money.

statements.statement: As the prostitute Piṅgalā stood in the doorway, many men came and went, walking by her house. Her only means of sustenance was prostitution, and therefore she anxiously thought, “Maybe this one who is coming now is very rich… Oh, he is not stopping, but I am sure someone else will come. Surely this man who is coming now will want to pay me for my love, and he will probably give lots of money.” Thus, with vain hope, she remained leaning against the doorway, unable to finish her business and go to sleep. Out of anxiety she would sometimes walk out toward the street, and sometimes she went back into her house. In this way, the midnight hour gradually arrived.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
आगतेष्वपयातेषु सा सङ्केतोपजीविनी ।
अप्यन्यो वित्तवान् कोऽपि मामुपैष्यति भूरिद: ॥ २५ ॥
एवं दुराशया ध्वस्तनिद्रा द्वार्यवलम्बती ।
निर्गच्छन्ती प्रविशती निशीथं समपद्यत ॥ २६ ॥
original.transliteration:
āgateṣv apayāteṣu
sā saṅketopajīvinī
apy anyo vittavān ko ’pi
mām upaiṣyati bhūri-daḥ

evaṁ durāśayā dhvasta-
nidrā dvāry avalambatī
nirgacchantī praviśatī
niśīthaṁ samapadyata
original.word_for_word: āgateṣu — when they came; apayāteṣu — and they went; sā — she; saṅketa-upajīvinī — she whose only income was from prostitution; api — maybe; anyaḥ — another one; vitta-vān — who has money; kaḥ api — someone; mām — me; upaiṣyati — will approach for love; bhūri-daḥ — and he will give lots of money; evam — thus; durāśayā — with vain hope; dhvasta — spoiled; nidrā — her sleep; dvāri — in the doorway; avalambatī — hanging on; nirgacchantī — going out toward the street; praviśatī — going back into her house; niśītham — midnight; samapadyata — arrived.

statements.statement: As the night wore on, the prostitute, who intensely desired money, gradually became morose, and her face dried up. Thus being filled with anxiety for money and most disappointed, she began to feel a great detachment from her situation, and happiness arose in her mind.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
तस्या वित्ताशया शुष्यद्वक्त्राया दीनचेतस: ।
निर्वेद: परमो जज्ञे चिन्ताहेतु: सुखावह: ॥ २७ ॥
original.transliteration:
tasyā vittāśayā śuṣyad-
vaktrāyā dīna-cetasaḥ
nirvedaḥ paramo jajñe
cintā-hetuḥ sukhāvahaḥ
original.word_for_word: tasyāḥ — of her; vitta — for money; āśayā — by the desire; śuṣyat — dried up; vaktrāyāḥ — her face; dīna — morose; cetasaḥ — her mind; nirvedaḥ — detachment; paramaḥ — very great; jajñe — awakened; cintā — anxiety; hetuḥ — because of; sukha — happiness; āvahaḥ — bringing.

statements.statement: It appears from these verses that on this particular night the prostitute Piṅgalā was not at all successful in attracting customers to her house. Being completely frustrated and disappointed, she gradually became indifferent to her situation. Thus, great suffering sometimes leads one to the path of enlightenment; or, according to a Sanskrit proverb, disappointment gives rise to the greatest satisfaction.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The prostitute had dedicated her life to satisfying the lusty desires of many men. Engaging her mind, body and words in the service of paying lovers, she completely forgot the devotional service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and thus her mind was most unsteady and disturbed. Finally, being completely frustrated, her face and throat drying up, she began to feel indifferent to her situation, and happiness arose in her mind.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The prostitute felt disgusted with her material situation and thus became indifferent to it. Indeed, detachment acts like a sword, cutting to pieces the binding network of material hopes and desires. Now please hear from me the song sung by the prostitute in that situation.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
तस्या निर्विण्णचित्ताया गीतं श‍ृणु यथा मम ।
निर्वेद आशापाशानां पुरुषस्य यथा ह्यसि: ॥ २८ ॥
original.transliteration:
tasyā nirviṇṇa-cittāyā
gītaṁ śṛṇu yathā mama
nirveda āśā-pāśānāṁ
puruṣasya yathā hy asiḥ
original.word_for_word: tasyāḥ — of her; nirviṇṇa — disgusted; cittāyāḥ — whose mind; gītam — song; śṛṇu — please hear; yathā — as it is; mama — from me; nirvedaḥ — detachment; āśā — of hopes and yearnings; pāśānām — of the binding network; puruṣasya — of a person; yathā — just as; hi — certainly; asiḥ — the sword.

statements.statement: The network of material desires is created when one falsely thinks that he can establish himself permanently in the material world. This binding network should be cut by the sword of detachment; otherwise one will be forced to wander in the illusory network of māyā with no understanding of liberated life on the spiritual platform.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: O King, just as a human being who is bereft of spiritual knowledge never desires to give up his false sense of proprietorship over many material things, similarly, a person who has not developed detachment never desires to give up the bondage of the material body.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
न ह्यङ्गाजातनिर्वेदो देहबन्धं जिहासति ।
यथा विज्ञानरहितो मनुजो ममतां नृप ॥ २९ ॥
original.transliteration:
na hy aṅgājāta-nirvedo
deha-bandhaṁ jihāsati
yathā vijñāna-rahito
manujo mamatāṁ nṛpa
original.word_for_word: na — does not; hi — certainly; aṅga — O King; ajāta — who has not developed; nirvedaḥ — detachment; deha — of the material body; bandham — bondage; jihāsati — he desires to give up; yathā — just as; vijñāna — realized knowledge; rahitaḥ — bereft of; manujaḥ — a human being; mamatām — false sense of proprietorship; nṛpa — O King.

statements.statement: The prostitute Piṅgalā said: Just see how greatly illusioned I am! Because I cannot control my mind, just like a fool I desire lusty pleasure from an insignificant man.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
पिङ्गलोवाच
अहो मे मोहविततिं पश्यताविजितात्मन: ।
या कान्तादसत: कामं कामये येन बालिशा ॥ ३० ॥
original.transliteration:
piṅgalovāca
aho me moha-vitatiṁ
paśyatāvijitātmanaḥ
yā kāntād asataḥ kāmaṁ
kāmaye yena bāliśā
original.word_for_word: piṅgalā — Piṅgalā; uvāca — said; aho — oh; me — my; moha — of illusion; vitatim — expansion; paśyata — just see, everyone; avijita-ātmanaḥ — of one whose mind is not controlled; yā — which person (me); kāntāt — from a lover; asataḥ — useless, insignificant; kāmam — lusty pleasure; kāmaye — I desire; yena — because; bāliśā — I am a fool.

statements.statement: In material existence all of the senses are attracted by different objects, and thus the conditioned soul becomes a first-class fool. The cause of material life is one’s indifference to the Absolute Truth. The conditioned soul considers himself to be the lord and enjoyer of the material world and considers the purpose of life to be sense gratification. The more one tries to enjoy the material world, the more one’s illusion increases.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: It appears from this verse that the prostitute Piṅgalā was not only earning her livelihood through prostitution, but was actually enjoying her illicit contact with innumerable men. The words kāntād asataḥ indicate that she was freely selling herself without discrimination to the most ordinary and useless men, considering them to be “lovers.” Thus she says, “I was a great fool.” The word bāliśā means “one who has a childish mentality, without practical experience of right and wrong.”

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: I am such a fool that I have given up the service of that person who, being eternally situated within my heart, is actually most dear to me. That most dear one is the Lord of the universe, who is the bestower of real love and happiness and the source of all prosperity. Although He is in my own heart, I have completely neglected Him. Instead I have ignorantly served insignificant men who can never satisfy my real desires and who have simply brought me unhappiness, fear, anxiety, lamentation and illusion.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
सन्तं समीपे रमणं रतिप्रदं
वित्तप्रदं नित्यमिमं विहाय ।
अकामदं दु:खभयाधिशोक-
मोहप्रदं तुच्छमहं भजेऽज्ञा ॥ ३१ ॥
original.transliteration:
santaṁ samīpe ramaṇaṁ rati-pradaṁ
vitta-pradaṁ nityam imaṁ vihāya
akāma-daṁ duḥkha-bhayādhi-śoka-
moha-pradaṁ tuccham ahaṁ bhaje ’jñā
original.word_for_word: santam — being; samīpe — most near (in my heart); ramaṇam — the most dear; rati — actual love or pleasure; pradam — giving; vitta — prosperity; pradam — giving; nityam — eternal; imam — Him; vihāya — giving up; akāma-dam — who can never satisfy one’s desires; duḥkha — misery; bhaya — fear; ādhi — mental distress; śoka — lamentation; moha — illusion; pradam — giving; tuccham — most insignificant; aham — I; bhaje — serve; ajñā — an ignorant fool.

statements.statement: Piṅgalā laments that she chose to serve most sinful, useless men. She falsely thought they would bring her happiness and neglected to serve the actual Lord of the heart, Kṛṣṇa. She could understand how foolishly she had struggled for money, not knowing that the Supreme Lord is always inclined to award prosperity to His sincere devotee. The prostitute was proud of her ability to please men, but she now laments that she did not try to please the Supreme Lord by loving service. The Supreme Lord is completely aloof from the transactions of the material world. Lord Kṛṣṇa is the actual enjoyer of everyone and everything, but one must learn how to please the Lord by pure spiritual service.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Oh, how I have uselessly tortured my own soul! I have sold my body to lusty, greedy men who are themselves objects of pity. Thus practicing the most abominable profession of a prostitute, I hoped to get money and sex pleasure.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:

स्त्रैणान्नराद् यार्थतृषोऽनुशोच्यात्
क्रीतेन वित्तं रतिमात्मनेच्छती ॥ ३२ ॥

statements.statement: The art of prostitution is based on awakening the enjoying propensity in men. Apparently this prostitute was so foolish that she maintained a romantic conception of her profession and was actually trying to enjoy loving affairs with her customers, not realizing that they were the lowest of men with the most abominable motives. Like the prostitute Piṅgalā, one should understand that by giving up the devotional service of the Lord one simply becomes a victim of the illusory energy and suffers greatly.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: This material body is like a house in which I, the soul, am living. The bones forming my spine, ribs, arms and legs are like the beams, crossbeams and pillars of the house, and the whole structure, which is full of stool and urine, is covered by skin, hair and nails. The nine doors leading into this body are constantly excreting foul substances. Besides me, what woman could be so foolish as to devote herself to this material body, thinking that she might find pleasure and love in this contraption?

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:

क्षरन्नवद्वारमगारमेतद्
विण्मूत्रपूर्णं मदुपैति कान्या ॥ ३३ ॥
original.transliteration:
yad asthibhir nirmita-vaṁśa-vaṁsya-
sthūṇaṁ tvacā roma-nakhaiḥ pinaddham
kṣaran-nava-dvāram agāram etad

original.word_for_word: yat — which; asthibhiḥ — with bones; nirmita — constructed; vaṁśa — the spine; vaṁśya — the ribs; sthūṇam — the bones in the hands and legs; tvacā — by skin; roma-nakhaiḥ — by hair and nails; pinaddham — covered; kṣarat — oozing; nava — nine; dvāram — doors; agāram — house; etat — this; viṭ — stool; mūtra — urine; pūrṇam — full of; mat — besides me; upaiti — devotes oneself to; kā — what woman; anyā — other.

statements.statement: The nine doors leading into and out of the body are the two eyes, the two nostrils, the mouth, the two ears, the genitals and the anus. Vaṁśa, or “spine,” also means “bamboo,” and indeed the skeleton appears to resemble a bamboo construction. Just as bamboo can be immediately burned to ashes or chopped into pieces, similarly, the material body, which is constantly deteriorating, may at any moment be crushed into powder, cut into pieces, drowned, burned, suffocated, and so on. Eventually the body must disintegrate, and therefore there is certainly no one as unfortunate as one who has dedicated himself heart and soul to this flimsy body, which is filled with unpleasant elements.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Certainly in this city of Videha I alone am completely foolish. I neglected the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who awards us everything, even our original spiritual form, and instead I desired to enjoy sense gratification with many men.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
विदेहानां पुरे ह्यस्मिन्नहमेकैव मूढधी: ।
यान्यमिच्छन्त्यसत्यस्मादात्मदात् काममच्युतात् ॥ ३४ ॥
original.transliteration:

aham ekaiva mūḍha-dhīḥ
yānyam icchanty asaty asmād
ātma-dāt kāmam acyutāt

statements.statement: The Supreme Personality of Godhead is absolutely the most dear one for all living beings because He is everyone’s well-wisher and Lord. He is the Supreme Soul situated in everyone’s heart. Therefore I will now pay the price of complete surrender, and thus purchasing the Lord I will enjoy with Him just like Lakṣmīdevī.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
सुहृत् प्रेष्ठतमो नाथ आत्मा चायं शरीरिणाम् ।
तं विक्रीयात्मनैवाहं रमेऽनेन यथा रमा ॥ ३५ ॥
original.transliteration:
suhṛt preṣṭhatamo nātha

rame ’nena yathā ramā

statements.statement: The real friend of all conditioned souls is the Supreme Lord, and only He can award the highest perfection in life. By following the example of Lakṣmīdevī, who always remains at the lotus feet of the Lord, one will certainly obtain eternal happiness. One should make the best use of the material body, which is a bad bargain, and surrender one’s body, mind and words to the Lord. Paying such a price, one can purchase the Lord, who is everyone’s dearmost well-wisher. Thus one’s ancient propensity for sense gratification will automatically be controlled.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Men provide sense gratification for women, but all these men, and even the demigods in heaven, have a beginning and an end. They are all temporary creations who will be dragged away by time. Therefore how much actual pleasure or happiness could any of them ever give to their wives?

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:

आद्यन्तवन्तो भार्याया देवा वा कालविद्रुता: ॥ ३६ ॥
original.transliteration:

statements.statement: In this material world everyone is basically pursuing his personal sense gratification, and thus everyone is being ruined by the influence of time. On the material platform no one actually helps anyone else. So-called material love is simply a cheating process, as the lady Piṅgalā is now discovering.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Although I most stubbornly hoped to enjoy the material world, somehow or other detachment has arisen in my heart, and it is making me very happy. Therefore the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu, must be pleased with me. Without even knowing it, I must have performed some activity satisfying to Him.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:

statements.statement: A person who has developed detachment can give up the bondage of material society, friendship and love, and a person who undergoes great suffering gradually becomes, out of hopelessness, detached and indifferent to the material world. Thus, due to my great suffering, such detachment awoke in my heart; yet how could I have undergone such merciful suffering if I were actually unfortunate? Therefore, I am in fact fortunate and have received the mercy of the Lord. He must somehow or other be pleased with me.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: With devotion I accept the great benefit that the Lord has bestowed upon me. Having given up my sinful desires for ordinary sense gratification, I now take shelter of Him, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:

statements.statement: I am now completely satisfied, and I have full faith in the Lord’s mercy. Therefore I will maintain myself with whatever comes of its own accord. I shall enjoy life with only the Lord, because He is the real source of love and happiness.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
सन्तुष्टा श्रद्दधत्येतद्यथालाभेन जीवती ।

statements.statement: The intelligence of the living entity is stolen away by activities of sense gratification, and thus he falls into the dark well of material existence. Within that well he is then seized by the deadly serpent of time. Who else but the Supreme Personality of Godhead could save the poor living entity from such a hopeless condition?

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
संसारकूपे पतितं विषयैर्मुषितेक्षणम् ।
ग्रस्तं कालाहिनात्मानं कोऽन्यस्त्रातुमधीश्वर: ॥ ४१ ॥

statements.statement: Piṅgalā stated in a previous verse that even the demigods are unable to give actual happiness to a woman. One may question who has authorized this lady to reject even such exalted personalities as Brahmā, Śiva and the other demigods. The answer given here is that if one actually wants to solve all the problems of life and go back home, back to Godhead, then the only solution is to take shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord. It is well known that the demigods themselves are subject to birth and death. As stated by Lord Śiva himself, mukti-pradātā sarveṣāṁ viṣṇur eva na saṁśayaḥ: “There is no doubt that Viṣṇu is the deliverer of liberation for everyone.”

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: When the living entity sees that the entire universe has been seized by the serpent of time, he becomes sober and sane and at that time detaches himself from all material sense gratification. In that condition the living entity is qualified to be his own protector.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:

statements.statement: In this verse, Piṅgalā states that by the Lord’s mercy a self-realized soul can see that the entire universe is existing within the jaws of the great serpent of time. Certainly this is not a promising situation, and one who sees it loses his desire for sense gratification. Thus, by the Lord’s causeless mercy, the spiritually sane living entity can protect himself from illusion.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Since Piṅgalā is now glorifying the Personality of Godhead for His mercy in awarding salvation, the following question might arise: Is she worshiping the Lord out of love, or is she merely a salvationist desiring liberation from material existence? In answer it may be said that in her Kṛṣṇa conscious situation she is already liberated, even though remaining in this world. Her program will now be simply to render loving service to the Personality of Godhead without any personal desire, including that of salvation.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The avadhūta said: Thus, her mind completely made up, Piṅgalā cut off all her sinful desires to enjoy sex pleasure with lovers, and she became situated in perfect peace. Then she sat down on her bed.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Material desire is undoubtedly the cause of the greatest unhappiness, and freedom from such desire is the cause of the greatest happiness. Therefore, completely cutting off her desire to enjoy so-called lovers, Piṅgalā very happily went to sleep.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Formerly, in the city of Videha, a courtesan named Piṅgalā lived; for her, from hope down to hopelessness, great dispassion arose.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पूर्वी विदेहाचे नगरीं । ’पिंगला’ नामें वेश्या वासु करी । तिसी आस निरासेंवरी । वैराग्य भारी उपजलें

statements.statement: Listen, king, treasury of discernment: he in whose intellect there is no dispassion - for him the mental and bodily afflictions of birth and death are an obstacle at every step.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ऐक राया विवेकनिधी । वैराग्य नाहीं ज्याचे बुद्धीं । त्यासी जन्ममरणाची आधिव्याधी । प्रतिपदीं बाधकु

statements.statement: He who has no remorse, in whose mind discernment does not arise, is the bonded slave-woman of worldly existence, bound by the noose of hope.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अनुतापु नाहीं ज्यासी । विवेक नुपजे मानसीं । तो संसाराची आंदणी दासी । आशापाशीं बांधिजे

statements.statement: Making desire cease, see, he supplies irresistible eternal happiness; he alone is the giver to the heart; his giving is extraordinary.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: काम निवर्तवूनि देख । अनिवार पुरवी नित्यसुख । चित्तदाता तोचि एक । अलोलिक पैं देणें

statements.statement: They could not give me happiness; they became givers of sorrow alone - fear, grief, mental and bodily afflictions I received through their company.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: त्यांचेनि सुख नेदवेच मातें । परी झाले दुःखाचेचि दाते । भय-शोक-आधि-व्याधींतें । त्यांचेनि सांगातें पावलें

statements.statement: In this city of Videha, I alone am the foolish embodied one who, abandoning Śrī Hari in the heart, went astray with unholy men.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ये विदेहाचे नगरीं । मूर्ख मीचि एक देहधारी । हृदयस्थ सांडूनि श्रीहरी । असंतां नरीं व्यभिचारु

statements.statement: Those who cannot grant desires are perishable; keeping company with them gives only sorrow; how foolish was my mind, that it was attached to them.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अकामद ते नाशवंत । त्यांसी संग केलिया दुःखचि देत । कैसें माझें मूर्ख चित्त । त्यासी आसक्त पैं होतें

statements.statement: That attachment was broken off sharply; the sweetness of Acyuta's happiness took hold - the happiness which, as it is enjoyed, grows higher moment by moment.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: त्या आसक्तीची झाली तडातोडी । लागली अच्युतसुखाची गोडी । ज्याचें सुख भोगितां चढोवढी । घडियाघडी वाढतें

statements.statement: He who is my kinsman, dwelling in the heart, Acyuta, who is happiness, love and the dear one - he is the all-pervading inner Self; he is my lord and beloved.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जो सोयरा माझा हृदयस्थु । सुख प्रीति प्रिय अच्युतु । तोचि अंतरात्मा सर्वगतु । नाथ कांतु तो माझा

statements.statement: When sorrow strikes the body, dispassion does not arise in the unfortunate; how Bhagavān showed grace! Through sorrow he gave me my own happiness.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: दुःख आदळतां अंगासी । वैराग्य नुपजे अभाग्यासी । भगवंतें कृपा केली कैशी । दुःखें निजसुखासी दीधलें

statements.statement: He in whom, the moment he sees sorrow, dispassion arises along with discernment, cuts the heart-knot of affection and at once obtains his own happiness.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: दुःख देखतांचि दृष्टी । ज्यासी वैराग्य विवेकेंसी उठी । तेणें छेदूनि स्नेहहृदयगांठी । पावे उठा‌उठी निजसुख

statements.statement: For persons the supreme treasure, know, is dispassion joined with discernment; by it becoming serene, they obtain contentment.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पुरुषांसी परमनिधान । विवेकयुक्त वैराग्य जाण । तेणें हो‌ऊनियां प्रसन्न । समाधान पावती

statements.statement: Objects, which are bitter and like poison, have become sweet to the worldly man; paramārtha, which is sweet and like nectar, has become bitter to the sense-addicted.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: केवळ विषप्राय विषयो कडू । तो प्रपंचिया जाला गोडु । अमृतप्राय परमार्थ गोडु । तो जाहला कडू विषयिकां

statements.statement: Or, as the tongue does not wish for food that has been vomited, so, seeing objects, the mind holds no desire or attachment.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अथवा वमिलिया अन्ना । जेवीं वांछीना रसना । तेवीं विषय देखोनि मना । न धरी वासना आसक्ती

statements.statement: By this strength of dispassion and discernment, cutting the roots of wrong hope, she attained cessation at once; she enjoys the festival of her own Self.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: येणें वैराग्यविवेकबळें । छेदूनि दुराशेचीं मूळें । उपरमु पावली एके वेळे । निजात्मसोहळे ते भोगी

statements.statement: Dispassion cut the nooses of hope; Piṅgalā became 'nirāśa' (without hope); for the one without hope there is unmatched courage, happiness and contentment always.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: वैराग्ये छेदिले आशापाश । पिंगला जाहली गा निराश । निराशासी असमसाहस । सुखसंतोष सर्वदा

statements.statement: Where there is hope, there is greed; with hope there is wretchedness; where there is hope, there is 'mine-ness', dancing everywhere.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: आशा तेथ लोलुप्यता । आशेपाशीं असे दीनता । आशा तेथ ममता । असे सर्वथा नाचती

statements.statement: Where there is hope there is no happiness; with hope there is supreme sorrow; hope obstructs all; hope is the chief fault.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: आशा तेथ नाहीं सुख । आशेपाशीं परम दुःख । आशा सर्वांसी बाधक । मुख्य दोष ते आशा

statements.statement: He whose hope goes completely obtains supreme happiness; Brahmā and others bow at his feet; the eighth siddhi stays as his maidservant.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ज्याची आशा निःशेष जाये । तोचि परम सुख लाहे । ब्रह्मादिक वंदिती पाये । अष्टमा सिद्धि राहे दासीत्वें

statements.statement: Therefore, with body, speech and mind, one should worship hopelessness; beyond this no other means to paramārtha is seen here.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: यालागीं कायावाचाचित्तें । उपासावें निराशेतें । यापरतें परमार्थातें । साधन येथें दिसेना

statements.statement: Compassion enveloped Avadhūta; holding Yadu to his belly, he said that hopelessness such as this must by all means be practised.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: कृपा जाकळिलें अवधूतासी । यदूसी धरोनियां पोटासी । निराशता हे जे ऐसी । अवश्यतेसीं साधावी

statements.statement: The Avadhūta says to Yadu: I made Piṅgalā the seventeenth guru; therefore I became free of hope; such is this lesson.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: म्हणे अवधूत यदूसी। सत्रावा गुरु केला पिंगलेसी। म्हणोन झालों निराशी। असे ऐशी शिक्षा हे

statements.statement: Enough of this much talk. There was a pure city, Videha, where virtuous people lived; there lived a courtesan named Piṅgalā.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: असो यव्हढाचि हा बोल। एक विदेहनगर विमळ। जेथें वसती पुण्यशील। तेथें पिंगळा वेश्या होती

statements.statement: To gather a heap of wealth, she would ask for money from whoever came to her; wishing for more than what he gave, she would turn him away.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: धनराशी मिळावी म्हणून। जो ये त्यापाशीं मागे धन। तो जें दे त्याहून। अधिक इच्छून फिरवी तया

statements.statement: Knowing this eagerness of hers, men of desire leave her house; yet she, dressed up, stays standing at the door.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हा तियेचा ल्हाव जाणून। कामी पुरूष तिचें सदन। मग देती सोडून। तरी ती नटून राहे द्वारीं

statements.statement: The courtesan sits at the door so, goes back into the house, moving to and fro like a cradle [footnote: pāḷaṇā]; sleep does not come to her.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: वेश्या असी बसे दारांत। पुनः जाई घरांत। दोल्या प्रमाणें फिरत। निद्रा न ये तियेसी

statements.statement: Suddenly, by the working of destiny, dispassion arose in her; she says, 'Alas, I am low, who wish for this misconduct.'

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: अकस्मात् दैवयोगेंकरून। वैराग्य तिला होऊन। म्हणे हाय मी हीन। दुराचरण इच्छी हें

statements.statement: A great thought arose in my mind while I was craving wealth; now discriminating contentment comes, as that foolishness goes.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: महान्विचार माझ्या चित्ता। झाला द्रव्यतृष्णा करितां। विवेक तृप्ती ये आतां। मूर्खता जातां ती

statements.statement: He who is the support of the universe, the inner dweller, the delighter, gives delight and wealth and makes one delight; leaving him, why do I wish for those who give fear, grief and delusion?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो विश्वाधार अंतर्यामी रमण। तो रती अर्थ देऊन। रमवी तया सोडून। भयशोकमोहदा कां इच्छीं

statements.statement: I, who wish for impermanent mortals: shame upon me at this time! Having sold this body, pure, I will worship Ātmārāma [the Self-delighting Lord].

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मी अनित्य मर्त्या इच्छी, मला। धिक्कार असो ये वेळां। हा देह विकून विमळा। आत्मारामा भजेन

statements.statement: 'I will delight with that God': making this resolve, giving up her practice of making appointments, free of hope, she sleeps happily.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मी त्या देवाशीं रमेन। असा निश्चय करून। सांकेतवृत्ती सोडून। निराश होऊन सुखें निजें

statements.statement: He with whom hope dwells does not get happy sleep. I took this lesson from the courtesan; now listen to the eighteenth guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: आशा वसे जयापाशीं। सुखें निद्रा नये त्यासी। हें शिक्षण घेतलें वेश्येपाशीं। आतां अठराव्या गुरूचें ऐक

statements.statement: As long as one has not become free of hope, happiness does not come to him; likewise, when he gives up parigraha [footnote: saṅgraha, collecting], composure comes.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जंववरी निराश न झाला। तंववरी सुख नये त्याला। तसाही होतां परिग्रहाला। सोडी त्या स्वस्थता ये

statements.statement: The saintly brāhmaṇa said: Everyone considers certain things within the material world to be most dear to him, and because of attachment to such things one eventually becomes miserable. One who understands this gives up material possessiveness and attachment and thus achieves unlimited happiness.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
श्रीब्राह्मण उवाच
परिग्रहो हि दु:खाय यद् यत्प्रियतमं नृणाम् ।
अनन्तं सुखमाप्नोति तद् विद्वान् यस्त्वकिञ्चन: ॥ १ ॥
original.transliteration:
śrī-brāhmaṇa uvāca
parigraho hi duḥkhāya
yad yat priyatamaṁ nṛṇām
