anantaṁ sukham āpnoti
tad vidvān yas tv akiñcanaḥ
original.word_for_word: śrī-brāhmaṇaḥ uvāca — the saintly brāhmaṇa said; parigrahaḥ — attachment to possession; hi — certainly; duḥkhāya — leading to misery; yat yat — whatever; priya-tamam — is most dear; nṛṇām — of men; anantam — unlimited; sukham — happiness; āpnoti — achieves; tat — that; vidvān — knowing; yaḥ — whoever; tu — indeed; akiñcanaḥ — is free from such attachment.

statements.statement: Once a group of large hawks who were unable to find any prey attacked another, weaker hawk who was holding some meat. At that time, being in danger of his life, the hawk gave up his meat and experienced actual happiness.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
सामिषं कुररं जघ्नुर्बलिनोऽन्ये निरामिषा: ।
तदामिषं परित्यज्य स सुखं समविन्दत ॥ २ ॥
original.transliteration:
sāmiṣaṁ kuraraṁ jaghnur
balino ’nye nirāmiṣāḥ
tadāmiṣaṁ parityajya
sa sukhaṁ samavindata
original.word_for_word: sa-āmiṣam — having meat; kuraram — a large hawk; jaghnuḥ — they attacked; balinaḥ — very strong; anye — others; nirāmiṣāḥ — without meat; tadā — at that time; āmiṣam — the meat; parityajya — giving up; saḥ — he; sukham — happiness; samavindata — achieved.

statements.statement: Incited by the modes of nature, birds become violent and kill other birds to eat them or to steal meat captured by them. Hawks, vultures and eagles are in this category. However, one should give up the envious propensity to commit violence against others and should take to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, whereby one sees every living entity as equal to oneself. On this platform of actual happiness one does not envy anyone and thus sees no one as his enemy.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The brāhmaṇa says to the king: he who has possessions, for him sorrow grows - higher and higher, day and night.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ब्राह्मण म्हणे रायासी । परिग्रहो जयापाशीं । वाढतें दुःख तयासी । अहर्निशीं चढोवढी

statements.statement: Whatever possessions are made with love, each gives rise to sorrow and quarrel; even when this is experienced, dispassion does not arise - see.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: आवडीं केला जो परिग्रहो । तो तो उपजवी दुःखकलहो । हा होतांही अनुभवो । वैराग्य पहा हो उपजेना

statements.statement: 'Worldly existence is impermanent and perishable; what is lasting in the hoard of it?' - reflecting thus on everything, they became of a mind with nothing of their own.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: प्रपंच अनित्य नाशवंत । तेथील संग्रह काय शाश्वत । ऐसें विवंचूनि समस्त । अकिंचनचित्त ते जाहले

statements.statement: Among possessions the heaviest shackle is the possession of the body; he who breaks it on the spot by seeing its falsity is a knower, firm in discernment.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: परिग्रहामाजीं गाढा । देहपरिग्रहाचा खोडा । मिथ्यात्वें फोडी रोकडा । तो विवेकें गाढा ज्ञाता पैं

statements.statement: Where the possession of the body has become false, he has come to the house of endless happiness; he has obtained that own happiness whose end cannot be made.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जेथ देहपरिग्रह मिथ्या जाहला । तो अनंत सुखाच्या घरा आला । ज्या सुखासी अंत न वचे केला । त्या पावला निजसुखा

statements.statement: The 'kurara' is called the lapwing; it got a fine mouthful of meat; it was meant to eat it right there, but its greedy nature held it back.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ’कुरर’ बोलिजे टिटवा । पावला आमिषकवळु बरवा । तेणें तेथेंची भक्षवा । तो लोभस्वभावा ठेविला

statements.statement: Seeing that meat, the stronger kurara birds that had no meat, large and small together, rushed up very swiftly.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तें आमिष देखोनियां फार । बळी जे निरामिष कुरर । ते धांविन्नले अतिसत्वर । लहान थोर मिळोनि

statements.statement: He says: 'The root of my sorrow is the mouthful of meat I have'; abandoning it at once, he sat happy and unmoved.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: म्हणे माझिया दुःखासी मूळ । मजपाशील आमिष-कवळ । तो त्यजोनियां तत्काळ । सुखी सुनिश्चळ बैसला

statements.statement: Where the mouthful of meat falls, there the uproar of quarrel breaks out; they split each other's heads and smash each other's beaks.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जेथ आमिषकवळु पडे । तेथ कलहाचा गोंधळ मांडे । परस्परें फुटती मुंडें । ठेंचिती तोंडे येरयेरां

statements.statement: The one who sat down after abandoning the meat watches the spectacle of the quarrel; where there are possessions, there is sorrow; in giving them up, supreme happiness.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: आमिष त्यजोनि बैसला देख । तो पाहे कलहाचें कौतुक । मूळ परिग्रहो तेथें दुःख । परम सुख त्यागितां

statements.statement: The root of all this possession is wholly the body-sense, and that is made strong by ego; thus the root of all is ego.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: या समस्त परिग्रहाचें मूळ । देहबुद्धि गा केवळ । तेहीं अभिमानें सबळ । एवं सर्वांस मूळ अभिमानु

statements.statement: When that ego is given up, the root of worldly existence is cut, as when its root is cut a great, huge tree topples over.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तो अभिमानु जैं सांडे । तैं प्रपंचाचें मूळ खंडे । मूळ छेदिल्या जेवीं उलंडे । अतिप्रचंडे तरुवर

statements.statement: Know the root of giving up possessions: first give up ego; without it, renunciation, if made, will be a mockery.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: परिग्रहत्यागाचें मूळ जाण । आधीं त्यजावा अभिमान । तेणेंवीण त्यागु तो विटंबन । केल्या जाण हो‌ईल

statements.statement: I took this device from the kurara [footnote: ṭiṭavī, lapwing]: once the kurara birds were dividing meat and eating it; one of them made a store of the meat.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: म्यां हें युक्ती घेतली कुररापाशीं। एकदां कुरर मांसासी। विभागूनी खाती त्या वेळेसी। मांससंग्रह करी एक

statements.statement: What each one wished, he ate; the one who kept a surplus, all of them began to peck at.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जें ज्यांना वाटलें। तें त्यांणीं भक्षिलें। ज्यानें शिल्लक राखिलें। त्याला टोचूं लागले सर्व ते

statements.statement: 'We have all finished ours; you took extra and kept it': hearing this, he let it go; and then they too released him.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सर्वानी आम्हीं संपविलें। त्वां विशेष घेऊन हें ठेविलें। असें ऐकतां तें त्याणें सोडिलें। त्याहीं सोडिलें तया मग

statements.statement: Having observed this, O king, I took this lesson: parigraha is the cause of sorrow; I learned it from the lapwing.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: म्यां हें विलोकन करून। नृपा घेतलें हें शिक्षण। परिग्रह दुःखाला कारण। टिटावूपासून कळलें

statements.statement: The learned man who is free of parigraha and eats what he gets, like fire, even if he has no wealth, is always happy.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो विद्वान् परिग्रहरहित। मिळे तें खाई अग्निवत्। तो जरी धनरहित। तरी तो सतत सुखी होई

statements.statement: As long as the kurara had meat, it got beaten; when it threw away the meat and was far from it, the sorrow too went far away.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मांसयुक्त होतां जंव कुरर। त्याला तंव मिळाला मार। मांस टाकून होता दूर। दुःखही त्याबरोबर दुरावलें

statements.statement: If even a yogī makes parigraha, his mind goes to it; his mind does not come within; therefore there should be no parigraha.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जरी योगी परिग्रह करी। त्याचें चित्त जाई तयावरी। त्याचें चित्त नये अंतरीं। म्हणूनी परिग्रह नसावा

statements.statement: In family life, the parents are always in anxiety about their home, children and reputation. But I have nothing to do with these things. I do not worry at all about any family, and I do not care about honor and dishonor. I enjoy only the life of the soul, and I find love on the spiritual platform. Thus I wander the earth like a child.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
न मे मानापमानौ स्तो न चिन्ता गेहपुत्रिणाम् ।
आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिर्विचरामीह बालवत् ॥ ३ ॥
original.transliteration:
na me mānāpamānau sto
na cintā geha-putriṇām
ātma-krīḍa ātma-ratir
vicarāmīha bāla-vat
original.word_for_word: na — not; me — in me; māna — honor; apamānau — dishonor; staḥ — exist; na — there is not; cintā — anxiety; geha — of those who have a home; putriṇām — and children; ātma — by the self; krīḍaḥ — sporting; ātma — in the self alone; ratiḥ — enjoying; vicarāmi — I wander; iha — in this world; bāla-vat — like a child.

statements.statement: In this world two types of people are free from all anxiety and merged in great happiness: one who is a retarded and childish fool and one who has approached the Supreme Lord, who is beyond the three modes of material nature.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
द्वावेव चिन्तया मुक्तौ परमानन्द आप्लुतौ ।
यो विमुग्धो जडो बालो यो गुणेभ्य: परं गत: ॥ ४ ॥
original.transliteration:
dvāv eva cintayā muktau
paramānanda āplutau
yo vimugdho jaḍo bālo
yo guṇebhyaḥ paraṁ gataḥ
original.word_for_word: dvau — two; eva — certainly; cintayā — from anxiety; muktau — freed; parama-ānande — in great happiness; āplutau — merged; yaḥ — one who; vimugdhaḥ — is ignorant; jaḍaḥ — retarded without developing activities; bālaḥ — childish; yaḥ — one who; guṇebhyaḥ — to the modes of nature; param — the Lord, who is transcendental; gataḥ — has achieved.

statements.statement: Those who fervently seek material sense gratification are gradually pushed down into a miserable condition of life because as soon as one even slightly violates the laws of nature, one must suffer sinful reactions. Thus even materially alert and ambitious persons are constantly in anxiety, and from time to time they are plunged into great misery. Those who are nonsensical and retarded, however, live in a fool’s paradise, and those who have surrendered to Lord Kṛṣṇa are filled with transcendental bliss. Therefore both the fool and the devotee may be said to be peaceful, in the sense that they are free from the ordinary anxiety of the materially ambitious person. However, this does not mean that the devotee and the retarded fool are on the same platform. A fool’s peace is like that of a dead stone, whereas a devotee’s satisfaction is based on perfect knowledge.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The child does not say 'mine' or 'yours'; he knows nothing of high or low; therefore he bears honour and dishonour happily in every way.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: बाल माझें तुझें न म्हणे । उंच नीच कांही नेणे । यालागीं मानापमान तेणें । सुखें साहणें सर्वथा

statements.statement: A three-month-old child does not recognize what honour is; dishonour too he does not see; he plays in his own happiness.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तिमासांचेनि बाळकें । मानु कोण हें नोळखे । अपमानु तोही न देखे । आपुलेनि सुखें क्रीडत

statements.statement: The child does not touch duality; in his own play he plays with himself alone; in his own company, he himself.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: दुजेपणातें नातळे । बालक आपुलियाचि लीळें । आप‍आपणियाशींच खेळें । आपुलेनि मेळें आपण

statements.statement: Worry about body and house never touches the child; by nature he is free of care; there is no talk of worry for him.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देहगेहांची चिंता । बाळासि नातळे सर्वथा । स्वभावेंचि निश्चिंतता । चिंताकथा त्या नाहीं

statements.statement: The yogī has no awareness of the world as real; therefore honour and dishonour are both equal to him.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: योगियासी प्रपंचाचें भान । सत्यत्वें नाहीं जाण । यालागीं मानापमान । दोन्ही समान तयासी

statements.statement: Imagination is the root of worldly existence, know; that imagination is subject to the mind; when that mind has become absorbed in the Self, then the Reality, the mass of consciousness, is everywhere.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: भवमूळ कल्पना जाण । ते कल्पना मना‌आधीन । तें मन स्वरूपीं जाहलिया लीन । तेव्हां वस्तु-चिद्घन सर्वत्र

statements.statement: Having reached the attainment of his own happiness, the mind and the other senses cease; no thought-activity stirs even by an atom - this they call 'samādhi'.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पावोनि निजसुखप्राप्ती । मन‍आदि इंद्रियें उपरमती । अणुभरी स्फुरेना वृत्ती । ’समाधि’ बोलती या नांव

statements.statement: For him, whose honour or dishonour? Who is to worry about house and children? His mind is lost in the Self; he has obtained his own contentment.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: त्यासी कोणाचा मानापमान । गृहपुत्रचिंता करी कोण । स्वरूपीं हारपलें मन । निजसमाधान पावला

statements.statement: That moving about without mind, know, is like the child's: movement and action by destiny; he acts devoid of thought-activity.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मनेंवीण जें विहरण । तें बालकाच्या ऐसें जाण । दैवयोगें चलनवलन । वृत्तिशून्य वर्तत

statements.statement: For one, sorrow will meet him later; the other has conquered pleasure and pain; for one it is the happiness of innocence; for the other, his own knowledge.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एकासी पुढे भेटेल् दुःख् । दुजेनि जिंतिलें सुखदुःख् । एकासी मुग्धतेचें सुख् । दुज्या देख् निजज्ञान्

statements.statement: Not so the yogī beyond the guṇas, filled with perfect bliss; for him there is no talk at all of pleasure and pain in the world.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसा नव्हे योगिया गुणातीत् । जो पूर्णानंदें पूर्णभरित् । त्यासी सुखदुःखाची मात् । नाहीं जगांत् सर्वथा

statements.statement: As long as there is a heap of firewood, the fire burns it with delight; when the bits of wood are finished, the fire enters its own brilliance.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जंव् जंव् काष्ठसंभार् असे । तंव् तंव् अग्नि जाळी उल्हासें । सरलेनि काष्ठलेशें । अग्नि प्रवेशे निजतेजीं

statements.statement: That happiness which has no end has been obtained as his own nature; living in the body, he is beyond the body; for him there is no eddy of worry.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ज्या सुखासी नाहीं अंत् । तें सुख् स्वरूपें झालें प्राप्त् । ते देहीं वर्ततां देहातीत् । चिंता‌आवर्त् त्यां नाहीं

statements.statement: To attain one's own aim I took the kurara's lesson; to give up worry about honour and dishonour, the child became my guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: स्वसाध्य साधावें म्हणून। कुरराचें घेतलें शिक्षण। मानापमानचिंता सोडून। द्यावया बाळ गुरु झाला

statements.statement: The child, in his own bliss, knows not ash or mud, nor fragrant scent, nor any honour or contempt.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो भस्म किंवा चिखल। नेणे सुगंधी परिमळ। सत्कार तिरस्कार सकळ। नेणे बाळ निजानंदें

statements.statement: He knows not rope or snake, so he feels no remorse; he who knows not merit and sin takes no stain upon himself.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हा रज्जु किंवा सर्प। नेणे तो न करी अनुताप। जो नेणे पुण्य पाप। न घे लेप आपणावरी

statements.statement: Whether there is great cheapness or great dearness, he takes no thought of it and is never dejected.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हो बहु सवंगायी। अथवा होवो महागायी। त्याची चिंता न घेई। न होई जो कदापि खिन्न

statements.statement: 'What is lacking in this house? How should I get it? Will insult come now?': though living at home, he thinks not of this either.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ह्या घरात काय न्यून। कसें करावें संपादन। आतां होईल कीं अपमान। हेंही घरी राहून न चिंती

statements.statement: 'Death will come now; or calamity will come; or disrepute will come': the child thinks not of this either.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मरण आतां हें येईल। किंवा आपत्ती होईल। किंवा अपकिर्ती होईल। हेंही बाल न चिंती

statements.statement: 'How should wealth be earned? How guarded? How should the family be maintained?': the child never thinks so.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: धन मेळवावें कसें। तें रक्षावें कसें। परिवारा पाळावें कसें। बाळ असें कधींही न चिंती

statements.statement: He who makes no wishes, plays by himself, loves himself: in this way the child is happy.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो मनोरथ न करी। आपण आपल्यासी क्रीडा करी। आपणावरी प्रीती करी। यापरी बाळ सुखी

statements.statement: When his hunger and thirst are satisfied, he plays, even if he is alone; by making this child one's guru, inwardness comes naturally.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ज्याची भूक तहान भागतां। खेळे असो का एकुलता। ह्या बाळा गुरू करितां। अंतर्निष्ठता सहज ये

statements.statement: This illusory world: who is whose family? whose house is where? All of this is a bazaar of worries.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हा मायिक संसार। कोण कोणाचा परिवार। कोणाचें कोठें घर। चिंतेचा बाजार हा सर्वही

statements.statement: 'How will that sweet food be got? How will friendship with these people be formed? How will sorrow be avoided? When will cheapness come now?'

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ते मिष्ठांन कसें मिळेल। ह्या लोकांशीं स्नेह कसा जुळेल। दुःख कसें टळेल। सवंगाई होईल कधीं आतां

statements.statement: Those men who are constantly pervaded by this worry, who say 'let there be no contempt, let there be honour',

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ह्या चिंतेनें निरंतर। व्याप्त असती जे नर। न व्हावा तिरस्कार। व्हावा सत्कार म्हणती जे

statements.statement: their inwardness does not come about; even if they listen [to teaching], the mind does not enter within; therefore I take the child's way.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: त्यांची न होई अंतर्वृत्ती। जरी ते श्रवण करिती। तरी आंत नये वृत्ती। म्हणोनी बाळरीती घेतों

statements.statement: That going as one pleases [kāmacāra; footnote: going wherever one wishes], that age: what use is there in reflection? Therefore I took freedom from attachment, aversion and the like from the nineteenth guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तो कामचार तें वय। मननीं उपयोग काय। म्हणूनी रागद्वेषादि राहित्य। घेतलें एकुणिसाव्या गुरूपासून

statements.statement: Once a marriageable young girl was alone in her house because her parents and relatives had gone that day to another place. At that time a few men arrived at the house, specifically desiring to marry her. She received them with all hospitality.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
क्व‍‍चित् कुमारी त्वात्मानं वृणानान् गृहमागतान् ।
स्वयं तानर्हयामास क्व‍ापि यातेषु बन्धुषु ॥ ५ ॥
original.transliteration:
kvacit kumārī tv ātmānaṁ
vṛṇānān gṛham āgatān
svayaṁ tān arhayām āsa
kvāpi yāteṣu bandhuṣu
original.word_for_word: kvacit — once; kumārī — a young girl; tu — indeed; ātmānam — herself; vṛṇānān — desiring as a wife; gṛham — to the house; āgatān — arrived; svayam — herself; tān — those men; arhayām āsa — received with great hospitality; kva api — to another place; yāteṣu — when they had gone; bandhuṣu — all her relatives.

statements.statement: The girl went to a private place and began to make preparations so that the unexpected male guests could eat. As she was beating the rice, the conchshell bracelets on her arms were colliding and making a loud noise.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
तेषामभ्यवहारार्थं शालीन् रहसि पार्थिव ।
अवघ्नन्त्या: प्रकोष्ठस्थाश्चक्रु: शङ्खा: स्वनं महत् ॥ ६ ॥
original.transliteration:
teṣām abhyavahārārthaṁ
śālīn rahasi pārthiva
avaghnantyāḥ prakoṣṭha-sthāś
cakruḥ śaṅkhāḥ svanaṁ mahat
original.word_for_word: teṣām — of the guests; abhyavahāra-artham — so that they could eat; śālīn — rice; rahasi — being alone; pārthiva — O King; avaghnantyāḥ — of her who was beating; prakoṣṭha — on her forearms; sthāḥ — situated; cakruḥ — they made; śaṅkhāḥ — bracelets made of conchshell; svanam — a sound; mahat — great.

statements.statement: The young girl feared that the men would consider her family to be poor because their daughter was busily engaged in the menial task of husking rice. Being very intelligent, the shy girl broke the shell bracelets from her arms, leaving just two on each wrist.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
सा तज्जुगुप्सितं मत्वा महती व्रीडिता तत: ।
बभञ्जैकैकश: शङ्खान् द्वौ द्वौ पाण्योरशेषयत् ॥ ७ ॥
original.transliteration:
sā taj jugupsitaṁ matvā
mahatī vrīḍitā tataḥ
babhañjaikaikaśaḥ śaṅkhān
dvau dvau pāṇyor aśeṣayat
original.word_for_word: sā — she; tat — that noise; jugupsitam — shameful; matvā — thinking; mahatī — very intelligent; vrīḍitā — shy; tataḥ — from her arms; babhañja — she broke; eka-ekaśaḥ — one by one; śaṅkhān — the shell bracelets; dvau dvau — two each; pāṇyoḥ — on her two hands; aśeṣayat — she kept on.

statements.statement: Thereafter, as the young girl continued to husk the rice, the two bracelets on each wrist continued to collide and make noise. Therefore she took one bracelet off each arm, and with only one left on each wrist there was no more noise.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
उभयोरप्यभूद् घोषो ह्यवघ्नन्त्या: स्वशङ्खयो: ।
तत्राप्येकं निरभिददेकस्मान्नाभवद् ध्वनि: ॥ ८ ॥
original.transliteration:
ubhayor apy abhūd ghoṣo
hy avaghnantyāḥ sva-śaṅkhayoḥ
tatrāpy ekaṁ nirabhidad
ekasmān nābhavad dhvaniḥ
original.word_for_word: ubhayoḥ — from the two (on each hand); api — still; abhūt — there was; ghoṣaḥ — noise; hi — indeed; avaghnantyāḥ — of her who was husking the rice; sva-śaṅkhayoḥ — from each set of two shell ornaments; tatra — therein; api — indeed; ekam — one only; nirabhidat — she separated; ekasmāt — from that one ornament; na — not; abhavat — there was; dhvaniḥ — a sound.

statements.statement: O subduer of the enemy, I travel throughout the surface of the earth learning constantly about the nature of this world, and thus I personally witnessed the lesson of the young girl.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
अन्वशिक्षमिमं तस्या उपदेशमरिन्दम ।
लोकाननुचरन्नेतान् लोकतत्त्वविवित्सया ॥ ९ ॥
original.transliteration:
anvaśikṣam imaṁ tasyā
upadeśam arindama
lokān anucarann etān
loka-tattva-vivitsayā
original.word_for_word: anvaśikṣam — I have seen with my own eyes; imam — this; tasyāḥ — of the young girl; upadeśam — lesson; arim-dama — O subduer of the enemy; lokān — worlds; anucaran — wandering; etān — these; loka — of the world; tattva — truth; vivitsayā — with a desire to know.

statements.statement: The brāhmaṇa sage here explains to King Yadu that he is not presenting theoretical knowledge. Rather, by wandering throughout the world the observant and thoughtful brāhmaṇa has personally experienced the lessons learned from all of the above-mentioned gurus. Thus, instead of posing himself to be omniscient like God, he humbly explains that he has faithfully learned these lessons in his travels.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: When many people live together in one place there will undoubtedly be quarreling. And even if only two people live together there will be frivolous conversation and disagreement. Therefore, to avoid conflict, one should live alone, as we learn from the example of the bracelet of the young girl.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
वासे बहूनां कलहो भवेद् वार्ता द्वयोरपि ।
एक एव वसेत्तस्मात् कुमार्या इव कङ्कण: ॥ १० ॥
original.transliteration:
vāse bahūnāṁ kalaho
bhaved vārtā dvayor api
eka eva vaset tasmāt
kumāryā iva kaṅkaṇaḥ
original.word_for_word: vāse — in a residence; bahūnām — of many people; kalahaḥ — quarrel; bhavet — will be; vārtā — conversation; dvayoḥ — of two people; api — even; ekaḥ — alone; eva — certainly; vaset — one should live; tasmāt — therefore; kumāryāḥ — of the young girl; iva — like; kaṅkaṇaḥ — the bracelet.

statements.statement: Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura has given a nice example in this regard. Because the young girl mentioned in this story had no husband, she had to fulfill her duties as a host by removing her bracelets so that each wrist held one bracelet only. In the same way, the process of jñāna-yoga, or spiritual advancement by philosophical speculation, demands that the speculating sages live alone, without any other association. Since jñānīs have dedicated their lives to speculation, there will undoubtedly be endless argument and quarreling on technical points if many jñānīs live together. Therefore, to keep a peaceful atmosphere they must live alone. On the other hand, a king’s daughter who has been duly married to an aristocratic prince fulfills her duties to her husband by dressing herself attractively with innumerable ornaments and approaching him for love. Similarly, the goddess of devotion, Bhaktidevī, decorates herself with the innumerable ornaments of the Vaiṣṇavas, who come together to relish the sweet sound of the holy name of the Lord. Because pure Vaiṣṇavas do not intimately associate with nondevotees, it may be said that they reside alone, and thus they also fulfill the purpose of this verse. There cannot be any quarrel among pure Vaiṣṇavas, because they are on the real platform of desirelessness, not wanting even salvation or mystic powers, what to speak of sense gratification. Because they are all devotees of Kṛṣṇa, they may freely associate with one another for glorifying the Lord. As stated in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (3.25.34):

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement:
naikātmatāṁ me spṛhayanti kecin
mat-pāda-sevābhiratā mad-īhāḥ
ye ’nyonyato bhāgavatāḥ prasajya
sabhājayante mama pauruṣāṇi

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: “A pure devotee, who is attached to the activities of devotional service and who always engages in the service of My lotus feet, never desires to become one with Me. Such a devotee, who is unflinchingly engaged, always glorifies My pastimes and activities.”

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura has commented on this verse as follows: “The young girl in the story kept only one bracelet on each wrist so that there would be no noisy conflict among the bracelets. Similarly, one should give up the association of those who are not devoted to the Supreme Lord.” This is the actual lesson to be learned. A real Vaiṣṇava is always pure and faultless in character. However, in those places where nondevotees congregate there will undoubtedly be envious criticism of the devotional service of the Lord, and those who falsely attempt to analyze reality without the Supreme Personality of Godhead will create much disturbing noise in the name of philosophy. Therefore, one should remain in those places where the Supreme Lord is properly worshiped according to the Vedic standard. If everyone is dedicated to glorifying the Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, there will not be any impediment in mutual association. However, in a place where people have many different purposes besides the pleasure of the Supreme Lord, social dealings will certainly be disrupted.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: One should therefore avoid the association of those who are inimical to devotional service; otherwise one will be frustrated in achieving the spiritual purpose of life. One who always keeps himself in the company of the devotees of the Lord is actually living alone. If one lives in a community where the only consideration is the pleasure of the Lord, then one can avoid the contradictory situations caused by many persons competing to satisfy their own material desires. This is the lesson intelligently understood by the brāhmaṇa from the bracelets of the young girl.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: In this connection Śrīla Madhvācārya quotes the following:

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement:
asaj-janais tu saṁvāso
na kartavyaḥ kathañcana
yāvad yāvac ca bahubhiḥ
saj-janaiḥ sa tu mukti-daḥ

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: “One should not under any circumstances live with those who are not devotees of the Lord. On the other hand, one should stay with many devotees, because such association awards liberation.”

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A certain maiden had been left to keep watch over the house; her father and mother, with their kinsfolk, had gone on pilgrimage to the family deity.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: कोणी एके कुमारीसी । घरीं राखण ठेवूनि तिसी । पिता माता स्वगोत्रेसीं । गेली यात्रेसी कुळदेवा

statements.statement: They ask, 'Who is in the house?' The bride, shy, keeps silent; without letting them see her, she arranges the rites of honouring them.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पुसती घरीं आहे कोण । लाजे नोवरी धरी मौन । त्यांसी न देतां दर्शन । पूजाविधान ते मांडी

statements.statement: Thinking thus, she herself set out to pound the paddy; listen to the cleverness of what she did while pounding.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ऐसें विचारूनि जाण । साळी कांडूं रिघे आपण । ते कंडणकाळींचे विंदान । चतुरलक्षण परियेसीं

statements.statement: As she struck the pounding, a jingling rose from the bangles on her hands; embarrassed by that sound, she thought in her mind:

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: घावो घालितां कांडणा । उठी झणत्कार करकंकणा । तेणें नादें लाजोनि जाणा । विचारु मनामाजीं करी

statements.statement: 'The sound of these conch-shell bangles will fall on the guests' ears; it would be a great shame to me that the new bride sat down to pound.'

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: या शंखवलयांचा ध्वनि । पडेल पाहुण्यांचें कानीं । ते अत्यंत लाज मजलागुनि । नववधु कांडणीं बैसली

statements.statement: That very intelligent maiden softly took the bangles off; she kept them carefully, keeping two on each of her two hands.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अति बुद्धिमंत ते कुमारी । हळूचि कंकणें उतरी । ते ठेवी जतनेवरी । राखे दों करीं दोनी

statements.statement: Leaving two bangles, she sat down to pound; a sound arose from between the two, and hearing it with her ears she was embarrassed.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: दोनी कंकणें उरवूनी । कांडूं बैसली कांडणीं । दोंहीमाजीं उठे ध्वनी । ऐकोनि कानीं लाजिली

statements.statement: She says: 'Where two are together in one place, the sound cannot fail to arise.' Removing one of the two, the maiden sat down to pound.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: म्हणे दोघांचा संगु एके स्थानीं । तेथें सर्वथा न राहे ध्वनी । दोंतील एक वेगळें काढोनी । बसे कांडणीं कुमारी

statements.statement: When she pounded in oneness, truly no sound arose. That teaching, O king, I received there, becoming a learner.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एकपणीं कांडितां । ध्वनि नुठेचि तत्त्वतां । तो उपदेशु नृपनाथा । झालों शिकता मी तेथ

statements.statement: Having conquered rival kings, you made all the kings your servants; you are a mighty 'crusher of foes' - that pride is wholly false.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जिणोनि प्रतिस्पर्धी भूपाळ । किंकर केले राजे सकळ । तूं अरिमर्दन सबळ । मिथ्या केवळ तो गर्व

statements.statement: Until the whole host of enemies - lust, anger and the rest - is completely conquered, the word 'crusher of foes' is a mockery; it will be apt in this sense.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: कामक्रोधादि अरिवर्ग । न जिणतां सकळ साङ्ग । ’अरिमर्दन’ हा बोल व्यंग । हो‌ईल चांग ये अर्थी

statements.statement: The six enemies, lust and the rest - when they are conquered with the weapon of this teaching and shackled, then in worldly life there is no enemy.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: कामादिक सहा वैरी । येणें उपदेशशस्त्रधारीं । जिणोनि घालितां तोडरीं । मग संसारी अरि नाहीं

statements.statement: Where many dwell together, there quarrel comes without fail; even when two sit together in solitude, they talk of many kinds of things.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जेथ होय बहुतांची वस्ती । तेथ अनिवार कलहप्राप्ती । दोघे बैसल्या एकांतीं । वार्ता करिती बहुविधा

statements.statement: Where time passes in talk, there one's own true purpose cannot be accomplished; therefore, seeing this, I wander alone.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जेथें गोष्टीखालीं काळु जाये । तेथें निजस्वार्थु हों न लाहे । यालागीं मी पाहें । विचरत आहें एकाकी

statements.statement: If one-pointedness is practised alone, great gain comes to hand; in this regard I truly made the arrow-maker a guru.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एकाकी एकाग्रता । साधिल्या थोर लाभु ये हाता । येचविषयीं शरकर्ता । गुरु तत्त्वतां म्यां केला

statements.statement: To become full of bliss like the child just described, one should practise after finding solitude; this I shall tell, as taught by the maiden's bangles.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: असा उक्त बालवत। व्हावया आनंदभरित। अभ्यास कीजे पाहूनी एकांत। हें कुमारीकंकणशिक्षित सांगेन

statements.statement: Solitude [vivikti; footnote: ekānta] will be beneficial; this will be known from this very lesson. A well-behaved maiden had become of marriageable age.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: विविक्तिं हित होईल। हें ह्याच शिक्षणें कळेल। एक कन्या सुशील। विवाहयोग्य जाहली होती

statements.statement: Learned brahmins came to choose her [as bride]; before that, her relatives had gone off to the village.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: आले विद्वान ब्राह्मण। तिला वरावी म्हणून। तत्पूर्वीं निघून। तिचे स्वजन गांवीं गेले

statements.statement: Since there was a cow at home, they had gone leaving her at home; she saw them, gave them seats and honoured them.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: घरीं धेनू होती म्हणून। गेले घरीं तिला ठेवून। तिणें त्यांला देखून। आसन देऊन सत्कार केला

statements.statement: For their midday meal she was pounding rice; the bangles jingling, she felt uneasy.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: त्यांच्या मध्यान्हाकरितां। तिणें साळी कांडतां। कांकणें खळखळतां। तिच्या चित्ता वाईट वाटे

statements.statement: 'This brings blemish to my ancestors': so, keeping two bangles on each arm, she pounded; even those, struck together, clanked.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हें ये पूर्वजांस कीं दूषण। म्हणून दोन दोन कंकणें राखून। कांडी तींही आपटून। खणखण होती

statements.statement: 'Removing all would bring blame': so she kept one on each arm as the remainder; no noise came of it; then she was content.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: संपूर्ण काढितां ये दोष। म्हणोन एक एक राखी शेष। त्याचा न झाला घोष। तिला संतोष झाला मग

statements.statement: That very lesson I got: when many gather, quarrel arises; with two, there is talk; when one is alone, meditation happens.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तेंच मज मिळालें शिक्षण। बहुत जमतां होई भांडण। दोघांचेही होई भाषण। एक असतां ध्यान घडे

statements.statement: 'Pramāda [heedlessness] indeed comes through company': making this resolve, I stayed lying alone; through that, satisfaction and rest come.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: प्रमादः खलु संगेन। असा निश्चय करून। राहिलों एकला पडून। तेणें समाधान विसावा ये

statements.statement: Even if one says one wishes to stay always full of perfect bliss, one should never keep any one fixed place.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जरी पूर्णानंदभरित। राहावें म्हणेल सतत। तरी त्याणें एक नियमित। स्थान कदापि न धरावें

statements.statement: Having perfected the yoga sitting postures and conquered the breathing process, one should make the mind steady by detachment and the regulated practice of yoga. Thus one should carefully fix the mind on the single goal of yoga practice.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
मन एकत्र संयुञ्ज्याज्जितश्वासो जितासन: ।
वैराग्याभ्यासयोगेन ध्रियमाणमतन्द्रित: ॥ ११ ॥
original.transliteration:
mana ekatra saṁyuñjyāj
jita-śvāso jitāsanaḥ
vairāgyābhyāsa-yogena
dhriyamāṇam atandritaḥ
original.word_for_word: manaḥ — the mind; ekatra — in one place; saṁyuñjyāt — one should fix; jita — conquered; śvāsaḥ — the breathing process; jita — conquered; āsanaḥ — the yoga sitting postures; vairāgya — by detachment; abhyāsa-yogena — by the regulated practice of yoga; dhriyamāṇam — the mind being steadied; atandritaḥ — very carefully.

statements.statement: One should develop vairāgya, or detachment, by observing that all material things are doomed. Thus one should take to the regulated practice of yoga, which in this age means the process of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra. According to Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura, the avadhūta brāhmaṇa is recommending bhakti-miśra aṣṭāṅga-yoga, or the eightfold mystic yoga process performed as an offering to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The desire to enjoy the material world is so strong that the mind wanders here and there uncontrollably. Therefore it is stated, dhriyamāṇam: the mind must be fixed in the goal of life, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In the perfect stage of mental concentration called samādhi there is no longer any distinction between internal and external vision, since one can see the Absolute Truth everywhere.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: In the mystic yoga process one must sit properly, and then it is possible to control the different airs within the body. When the breathing process is controlled, the mind, which is dependent upon the actions of the bodily airs, is easily fixed in higher consciousness. But although the mind may be momentarily controlled, if one is overcome by desire for sense gratification the mind will again be lost. Thus, this verse emphasizes vairāgya, detachment from material illusion. This is attained by abhyāsa-yoga, the regulated practice of Kṛṣṇa consciousness, which is the highest yoga system, as confirmed in Bhagavad-gītā (6.47):

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement:
yoginām api sarveṣāṁ
mad-gatenāntar-ātmanā
śraddhāvān bhajate yo māṁ
sa me yuktatamo mataḥ

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: “And of all yogīs, he who always abides in Me with great faith, worshiping Me in transcendental loving service, is most intimately united with Me in yoga and is the highest of all.”

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The mind can be controlled when it is fixed on the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Having achieved a stable situation, the mind becomes free from polluted desires to execute material activities; thus as the mode of goodness increases in strength, one can completely give up the modes of passion and ignorance, and gradually one transcends even the material mode of goodness. When the mind is freed from the fuel of the modes of nature, the fire of material existence is extinguished. Then one achieves the transcendental platform of direct relationship with the object of his meditation, the Supreme Lord.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
यस्मिन् मनो लब्धपदं यदेत-
च्छनै: शनैर्मुञ्चति कर्मरेणून् ।
सत्त्वेन वृद्धेन रजस्तमश्च
विधूय निर्वाणमुपैत्यनिन्धनम् ॥ १२ ॥
original.transliteration:
yasmin mano labdha-padaṁ yad etac
chanaiḥ śanair muñcati karma-reṇūn
sattvena vṛddhena rajas tamaś ca
vidhūya nirvāṇam upaity anindhanam
original.word_for_word: yasmin — in which (the Supreme Lord); manaḥ — the mind; labdha — having obtained; padam — a permanent situation; yat etat — that very mind; śanaiḥ śanaiḥ — gradually, step by step; muñcati — gives up; karma — of fruitive activities; reṇūn — the contamination; sattvena — by the mode of goodness; vṛddhena — which has grown strong; rajaḥ — the mode of passion; tamaḥ — the mode of ignorance; ca — also; vidhūya — giving up; nirvāṇam — the transcendental position in which one is united with the object of his meditation; upaiti — achieves; anindhanam — without fuel.

statements.statement: The interaction of the three modes of nature creates great obstacles in one’s path of spiritual advancement, and there is danger that one may be thrown down into the darkness of ignorance. Those who are experienced in practical psychology know the dangers of the uncontrolled mind and constantly endeavor to bring the mind under control. If one can free oneself from the influence of the material modes of passion and ignorance, then life becomes very auspicious. Controlling the mind, and thereby freeing oneself from the influence of the material modes of nature, is the only means of making actual progress in life. The word yasmin in this verse, according to Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī, indicates the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the reservoir of all pleasure. Giving up the material propensities of the mind does not mean merging into an impersonal existence, such as that experienced in dreamless sleep. As stated in this verse, sattvena vṛddhena: one must become firmly established in the mode of goodness and then gradually rise onto the spiritual platform, where one may dwell in the company of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Thus, when one’s consciousness is completely fixed on the Absolute Truth, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one no longer sees duality, or internal and external reality. The example is given of the arrow maker who was so absorbed in making a straight arrow that he did not even see or notice the king himself, who was passing right next to him.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
तदैवमात्मन्यवरुद्धचित्तो
न वेद किञ्चिद् बहिरन्तरं वा ।
यथेषुकारो नृपतिं व्रजन्त-
मिषौ गतात्मा न ददर्श पार्श्वे ॥ १३ ॥
original.transliteration:
tadaivam ātmany avaruddha-citto
na veda kiñcid bahir antaraṁ vā
yatheṣu-kāro nṛpatiṁ vrajantam
iṣau gatātmā na dadarśa pārśve
original.word_for_word: tadā — at that time; evam — thus; ātmani — in the Supreme Personality of Godhead; avaruddha — fixed; cittaḥ — the mind; na — does not; veda — know; kiñcit — anything; bahiḥ — outside; antaram — inside; vā — either; yathā — just as; iṣu — of arrows; kāraḥ — a maker; nṛ-patim — the king; vrajantam — going; iṣau — in the arrow; gata-ātmā — being absorbed; na dadarśa — did not see; pārśve — right next to him.

statements.statement: It is understood that when a king moves on a public street he is heralded by kettledrums and other musical instruments and is accompanied by soldiers and other members of his retinue. Thus, despite this royal extravaganza passing right by his workshop, the arrow maker did not even notice because he was completely absorbed in his prescribed duty of making an arrow straight and sharp. One who is completely absorbed in loving devotional service to the Absolute Truth, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, no longer pays attention to material illusion. In this verse the word bahis, “external,” refers to the innumerable objects of material sense gratification, such as food, drink, sex, and so on, which drag the senses of the conditioned soul into material duality. The word antaram, or “internal,” refers to memory of previous sense gratification or hopes and dreams for future materialistic situations. One who is seeing everywhere the Absolute Truth, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, categorically rejects both internal and external illusion. This is called mukti-pada, or the status of liberation. On this platform there is neither attraction nor aversion to sense objects; rather, there is loving absorption in the Absolute Truth, Kṛṣṇa, and an overwhelming desire to please Him by devotional service. One who gives up the reality of Kṛṣṇa will be forced to wander uselessly in the kingdom of mental speculation. One who cannot see that the Absolute Truth, Lord Kṛṣṇa, is the background and basis of everything that exists will be bewildered by the false concept that there is something that is not Kṛṣṇa. Everything emanates from the Lord, and He is the Lord of everything. This simple understanding is the actual existential situation.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Where practice is done without dispassion, the thieves of sense-objects rise up strongly; the raid of desire falls, and the capital, one's own knowledge, is lost.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: वैराग्येंवीण अभ्यासु घडे । तेथ विषयचोर उठती गाढे । कामाचा घाला पडे । मुद्दल बुडे निजज्ञान

statements.statement: For a long time prāṇa and apāna had been missing each other; by the strength of practice, suddenly the two were made to recognize each other.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: प्राणापानाची चुकामुकी । झाली होती बहुकाळ कीं । ते अभ्यासबळें एका‌एकीं । केली वोळखी दोघांसी

statements.statement: There a fine battle took place: the six enemies, lust and the rest, were felled in the fight without fail, while the bright sword flashed.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तेथ युद्ध झालें चांग । कामादिक अरिषड्वर्ग । रणीं पाडिले अमोघ । सतेज खड्ग झळकत

statements.statement: The object of meditation, the meditation and the meditator - the triad is not seen on looking; for this reason he does not hold the sword of meditation at all.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ध्येय ध्यान ध्याता । त्रिपुटी न दिसे पाहतां । ध्यानखड्ग तत्त्वतां । न धरी सर्वथा या हेतू

statements.statement: Holding the canopy of absorption, on the throne of perfect equality he sat, naturally contented, having cast off the sense of being a jīva.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तन्मयतेचें छत्र धरूनी । समसाम्यसिंहासनीं । बैसला सहज समाधानी । त्यागी वोंवाळुनी जीवभावो

statements.statement: As the fire that is among sticks of wood, when they are churned, makes a bonfire of the wood; having destroyed the wood at once, it leaves the embers and subsides.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जैसा अग्नि असे काष्ठांच्या मेळीं । मंथिल्या काष्ठाची करी होळी । काष्ठ नाशूनि तत्काळीं । त्यजूनि इंगळीं उपशमे

statements.statement: Likewise, excellent sattva grows, destroys rajas and tamas and casts them off; afterwards even the agitation of sattva itself comes to rest.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसें वाढोनि सत्त्व उत्तम । नाशूनि सांडी रजतम । पाठीं सत्त्वाचाही संभ्रम । स्वयें उपरम पावला

statements.statement: There the jīva-ness of the jīva ended; knowledge ended along with the state of being the knower; the awareness of the world ended; pure consciousness alone filled everything.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तेथें निमालें जीवाचें जीवपण । ज्ञातृत्वेंसीं निमालें ज्ञान । निमालें प्रपंचाचें भान । चिन्मात्र पूर्ण कोंदलें

statements.statement: Such is the fullness of pure consciousness; when the mind is restrained and brought there, the mind attains the state of consciousness - know this fully, O hero among men.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ऐसी चिन्मात्र परिपूर्णता । तेथ निरोधूनि आणितां चित्ता । चित्त पावे चैतन्यता । जाण सर्वथा नरवीरा

statements.statement: Where, looking at the object of meditation, the meditator and the meditation, the mind is joyfully entangled - know that to be 'samprajñāta samādhi'; they enjoy it without the guṇas.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पाहतां ध्येय ध्याता ध्यान । जेथ उल्हासें विगुंतलें मन । ते ’संप्रज्ञातसमाधी’ जाण । गुणेंवीण भोगिती

statements.statement: Brahman is not within the range of the senses; when the guṇas have gone, it is seen with the eye; this is known only to one who has experienced it; it is not something that can be spoken.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ब्रह्म इंद्रियां गोचर नसे । गुण गेलिया डोळां दिसे । हे अनुभव्यासीचि भासे । बोलावें ऐसें तें नव्हे

statements.statement: Here the scriptures, in their disputations, were baffled; the Veda said 'neti, neti'; throngs of yogis were left speechless; the experienced know it by their own realization.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: येथ शास्त्रें विषम झालीं वादें । ’नेति नेति’ म्हणितलें वेदें । थोटावलीं योगिवृंदें । अनुभवी निजबोधें जाणती

statements.statement: There reason, word and illustration all sank without a trace; the talk of the non-dual doctrine itself was abashed in that place.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तेथ हेतु-मातु-दृष्टांतु । समूळ बुडाला समस्तु । अद्वैतवादाची मातु । ज्या ठायांतु लाजिली

statements.statement: Equal vision inside and outside - this is the mark of final liberation in experience; marking this very sign, I made the arrow-maker my guru.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सबाह्य समदर्शन । हे अनुभवाची निर्वाणखूण । ’शरकार’ गुरु केला जाण । हेंचि लक्षण लक्षूनि

statements.statement: While he heated and straightened an arrow, his attention became firmly fixed; because of that, his awareness of worldly affairs stopped.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तावूनि उजू करितां बाण । दृढ लागलें अनुसंधान । इतुकेन प्रपंचाचें भान । खुंटलें जाण तयाचें

statements.statement: With banners, kettledrums and musical instruments, with chariots, elephants and an army's equipment, the king passed by with a great din; the arrow-maker, his eyes on the arrow, did not know it.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: निशाण भेरी वाजंतरें । रथ गज सैन्य संभारें । राजा गेला अतिगजरें । नेणिजे शरकारें शरदृष्टीं

statements.statement: Behind the king came his attendant; he asks, 'Did the king go by this road?' The other says, 'I did not see; who knows whether he went or not.'

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मागूनि रायाचा हडपी आला । तो पुसे ये मार्गी राजा गेला । येरु म्हणे नाहीं देखिला । गेला कीं न गेला कोण जाणे

statements.statement: I saw that arrow-maker, and hearing that account: in the world one-pointedness is great; it does not let worldly affairs come into view.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तो शरकारू देखिला दृष्टीं । हे ऐकोनि तयाची गोष्टी । जगीं एकाग्रता मोठी । प्रपंच दृष्टीं येवों नेदी

statements.statement: In meditation the main things are posture and the conquest of breath; when this comes, the external is not known. The arrow-maker guru gives this one-pointedness; this is the twenty-second guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ध्यानीं मुख्य आसन श्वासजय। होतां न कळे बाह्य। शरकार गुरु दें हें ऐकाग्र्य। बाविसावा हा गुरू

statements.statement: The arrow-maker, his mind fixed on his arrow: the king passes right in front of him with his retinue, a great uproar going along; yet he does not know it.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: बाणदत्तचित्त शरकार। पुढ्यांतून राजा सपरिवार। चाले सवें गजर। होई तरी नेणें तो

statements.statement: Though someone speaks abusive words, or there is a great noise nearby, it does not fill the mind of one who remains one-pointed.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: अवाच्य बोले कोणी। हो कां जवळ मोठा ध्वनी। राहे जो एकाग्र होऊनी। त्याचे मनीं हें न भरे

statements.statement: Likewise a yogī, conquering posture and breath and fixing his aim by dispassion and practice, stays, and giving up the sense of duality becomes established in samādhi.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: योगी तेवीं आसनश्वास जिंकून। वैराग्याभ्यासें लक्ष्य धरून। राहे तरी द्वैतभान। सोडून होई समाधिस्थ

statements.statement: If one has not first conquered posture and breath, obstacle arises; as soon as the breath is conquered, the mind is conquered.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जर पूर्वीं आसन श्वासजय। न करी तरी ये अंतराय। होतांच श्वासजय। मनोजय होतसे

statements.statement: If the mind does not stay completely within, then if one holds within the form of the Lord with qualities, the mind will delight.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: संपूर्णपणें अंतरीं। चित्त न ठरे जरी। तरी सगुण ईश्वररूप अंतरीं। धरितां चित्त रमेल

statements.statement: This is the secret of yoga: by practice the mind is bound; then its steadiness on the aim comes about.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: रहस्य हेंची योगाचें। अभ्यासें बंधन होय मनाचें। मग लक्षावरी त्याचें। स्थैर्य होतसे

statements.statement: Seeing that unprecedented sight, not remembering the objects, not even going into sleep, he becomes absorbed in his own nature.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तो अपूर्व देखावा दिसतां। विषया न स्मरतां। झोंपेंतही न जातां। स्वरूपींच लीन होई

statements.statement: Sattva guṇa growing completely, [and] the rajas and tamas guṇas, the mind merges, as fire does when the wood is burnt. [The construction is terse in the original.]

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: संपूर्णपणें सत्त्वगुण। वाढता रजस्तम गुण। लीन होई मन। काष्ठ जळतां अग्नी जसा

statements.statement: When the mind has merged so, he does not know outer or inner; by making the arrow-maker my guru, I truly came to know this.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: असें मानस लीन होतां। नेणवे बाह्याभ्यंतरता। शरकार गुरु करितां। हें तत्वता कळलें

statements.statement: A saintly person should remain alone and constantly travel without any fixed residence. Being alert, he should remain secluded and should act in such a way that he is not recognized or noticed by others. Moving without companions, he should not speak more than required.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
एकचार्यनिकेत: स्यादप्रमत्तो गुहाशय: ।
अलक्ष्यमाण आचारैर्मुनिरेकोऽल्पभाषण: ॥ १४ ॥
original.transliteration:
eka-cāry aniketaḥ syād
apramatto guhāśayaḥ
alakṣyamāṇa ācārair
munir eko ’lpa-bhāṣaṇaḥ
original.word_for_word: eka — alone; cārī — moving; aniketaḥ — without fixed residence; syāt — should be; apramattaḥ — being very alert; guhā-āśayaḥ — remaining secluded; alakṣyamāṇaḥ — without being recognized; ācāraiḥ — by his activities; muniḥ — a sage; ekaḥ — without companions; alpa — very little; bhāṣaṇaḥ — speaking.

statements.statement: The previous narration concerning the shell bracelets of the young girl demonstrates that even saintly persons engaged in ordinary yoga processes should remain alone to avoid conflict or disturbance. In other words, persons engaged in ordinary yoga processes should not even associate with each other. This verse indirectly refers to the serpent, who, fearing attack from human beings, keeps himself secluded. From this example we learn that a saintly person should not associate with ordinary materialistic people. He should also avoid having a fixed residence and should wander unnoticed by others.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Our engagement in material existence is the cause of our unhappiness. Such engagement destroys the real purpose of our life, Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Somehow or other one must give up the deep-rooted attachment to material society, friendship and love. One must practice detachment, and by surrender to the principles of Kṛṣṇa consciousness one’s auspicious life will begin. By organizing one’s life according to the varṇāśrama system one can take the first step in self-realization. In other words, one should accept an honest occupation and regulate his sex life, either by giving it up entirely as a brahmacārī or sannyāsī or by living as a married householder. Without regulating one’s occupation and personal life, there will be chaos, and it will be very difficult to make spiritual advancement. The attachments to material society, friendship and love are based on a long previous experience in the material world. They are great obstacles in the path of transcendental understanding, and if one maintains them, spiritual progress will be most difficult. Caitanya Mahāprabhu taught by His example and precept what a devotee should and should not do, and obedience to such principles brings one to the path of supreme perfection. Thus, one has to rise above ordinary social custom, which directs the living entity toward useless sense gratification.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: When a person living in a temporary material body tries to construct a happy home, the result is fruitless and miserable. The snake, however, enters a home that has been built by others and prospers happily.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
गृहारम्भो हि दु:खाय विफलश्चाध्रुवात्मन: ।
सर्प: परकृतं वेश्म प्रविश्य सुखमेधते ॥ १५ ॥
original.transliteration:
gṛhārambho hi duḥkhāya
viphalaś cādhruvātmanaḥ
sarpaḥ para-kṛtaṁ veśma
praviśya sukham edhate
original.word_for_word: gṛha — of a home; ārambhaḥ — construction; hi — certainly; duḥkhāya — leads to unhappiness; viphalaḥ — fruitless; ca — also; adhruva — impermanent; ātmanaḥ — of the living being; sarpaḥ — a serpent; parakṛtam — built by others; veśma — home; praviśya — having entered; sukham — happily; edhate — prospers.

statements.statement: The snake does not have the proclivity to build his own home, but rather lives in a suitable place constructed by other creatures. Thus he does not entangle himself in the labor of home building. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura points out that although materialistic persons take unlimited pains to invent and mass-produce electricity, automobiles, airplanes, etc., ultimately these things are meant for the convenience of the Vaiṣṇavas who are preaching Kṛṣṇa consciousness. The karmīs will always go to such trouble, and the devotees will always offer such laborious productions to the Supreme Personality of Godhead by engaging them in His loving service. The devotees, being concerned with the ultimate perfection of life, do not personally struggle for material advancement. On the other hand, there is no need for the devotees to artificially imitate the austere lifestyle of ancient times. A devotee’s goal is simply to serve Kṛṣṇa as nicely as possible; therefore the devotees willingly accept beautiful mansions and all types of material opulences, not with any personal attachment, but only so that these things can be engaged in the loving service of the Lord. If one engages such things with a desire to enjoy them, one falls down from the platform of pure devotional service. Materialistic persons are only interested in exploiting their so-called yoga practice in order to rejuvenate their sexual potency or to vainly remember their previous conditioned lives. Thus, applying mysticism to the endless search for sense gratification, they do not understand the actual goal of human life.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The serpent cannot bear company; alone it goes about happily; it always stays alert and does not let a breath go to waste.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सर्प सांघातु न साहे । एकाकी सुखें विचरत जाये । सदा सावधान राहे । श्वासु वाये जावों नेदी

statements.statement: Such too is the way of the yogī: he cannot bear the company of duality; he lives alone in solitude, unnoticed by people.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसीच योगियाची गती । न साहे द्वैताची संगती । एकाकी वसे एकांतीं । जनाप्रती अलक्ष्य

statements.statement: The serpent forces its way into a hole; everyone sees its trail on the road, but whether it is fed or hungry they cannot know - that it has gone, everyone knows.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सर्प बिळामाजीं रिघें बळें । मार्गीं मागू देखती सकळें । धाला भुकेला हें त्यां न कळे । गेला कळे सर्वांसी

statements.statement: Likewise the yogī, by the strength of yoga, does not stay among people in the company of people; lying in a cave, he plays alone in oneness.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसाचि योगियाही योगबळें । न राहे जनांमाजीं जनमेळें । गुहेमाजीं पडिला लोळे । एकला खेळे एकपणीं

statements.statement: Young and old see the yogīs' conduct as they carry it out, but whether their state is savikalpa or nirvikalpa, no one truly knows.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: हो का योगियांचा आचार । करितां देखती लहान थोर । सविकल्पनिर्विकल्प विचार । न कळे साचार कोणासी

statements.statement: Some call him ritualistic; some call him fallen from ritual; some call him established in the Self; no one understands clearly.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एक म्हणती कर्मठ । एक म्हणती कर्मभ्रष्ठ । एक म्हणती आत्मनिष्ठ । कळेना स्पष्ट कोणासी

statements.statement: The serpent has no speech at all; if it speaks, it is only a little; just so the yogī is not eager for verbal disputes.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सर्पास बोलणेंचि नाहीं । बोले तरी अल्प कांहीं । तैसाच योगिया पाहीं । वाग्वादीं नाहीं सादर

statements.statement: His speech is very little, yet it cuts through resolve and wavering; the nature of his words is known to those of true resolve.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: बोलणें तरी अति‌अल्प । परी छेदी संकल्पविकल्प । त्याच्या बोलाचे स्वरूप । सत्यसंकल्प जाणती

statements.statement: He who is alone and indifferent to the world, whose mind is set on the supreme goal, should not make vain efforts in hope of building a house.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जो एकाकी उदास । ज्याचें परमार्थीं मानस । तेणें गृहारंभाची आस । वृथा प्रयास न करावे

statements.statement: At the very root the undertaking of a house is sorrow; to labour at it is painful; even a three-storeyed house that is built is altogether impermanent, see.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मूळीं गृहारंभ तें दुःख । कष्ट करितां दुःखकारक । निपजविलें त्रिमाळिक । तें अध्रुव देख सर्वथा

statements.statement: Where worldly existence itself is perishable and the body, though visible, is unreal, can the house there be lasting? The foolish take it to be true.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जेथें संसारचि नाशवंत । देह प्रत्यक्षाकारें असंत । तेथींचें गृह काय शाश्वत । मूर्ख मानित सत्यत्वें

statements.statement: So too the yogī, know: he holds no pride in body or house; he dwells in another's house without pride, always full of happiness.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसाचि योगियाही जाण । न धरी देहगेह अभिमान । परगृहीं वसे निरभिमान । सुखसंपन्न सर्वदा

statements.statement: One should not build even a single house - this I accepted as true in my heart. God made this whole creation; how is it that it does not bind him?

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एकही गृह न करावें । हें सत्य मानिलें जीवें । एवढी सृष्टि केली देवें । बाधूं न पवे त्या केवीं

statements.statement: All people come to know; if one makes one's dwelling so, people give trouble; take that lesson from the serpent.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: संपूर्ण लोक जाणती। असी करितां वसती। लोक उपद्रव देती। सर्पापासूनी ती शिक्षा घेई

statements.statement: Serpents do not roam together; they go cautiously, without making a sound; they live in caves, and do not always stay in one place.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सर्प मिळोनी न फिरती।शब्द न करितां सावधान जाती। गुहेमध्ये वास करिती। नित्य न राहती एके ठाई

statements.statement: The serpent does not roam about openly, does not sleep without fear; it does not, for no reason, get angry at anyone by itself.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: विशदपणें न फिरे सर्प। निर्धोकानें न घे झोंप। निष्कारण आपोआप। न करी कोप कोणावरी

statements.statement: One should take all these qualities and behave like the serpent; one should look to a ready-made place, as the cobra [nāgobā] does in a house already built.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हे सम्पूर्ण गुण घ्यावें। सर्पापरी वागावें। सिद्धस्थान लक्षावें। आइत्या घरांत नागोबा जसा

statements.statement: Even if one builds a house of leaves, great sorrow comes to him; this body is perishable; it is not known whether it will fall even before that.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: कां पर्णाचेंही घर। करी त्या दुःख ये घोर। हे नश्वर शरीर। नकळे पूर्वीच पडेल कीं

statements.statement: As a river flood [footnote: nadīcā pūra] runs off, so does life run; it does not turn back; it is not known when it will end.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: सरित्पूर जसा पळे। तसें आयुष्यही पळे। तें माघारां न वळे। नकळे केव्हां संपेल तें

statements.statement: [For him] whose whole life-span [is so], karma does not keep him together in one place [the construction of these lines is unclear]; therefore one should not tie oneself to a house; I learned this from the serpent.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: संपूर्ण आयुष्य जयासी। कर्म एकत्र न ठेवी तयासी। म्हणोन न बांधावें घरासी। सर्पापाशीं शिकलों हें

statements.statement: The Lord of the universe, Nārāyaṇa, is the worshipable God of all living entities. Without extraneous assistance, the Lord creates this universe by His own potency, and at the time of annihilation the Lord destroys the universe through His personal expansion of time and withdraws all of the cosmos, including all the conditioned living entities, within Himself. Thus, His unlimited Self is the shelter and reservoir of all potencies. The subtle pradhāna, the basis of all cosmic manifestation, is conserved within the Lord and is in this way not different from Him. In the aftermath of annihilation the Lord stands alone.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
एको नारायणो देव: पूर्वसृष्टं स्वमायया ।
संहृत्य कालकलया कल्पान्त इदमीश्वर: ।
एक एवाद्वितीयोऽभूदात्माधारोऽखिलाश्रय: ॥ १६ ॥
original.transliteration:
eko nārāyaṇo devaḥ
pūrva-sṛṣṭaṁ sva-māyayā
saṁhṛtya kāla-kalayā
kalpānta idam īśvaraḥ
eka evādvitīyo ’bhūd
ātmādhāro ’khilāśrayaḥ
original.word_for_word: ekaḥ — alone; nārāyaṇaḥ — the Supreme Personality of Godhead; devaḥ — God; pūrva — previously; sṛṣṭam — created; sva-māyayā — by His own potency; saṁhṛtya — withdrawing within Himself; kāla — of time; kalayā — by the portion; kalpa-ante — at the time of annihilation; idam — this universe; īśvaraḥ — the supreme controller; ekaḥ — alone; eva — indeed; advitīyaḥ — without a second; abhūt — became; ātma-ādhāraḥ — one whose self is the reservoir and resting place of everything; akhila — of all potencies; āśrayaḥ — the reservoir.

statements.statement: As will be explained in verse 21 of this chapter, the Lord’s independent creation and annihilation of the universe can be compared to the spider’s creating and withdrawing his web. The word eka, or “one alone,” is mentioned twice in this verse to emphasize that there is only one Supreme Personality of Godhead and that all universal affairs, as well as spiritual pastimes, are conducted by His potency alone. According to Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura, this verse refers to Kāraṇārṇavaśāyī Viṣṇu, or Mahā-Viṣṇu lying in the Causal Ocean. The words ātmādhāra and akhilāśraya both indicate that Nārāyaṇa is the reservoir or shelter of all existence. Ātmādhāra indicates that the Lord’s personal body is the shelter of everything. Mahā-Viṣṇu is a plenary portion of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, from whose body expand the innumerable potencies that manifest the material and spiritual worlds. According to the Brahma-saṁhitā these innumerable worlds rest within the brahmajyoti, or spiritual effulgence, also emanating from the Lord’s body. Thus Kṛṣṇa is īśvara, the supreme controller.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: When the Supreme Personality of Godhead displays His own potency in the form of time and guides His material potencies, such as the mode of goodness, into a neutral condition of equilibrium, He remains as the supreme controller of that neutral state, called pradhāna, as well as of the living entities. He is also the supreme worshipable object for all beings, including liberated souls, demigods and ordinary conditioned souls. The Lord is eternally free from any material designation, and He constitutes the totality of spiritual bliss, which one experiences by seeing the Lord’s spiritual form. The Lord thus exhibits the fullest meaning of the word “liberation.”

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
कालेनात्मानुभावेन साम्यं नीतासु शक्तिषु ।
सत्त्वादिष्वादिपुरुष: प्रधानपुरुषेश्वर: ॥ १७ ॥
परावराणां परम आस्ते कैवल्यसंज्ञित: ।
केवलानुभवानन्दसन्दोहो निरुपाधिक: ॥ १८ ॥
original.transliteration:
kālenātmānubhāvena
sāmyaṁ nītāsu śaktiṣu
sattvādiṣv ādi-puruṣaḥ
pradhāna-puruṣeśvaraḥ

parāvarāṇāṁ parama
āste kaivalya-saṁjñitaḥ
kevalānubhavānanda-
sandoho nirupādhikaḥ
original.word_for_word: kālena — by the time factor; ātma-anubhāvena — which is the Lord’s own potency; sāmyam — to equilibrium; nītāsu — being brought; śaktiṣu — the material potencies; sattva-ādiṣu — the mode of goodness, etc.; ādi-puruṣaḥ — the eternal Supreme Personality of Godhead; pradhāna-puruṣa-īśvaraḥ — the supreme controller of the neutral state of nature (pradhāna) and of the living entities; para — of the liberated living entities or the demigods; avarāṇām — of ordinary conditioned souls; paramaḥ — the supreme worshipable object; āste — exists; kaivalya — liberated existence; saṁjñitaḥ — that which is indicated by the term; kevala — pure without material tinge; anubhava — experience of revelation; ānanda — bliss; sandohaḥ — the totality; nirupādhikaḥ — devoid of materially designated relationships.

statements.statement: One who fixes his mind in the Absolute Truth, the Personality of Godhead, gets immediate relief from the waves of material anxiety because the Lord’s transcendental form is completely free of any material contamination or designation. Less intelligent persons accept the illogical doctrine that the Lord is transformed into His creation and maintains no separate, individual existence. They falsely imagine that they can merge their individuality into the universal oneness and become exactly equal to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. However, in the opinion of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam the Personality of Godhead is not impersonal but is instead full of all transcendental qualities. The three modes of material nature constitute His inferior energy, and the omnipotent time factor, upon which the modes rest, is the personal expansion of the Lord. Thus, the Lord creates, maintains and annihilates the material manifestation and yet remains completely apart from it. The conditioned souls who desire to exploit the Lord’s inferior creation are impelled by the Personality of Godhead to do so, and thus they become imitation enjoyers in the temporary world of matter. But when one gains practical experience that the gross and subtle material bodies are simply coverings of the eternal soul, one gives up the foolishness of material attachment and becomes attached to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He realizes that his constitutional position is neither to enjoy matter nor merge into the Lord’s existence. His real nature is that he is a servant of God. Service rendered to the Lord is eternal, full of bliss and knowledge, and by the potency of such service one becomes liberated and his activities become glorious. Such service is eternal and gradually promotes one to the platform of kevalānubhavānanda-sandoha, or merging into the ocean of bliss by seeing the transcendental personal form of the Lord.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: O subduer of the enemies, at the time of creation the Personality of Godhead expands His own transcendental potency in the form of time, and agitating His material energy, māyā, composed of the three modes of material nature, He creates the mahat-tattva.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
केवलात्मानुभावेन स्वमायां त्रिगुणात्मिकाम् ।
सङ्क्षोभयन् सृजत्यादौ तया सूत्रमरिन्दम ॥ १९ ॥
original.transliteration:
kevalātmānubhāvena
sva-māyāṁ tri-guṇātmikām
saṅkṣobhayan sṛjaty ādau
tayā sūtram arindama
original.word_for_word: kevala — pure; ātma — of His own Self; anubhāvena — by the potency; sva-māyām — His own energy; tri — three; guṇa — modes; ātmikām — composed of; saṅkṣobhayan — agitating; sṛjati — He manifests; ādau — at the time of creation; tayā — with that energy; sūtram — the mahat-tattva distinguished by the power of action; arindama — O subduer of the enemies.

statements.statement: The word kevala means “pure” and indicates that the Lord’s kālaśakti, or time potency, is a transcendental energy nondifferent from His personal body. The brāhmaṇa addresses King Yadu here as arindama, subduer of the enemies. This indicates that although the topic of māyā, or illusory creation, is being discussed, the King need not worry, because as a staunch devotee of the Lord, he is able to subdue the real enemies of life, namely lust, anger and greed, which make one a prisoner in māyā’s kingdom. The word sūtram indicates the mahat-tattva, on which many material creations rest, just like jewels rest on a thread. In the state of pradhāna, or material equilibrium, the modes of nature do not interact. In the Third Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Lord Kapila explains in His Sāṅkhya teachings that the Supreme Personality of Godhead agitates the neutral state of nature and thus creation takes place. The created manifest form of nature in which fruitive activities are stimulated is called mahat-tattva, as indicated in this verse.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: If one tries to renounce the illusory creation of the Lord by taking shelter of impersonal Vedānta philosophy, thus artificially equating the infinite consciousness of the Lord and the infinitesimal consciousness of the conditioned soul, one’s analysis will fall far short of reality.
