The word sva-māyām in this verse indicates that the illusory potency that covers the conditioned souls is always subordinate to the Lord, whose consciousness is infallible and infinite and who is always a person.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: According to great sages, that which is the basis of the three modes of material nature and which manifests the variegated universe is called the sūtra or mahat-tattva. Indeed, this universe is resting within that mahat-tattva, and due to its potency the living entity undergoes material existence.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
तामाहुस्त्रिगुणव्यक्तिं सृजन्तीं विश्वतोमुखम् ।
यस्मिन् प्रोतमिदं विश्वं येन संसरते पुमान् ॥ २० ॥
original.transliteration:
tām āhus tri-guṇa-vyaktiṁ
sṛjantīṁ viśvato-mukham
yasmin protam idaṁ viśvaṁ
yena saṁsarate pumān
original.word_for_word: tām — the mahat-tattva; āhuḥ — they say; tri-guṇa — the three modes of material nature; vyaktim — manifesting as the cause; sṛjantīm — creating; viśvataḥ-mukham — many different categories of cosmic manifestation; yasmin — within the mahat-tattva; protam — strung and bound; idam — this; viśvam — universe; yena — by which; saṁsarate — undergoes material existence; pumān — the living being.

statements.statement: The cosmic manifestation is a reality because it emanates from the supreme reality, the Personality of Godhead. The material world, however, is temporary and full of problems. The conditioned soul foolishly tries to become the lord of this inferior creation and becomes separated from his real friend, the Supreme Lord. In this state, his only business is material sense gratification, and his real knowledge is lost.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Just as from within himself the spider expands thread through his mouth, plays with it for some time and eventually swallows it, similarly, the Supreme Personality of Godhead expands His personal potency from within Himself. Thus, the Lord displays the network of cosmic manifestation, utilizes it according to His purpose and eventually withdraws it completely within Himself.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
यथोर्णनाभिर्हृदयादूर्णां सन्तत्य वक्त्रत: ।
तया विहृत्य भूयस्तां ग्रसत्येवं महेश्वर: ॥ २१ ॥
original.transliteration:
yathorṇanābhir hṛdayād
ūrṇāṁ santatya vaktrataḥ
tayā vihṛtya bhūyas tāṁ
grasaty evaṁ maheśvaraḥ
original.word_for_word: yathā — just as; ūrna-nābhiḥ — the spider; hṛdayāt — from within himself; ūrṇām — thread; santatya — expanding; vaktrataḥ — from his mouth; tayā — with that thread; vihṛtya — enjoying; bhūyaḥ — again; tām — that thread; grasati — he swallows; evam — in the same way; mahā-īśvaraḥ — the Supreme Lord.

statements.statement: One who is intelligent obtains spiritual knowledge even from an insignificant creature like the spider. Thus, transcendental knowledge is visible everywhere for one whose eyes are opened in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: He is the abode of men [the souls]; therefore he is called 'Nārāyaṇa'; he alone is the life of the jīva; Nārāyaṇa is the Lord of all.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: नरांचे आश्रयस्थान । यालागीं बोलिजे ’नारायण’ । जीवाचें तोचि जीवन । स्वामी नारायण सर्वांचा

statements.statement: Thus he glanced at his own māyā and made her dwell on his own body, yet he did not let her cling to his body; only he who did this non-attachment knows it.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ऐसी निजमाया अवलोकिली । ते निजांगावरी नांदविली । परी अंगीं लागों नाहीं दिधली । हे अलिप्तता केली तो जाणे

statements.statement: Smoke gathers in the sky, but the sky does not touch the smoke; so, having made māyā grow out of his own being, he remains detached from her.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: धु‌ई दाटली आकाशीं । आकाश नातळे धु‌ईसी । तैसी निजांगे वाढवूनि मायेसी । अलिप्त तियेसी वर्ततु

statements.statement: He who is the substratum of his own māyā is himself the dwelling in which māyā lives; thus Nārāyaṇa is the controller of māyā - know this to be wholly true.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: स्वमायेसी जो अधिष्ठान । मायेसी नांदावया तोचि भुवन । एवं मायानियंता नारायण । सत्य जाण सर्वथा

statements.statement: Rajo-guṇa creates the creation; sattva-guṇa sustains it; at the end of the kalpa, stirring up tamo-guṇa, he destroys it in the form of Time.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: रजोगुण सृजी सृष्टीसी । सत्त्वगुण प्रतिपाळी तिसी । कल्पांतीं क्षोभवोनि तमोगुणासी । काळरूपेंसीं संहारी

statements.statement: Thus, having dissolved cause and effect, Nārāyaṇa alone remains, the one without a second, full in his oneness, having set aside qualities and non-qualities.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एवं संहारोनि कार्यकारण । एक अद्वितीय नारायण । एकपणें परिपूर्ण । गुणागुण निरसोनि

statements.statement: 'Nārāyaṇa alone, the One' - who is there even to say this? This is the mark of non-duality, a state empty of difference.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एकला एकु नारायण । हेंही तेथ म्हणे कोण । हें अद्वितीय लक्षण । भेदशून्य अवस्था

statements.statement: In that place there is no 'vijātīya-bheda' [difference from another kind], no 'sajātīya-bheda' [difference from the same kind], and not even 'svagata-bheda' [internal difference]; see it thus as empty of difference.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ’विजातीयभेद’ ते ठायीं । नसे ’सजातीयभेद’ कांहीं । ’स्वगतभेदु’ तोही नाहीं । भेदशून्य पाहीं ये रीतीं

statements.statement: He himself has no support, yet he has become the support of the universe, as a rope truly appears to be the resting-place of the appearance of a snake.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तो स्वयें तंव निराधार । परी झाला विश्वासी आधार । जेवीं सर्पाभासा दोर । दिसे साचार आश्रयो

statements.statement: So, swallowing all limiting adjuncts, he remains alone, free of adjuncts, as the Milk Ocean stays still once Mount Mandara has been taken out.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तैसा उपाधि गिळूनि सकळ । निरुपाधिक केवळ । जेवीं काढिलिया मंदराचळ । राहे निश्चळ क्षीराब्धी

statements.statement: As the sun hides the sight of the many stars by his own brilliance, so, swallowing the adjuncts, the One remains, free of adjuncts.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: नाना नक्षत्रावलोकु । निजतेजें लोपी अर्कु । तैसा उपाधि गिळूनि एकु । निरुपाधिकु उरलासे

statements.statement: Giving the firm bond of body-pride, she [kriyā-śakti, the power of action] makes people worldly; she brings up irrepressible desires and causes them to be born in many wombs.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: दृढबंध देहाभिमाना । दे‌ऊन संसारी करी जना । उपजवी अनिवार वासना । योनीं नाना जन्मवी

statements.statement: Having put such a link of pleasure and pain, the firm shackle of the three guṇas, she makes them suffer crores of sorrows, and still ignorance does not let go.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ऐसी सुखदुःखांची कडी । घालोनि त्रिगुणीं दृढ बेडी । भोगवी दुःखांच्या कोडी । तरी न सोडी अविद्या

statements.statement: 'Ūrṇanābhi' means the spider; she draws the thread from her heart out through her mouth and spreads it outside, by her own nature.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ’ऊर्णनाभि’ म्हणजे कांतिणी । हृदयतंतु मुखेंकरूनी । विस्तारी बाहेर काढूनी । निजगुणीं स्वभावे

statements.statement: On those spread threads, below and above, she herself plays in many ways, in her own sport.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: त्या विस्तारिल्या तंतूंवरी । तळीं आणि उपरी । आपणचि क्रीडा करी । नानापरी स्वलीला

statements.statement: She plays her sport with the spreading of the threads; right before the eyes, swallowing it back she takes it to her heart-lotus - she shows the art of non-duality.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तंतुविस्तारें खेळती लीला । प्रत्यक्ष देखतांचि डोळां । ग्रासूनि ने हृदयकमळा । अद्वैतकळा दाखवी

statements.statement: In this very way the Lord of all alone creates the world; at the end, having destroyed it, the unchanging Self alone remains.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: याचि रीतीं सर्वेश्वरु । एकला रची संसारु । अंतीं करूनि संहारु । उरे निर्विकारु निजात्मा

statements.statement: I, becoming the disciple of the spider, took the teaching of non-duality; hear this true teaching of the twenty-fourth guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: म्यां शिष्य होऊन कोळियाचा। उपदेश घेतला अद्वैताचा। हा चोविसाव्या गुरूचा। ऐक साचा उपदेश

statements.statement: O king, this is no picture [or: no wonder]: the spider draws a thread from its navel; making its house of it, day and night it plays strange games there.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: भूप ते हें नोहे चित्र। कोळी नाभीपासून काढी सूत्र। त्याचें घर करोनी अहोरात्र। करी विचित्र क्रीडा तेथें

statements.statement: Then at the end, eating that thread, it stays alone; know God to be so; he protects the creation.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मग अन्तीं तें सूत्र खाऊन। राही एकला होऊन। असा ईश्वर जाण। सृष्टिसंरक्षण करीतसे

statements.statement: Before, God, being one, without any materials, creates the worlds by himself by a mere glance.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: पूर्वीं तो ईश्वर एक असून। कांहीं सामग्री नसून। ईक्षणलेशेंकरून। स्वयें उत्पन्न करी लोकां

statements.statement: That same God, the support of the universe, sports here; then he withdraws it into himself by his own power of time.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तोचि देव विश्वाधार। येथे करी विहार। मग त्याचा करी संहार। काळशक्तीनें आपुल्या ठाई

statements.statement: Then the powers of sattva, rajas and tamas merge together with Pradhāna and Puruṣa; the adjuncts perish; then he becomes alone.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तेधवा सत्त्वरजस्तमःशक्ती। प्रधान पुरुषासह लीन होती। उपाधी नष्ट होती। मग होतो एकला

statements.statement: Before, the jīvas, all from Brahmā downward, who took their place in him: that their re-emergence should be made, so then that God wishes.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: पूर्वीं अखिल ब्रह्मादि जीव। त्याचे ठाई जे घेती ठाव। त्यांचा पुनः करावा उद्भव। असें तो देव इच्छि मग

statements.statement: Those men who do not become liberated while living, who enjoy their karma after death, do not merge into the Lord's own nature even in the dissolution.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जे जिवंतपणीं नर मुक्त न होती। मेल्यावरी कर्म भोगिती। ते प्रळयींही न मिळती। ईश्वरस्वरूपीं सर्वथा

statements.statement: When their desires, the cause, become ripe for fruit, it comes to the Lord's mind: 'Now their re-emergence should be made,' O king.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: त्या हेतुभूत वासना त्यांच्या। फळोन्मुख होतां ईश्वराच्या। चित्तीं येई आतां त्यांचा। उद्भव करावा असें भूपा

statements.statement: By that wish, manifesting the Māyā made of the guṇas, he in due order creates the universe again.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: त्या मनोरथेंकरून। गुणात्मक माया प्रगटून। अनुक्रमेंकरून। पुनः उत्पन्न करी तो विश्व

statements.statement: He has no effort in this; by mere resolve everything happens; having sported, he afterwards withdraws it again, as before.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हा प्रयत्न त्याला न पडे। संकल्पमात्रें सर्व घडे। क्रीडा करूनी तो पुनः पुढें। पूर्ववत् संहारी

statements.statement: Then the Self is one; all this that appears is illusory, all consisting of name and form: such discrimination I made.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तेव्हां तो आत्मा आहे एक। दिसतें हें सर्व मायिक। सर्वही नावरूपात्मक। असा विवेक केला म्यां

statements.statement: As the spider alone does not wish for materials, so this Self seemed to me to be the non-different instrumental and material cause.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हा जेवि कोळी एकला। इच्छीना सामग्रीला। तसा हा आत्मा मला। गमला अभिन्न निमित्तोपादान

statements.statement: If out of love, hate or fear an embodied soul fixes his mind with intelligence and complete concentration upon a particular bodily form, he will certainly attain the form that he is meditating upon.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
यत्र यत्र मनो देही धारयेत् सकलं धिया ।
स्‍नेहाद् द्वेषाद् भयाद् वापि याति तत्तत्स्वरूपताम् ॥ २२ ॥
original.transliteration:
yatra yatra mano dehī
dhārayet sakalaṁ dhiyā
snehād dveṣād bhayād vāpi
yāti tat-tat-svarūpatām
original.word_for_word: yatra yatra — wherever; manaḥ — the mind; dehī — the conditioned soul; dhārayet — fixes; sakalam — with complete concentration; dhiyā — with the intelligence; snehāt — because of affection; dveṣāt — because of envy; bhayāt — because of fear; vā api — either; yāti — he goes; tat-tat — to that, whatever it is; svarūpatām — particular state of existence.

statements.statement: From this verse it is not hard to understand that if one constantly meditates upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one will achieve a spiritual body just like that of the Lord. The word dhiyā, “with intelligence,” indicates complete intellectual conviction in a particular understanding, and similarly the word sakalam indicates one-pointed attention of the mind. With such complete absorption of consciousness, surely one will attain in the next life a form exactly like that upon which one was meditating. This is another example learned from the insect kingdom, as explained in the following verse.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: O King, once a wasp forced a weaker insect to enter his hive and kept him trapped there. In great fear the weak insect constantly meditated upon his captor, and without giving up his body, he gradually achieved the same state of existence as the wasp. Thus one achieves a state of existence according to one’s constant concentration.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

original.text:
कीट: पेशस्कृतं ध्यायन् कुड्यां तेन प्रवेशित: ।
याति तत्सात्मतां राजन् पूर्वरूपमसन्त्यजन् ॥ २३ ॥
original.transliteration:
kīṭaḥ peśaskṛtaṁ dhyāyan
kuḍyāṁ tena praveśitaḥ
yāti tat-sātmatāṁ rājan
pūrva-rūpam asantyajan
original.word_for_word: kīṭaḥ — an insect; peśaskṛtam — a wasp; dhyāyan — meditating on; kuḍyām — in his hive; tena — by the wasp; praveśitaḥ — forced to enter; yāti — he goes; tat — of the wasp; sa-ātmatām — the same state of existence; rājan — O King; pūrva-rūpam — the previous body; asantyajan — not giving up.

statements.statement: The following question may be raised: Since the weaker insect in this story did not physically change his body, how can it be said that he achieved the same state of existence as the wasp? Actually, by constant meditation upon a particular object one’s consciousness becomes filled with its qualities. Due to extreme fear the smaller insect was absorbed in the characteristics and activities of the large wasp and thus entered into the existence of the wasp. Due to such meditation, he actually took the body of a wasp in his next life.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Similarly, although we are conditioned souls, if we absorb our consciousness in Lord Kṛṣṇa we can become liberated even before giving up our present body. If our intelligence becomes steady on the spiritual platform by understanding that Lord Kṛṣṇa is everything, then we can give up unnecessary consciousness of the external body and absorb ourselves in the spiritual pastimes of Vaikuṇṭha. Thus even before death one can raise oneself to the spiritual platform and enjoy life as a liberated soul. Or, if one is a stubborn fool, then even in this life one can become just like an animal, such as a hog or a dog, constantly thinking of eating and sex life. But human life is actually meant for understanding the science of consciousness and the future results of our meditation.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The wasp is known as supeśa-kṛt because it causes the insect that it kills to take a beautiful form in the next life.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: When a person, with body, speech and mind made one-pointed, meditates on any thing, he becomes of that very form - know this.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: काया वाचा आणि मन । पुरुषें एकाग्र करून । जे जे वस्तूचें करी ध्यान । तद्‌रूप जाण तो होय

statements.statement: Through affection, hatred or fear - by whatever means firm meditation comes about, by that very means identity with that is gained; I declare it with raised arms.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: स्नेहें द्वेषें अथवा भयें । दृढ ध्यान जेणें होय । तेणेंचि तद्‌रूपता लाहे । उभवूनि बाहे सांगतु

statements.statement: The saying that identity with it will come after the body has gone is in vain; it is to be attained while one is here, in this very body.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देह गेलिया तद्‌रूपता । हो‌ईल हें वचन वृथा । येणेंचि देहें येथ असतां । तद्‌रूपता पाविजे

statements.statement: The wasp (bhiṅguraṭī) seizes an insect and shuts it up in a house within the wall; out of fear of death, that insect meditates without a break on the bhramarī [wasp].

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: भिगुरटी कीटकीतें धरी । कोंडी भिंतीमाजिले घरीं । ते मरणभयें ध्यान करी । निरंतरीं भ्रमरीचें

statements.statement: By that intense meditation, that insect becomes a wasp itself; it flies up into the sky at once - this is seen directly with the eyes.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तेणें तीव्रध्यानें ती कीटी । हो‌ऊनि ठाके भिंगुरटी । गगनीं चढे उठा‌उठी । प्रत्यक्ष दृष्टीं देखिजे

statements.statement: The wasp is inert and unreal; the foolish insect meditates on her, and by that gains identity with her; the Lord, however, is not like that.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: भिंगुरटी जड असंत । मूढ कीटी तिचें ध्यान करीत । तेणें तद्‌रूपता प्राप्त । तैसा भगवंत तंव नव्हे

statements.statement: He is not inert; he is of the form of consciousness, the giver of happiness; when a knower, a qualified one, meditates on him, there is no delay at all in attaining identity with him.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तो अजड चिद्‌रूप सुखदाता । ज्ञाता अधिकारी ध्यान करिता । तेथ तद्‌रूपता पावतां । विलंबू सर्वथा पैं नाहीं

statements.statement: Meditation on the Lord is not like that; the meditator is already of the Lord's form; by meditation only the delusion is destroyed, and effortlessly he is of that form.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: भगवद्ध्यान नव्हे तैसें । ध्याता भगवद्‌रूपचि असे । ध्याने भ्रममात्र नासे । अनायासें तद्‌रूप

statements.statement: If, in this very body and with this very mind, one does not know one's own liberation for oneself and does not attain the Lord's state, then learning in a human body is in vain.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: येणें देहें याचि वृत्तीं । आपुली आपण न जाणे मुक्ती । नेघवे भगवत्पदप्राप्ती । तैं वृथा व्युत्पती नरदेहीं

statements.statement: In vain is his knowledge and meditation; in vain his worship and officiating at sacrifices; in vain his observance of dharma - if he does not become the mass of consciousness.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: वृथा त्याचें ज्ञान ध्यान । वृथा त्याचें यजन याजन । वृथा त्याचें धर्माचरण । चैतन्यघन जरी नोहे

statements.statement: Whoever constantly meditates on something goes into that form; this lesson I took from the peśaskāra [footnote: kuṃbhāriṇa māśī, the potter wasp].

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो सदा ज्याचें करी ध्यान। तो जाई तदाकार होऊन। हें पेशस्करापासून। म्यां शिक्षण घेतलें

statements.statement: Listen, disciple: even the man who worships Īśvara from fear or hatred obtains good liberation hereafter. This is the teaching of the twenty-third guru.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

statements.statement: O King, from all these spiritual masters I have acquired great wisdom. Now please listen as I explain what I learned from my own body.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The material body is also my spiritual master because it teaches me detachment. Being subject to creation and destruction, it always comes to a painful end. Thus, although using my body to acquire knowledge, I always remember that it will ultimately be consumed by others, and remaining detached, I move about this world.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The words yathā tathāpi are significant in this verse. Although the body bestows great benefit by enabling one to learn about this world, one should always remember its unhappy, inevitable future. If cremated, the body is burned to ashes by fire; if lost in a lonely place, it is consumed by jackals and vultures; and if buried in a luxurious coffin, it decomposes and is consumed by insignificant insects and worms. Thus it is described as pārakyam, “ultimately to be consumed by others.” One should, however, carefully maintain bodily health to execute Kṛṣṇa consciousness, but without undue affection or attachment. By studying the body’s birth and death, one can acquire virakti-viveka, the intelligence to detach oneself from useless things. The word avasita indicates conviction. One should be convinced of all the truths of Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A man attached to the body accumulates money with great struggle to expand and protect the position of his wife, children, property, domestic animals, servants, homes, relatives, friends, and so on. He does all this for the gratification of his own body. As a tree before dying produces the seed of a future tree, the dying body manifests the seed of one’s next material body in the form of one’s accumulated karma. Thus assuring the continuation of material existence, the material body sinks down and dies.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: One might argue, “Among all the gurus mentioned thus far, the material body is certainly the best, since it awards the detachment and fine intelligence that enable one to engage in the devotional service of the Lord. Thus, we should serve the body, although it is temporary, with great attachment, or risk the offense of ungratefulness. How can detachment from the body be recommended when the body is endowed with so many wonderful qualities?” The answer is given in this verse. The body does not award detachment and knowledge in the manner of some benevolent teacher; rather, it causes so much pain and misery that any commonsense person cannot help being convinced of the uselessness of material life. Just as a tree produces the seeds of the next tree and then dies, the body’s lusty desires induce the conditioned soul to create a further chain of karma. Finally the body, having paved the way for unlimited suffering in material existence, drops dead.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: According to Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, deha indicates both the gross body and the subtle, mental body. Those who do not clearly understand the difference between body and soul falsely think that body and soul are identical and that one can find perfect happiness in bodily sense gratification. But those who foolishly accept the temporary body as all-important cannot be compared with self-realized souls who intelligently understand the superiority of the eternal soul.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: A man who has many wives is constantly harassed by them. He is responsible for their maintenance, and thus all the ladies constantly pull him in different directions, each struggling for her self-interest. Similarly, the material senses harass the conditioned soul, pulling him in many different directions at once. On one side the tongue is pulling him to arrange tasty food; then thirst drags him to get a suitable drink. Simultaneously the sex organs clamor for satisfaction, and the sense of touch demands soft, sensuous objects. The belly harasses him until it is filled, the ears demand to hear pleasing sounds, the sense of smell hankers for pleasant aromas, and the fickle eyes clamor for pleasing sights. Thus the senses, organs and limbs, all desiring satisfaction, pull the living entity in many directions.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura mentions that after understanding this verse one should merely offer, without attachment, the bare necessities to the guru of one’s body. One should keep one’s body fit and working in the simplest possible way, and that is the sum and substance of service to this so-called guru. If one desires to faithfully serve the body, one should consider that the body pulls the consciousness of the conditioned soul in many ways at once, and thus for the servant of the body there is no possibility of understanding God or even of becoming peaceful.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, expanding His own potency, māyā-śakti, created innumerable species of life to house the conditioned souls. Yet by creating the forms of trees, reptiles, animals, birds, snakes and so on, the Lord was not satisfied within His heart. Then He created human life, which offers the conditioned soul sufficient intelligence to perceive the Absolute Truth, and became pleased.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: God has specifically created the human form of life to facilitate the liberation of the conditioned soul. Therefore one who abuses human life prepares his path to hell. As stated in the Vedas, puruṣatve cāvistarām ātmā: “In the human form of life there is good possibility of understanding the eternal soul.” The Vedas also state:

statements.statement: The purport of this śruti-mantra is that lower forms of life, such as the cow and horse, are not actually suitable to fulfill the purpose of creation. But human life awards the opportunity to understand one’s eternal relationship with God. Thus, one must control the material senses and fulfill the real purpose of human life. If one takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, the Supreme Lord personally feels happiness and gradually reveals Himself to His devotee.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The Lord’s material creation consists of the living entities and dead matter, which the less intelligent try to enjoy. The Lord, however, is not satisfied by those species that blindly strive for sense gratification without understanding spiritual nature. We are suffering due to our forgetfulness of Kṛṣṇa and the blissful situation of His abode. If we accept the Lord as protector and shelter and execute His order, we can easily revive our eternal, blissful nature as parts and parcels of the Personality of Godhead. It is for this purpose that the Lord has created human life.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: After many, many births and deaths one achieves the rare human form of life, which, although temporary, affords one the opportunity to attain the highest perfection. Thus a sober human being should quickly endeavor for the ultimate perfection of life as long as his body, which is always subject to death, has not fallen down and died. After all, sense gratification is available even in the most abominable species of life, whereas Kṛṣṇa consciousness is possible only for a human being.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: Material life essentially means repeated birth and death. Even the lowest forms of life, such as reptiles, insects, pigs and dogs, have ample opportunity for sense gratification. Even ordinary houseflies have a busy sex life and thus multiply rapidly. Human life, however, enables one to understand the Absolute Truth and is therefore full of grave responsibility. Since the valuable human life is not eternal, we should do the needful to achieve the highest perfection, Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Before death appears, we should seriously cultivate our real self-interest.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: One can experience Kṛṣṇa consciousness in the association of devotees of the Lord. Without their association, one is in danger of being attracted to an impersonal conception of life, which causes one to fall away from devotional service to the Absolute Truth. Or, being discouraged by one’s failure to understand the Absolute Truth, one may return to the false platform of sense gratification. In conclusion, human life is meant for cultivating Kṛṣṇa consciousness under the guidance of the experienced, self-realized devotees of the Lord.

source.work: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (Bhāgavata Purāṇa), Canto 11, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust edition

statements.statement: The guru even of the twenty-four gurus, the reflection on discrimination and dispassion, is firmly obtained in the human body; therefore the human body is the chief guru.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

statements.statement: There is nothing as bad as the body anywhere on earth; looking through the three worlds, nothing as good as the body is found.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

statements.statement: If one gives it up as bad, one is cheated of the happiness of liberation; if one indulges it as good, one must surely go to hell.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

statements.statement: The body's course is perishable; from perishability dispassion arises; seekers of liberation never become attached to what is perishable.

statements.statement: That by which dispassion arises, know that for certain to be discrimination; thus the attainment of discrimination and dispassion comes, by one's own means, in the human body.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जंव जन्मलेंचि नाहीं । तंव मरण लागलें पाहीं । गर्भाच्याचि ठायीं । मरणघायीं धाकती

statements.statement: The freshness of that youth Time swallows without even removing the stalk; then decrepit old age arrives at the time of death.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: त्या तारुण्याची नवाळी । देंठ न फेडितां काळ गिळी । मग जरा जर्जरित मेळी । मरणकाळीं पातली

statements.statement: Even if death does not come, the disgrace of old age is great; wife and sons turn away and make him very wretched.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मरण न येतां जाण । थोर जरेचें विटंबन । विमुख स्त्रीपुत्रजन । अतिदीन ते करी

statements.statement: The whole body is subject to six changes; from each change come a crore of calamities; the six waves have attached within it, like a stream of ghee on fire.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देहो तितुका षड्‌विकारी । कोटि अनर्थ एकेके विकारीं । षडूर्मी लागल्या त्या भीतरी । जेवीं अग्नीवरी घृतधारा

statements.statement: The root of this sorrow is the pampering of the body; as the body is increased, sorrow grows strong; the final fruit is great sorrow.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: या दुःखाचें जें मूळ । तें देहाचें आळवाळ । देहो वाढवितां दुःख प्रबळ । उत्तरफळ महादुःख

statements.statement: Thus the company of the body is a constant attainment of sorrow; so attachment should be given up; for this reason the body is the guru of dispassion.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एवं देहाची जे संगती । ते निरंतर दुःखप्राप्ती । यापरी सांडावी आसक्ती । या हेतु विरक्ती देहगुरु

statements.statement: By means of this body the imperishable state is attained; in this way too, guruhood is said of the body.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: या देहाचेनि साधनें । अविनाश पद पावणें । याहीपरी येणें गुणें । गुरुत्व म्हणणे देहासी

statements.statement: The body is both a benefactor and a harmer; its guruhood is in both ways; the clever man who discriminates here and does his own good is blessed.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देह उपकारी अपकारी । यासी गुरुत्व दोन्हीपरी । येथ विवंचूनिं चतुरीं । निजहित करी तो धन्य

statements.statement: Thus the whole pomp of microcosm and macrocosm is only superimposition [āropa]: the rope has not become a snake; through delusion people call it a snake.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एवं पिंडब्रह्मांडखटाटोप । हा अवघाचि ’आरोप’ । दोरु जाहला नाहीं साप । भ्रमें सर्प तो म्हणती

statements.statement: To say 'I' of the body, known to be made of the five elements, is incongruous; the body is impure, I am pure; utterly opposed to us.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देह पांचभौतिक प्रसिद्ध । तो ’मी’ म्हणणें हें अबद्ध । देहो मलिन मी शुद्ध । अतिविरुद्ध या आम्हां

statements.statement: I am not earth, because of inertness; I am not water, because of fluidity; I am not fire, because of burning; I am not air, because of restlessness.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पृथ्वी मी नव्हे जडत्वें । जळ मी नव्हे द्रवत्वें । तेज मी नव्हें दाहकत्वें । चंचलत्वें नव्हें वायु

statements.statement: I am not the sky, because of emptiness; I am not ego, because of being seen; I am not the jīva, because of limitedness; I am not māyā, because of falsity.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: नभ मी नव्हे शून्यत्वें । अहं मी नव्हें दृश्यत्वें । जीव नव्हें मी परिच्छिन्नत्वें । माया मिथ्यात्वें मी नव्हें

statements.statement: I am not the body, because of perishability; I am not the sense-objects, because of obstruction; between these elements and me there is no connection here.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देह नव्हें मी नश्वरत्वें । विषय नव्हे मी बाधकत्वें । या तत्त्वां आणि मातें । संबंधू येथें असेना

statements.statement: As many as are the statements of the elements, so many are the negations [apavāda] upon me; this is the teaching of my intellect that I have told you, Yadu.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जितुका तत्त्वांचा अनुवादु । तितुका मजवरी ’अपवादु’ । हा माझा बुद्धीचा बोधु । तुज म्यां यदु सांगितला

statements.statement: Such a benefactor: there is no friend like this body; you say it should be kept carefully; but it is alien from the very root.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ऐसा उपकारी देखा । या देहासारिखा नाहीं सखा । म्हणसी राखावा नेटका । तंव तो पारका मुळींचि

statements.statement: If guarded with the utmost care, the end is seen to be perverse: it becomes food for dogs and jackals, or is eaten by fire.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: यासी अत्यंत करितां जतन । दिसे विपरीत निदान । श्वानशृगालांचें भोजन । कां होय भक्षण अग्नीचें

statements.statement: If it escapes both these fates, it teems with worms; a fourth state does not occur to it; you too know this plainly.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: या दोंही गतींवेगळें पडे । तरी सुळबुळीत होती किडे । चौथी अवस्था यासी न घडे । हें तूंही रोकडें जाणशी

statements.statement: Therefore I do not hold attachment for the body, O king; I wander unattached on earth, through the knowledge of abiding in the Self.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: यालागीं देहाची आसक्ती । मी न धरींच गा नृपती । निःसंगु विचरतसें क्षितीं । आत्मस्थितीचेनि बोधें

statements.statement: Know that all the means of enjoyment of the body are bonds; by them desire grows irresistibly.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देहासी उपभोगसाधनें । तितुकीं जाण पां बंधनें । दृढ वासना तेणें । अनिवारपणें वाढते

statements.statement: To give the body happiness, he increases sorrow a hundredfold; through body-pride, foolish people increase vain desires.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देहासी द्यावया सुख । शतधा वाढवी दुःख । देहाभिमानें जन मूर्ख । वृथाभिलाख वाढविती

statements.statement: The affection the body has increased, for house, wife, sons and wealth, that itself becomes desire at the end of the body: the seed for another body.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देहें वाढविली प्रीती । गृह दारा पुत्र संपत्ती । तेचि वासना होय देहांतीं । देहांतराप्रती निजबीज

statements.statement: As jowar rises to the ear, the grain of the ear falls to the earth; the grown plant, fully grown, breaks; that firm seed remains.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जैसा जोंधळा कणिसा चढे । कणसींचा क्षितीवरी झडे । वाढी वाढलें झाड मोडे । तें बीज गाढें उरलेंसे

statements.statement: That same seed, in the company of water and earth, grows again into a plant; so desire remains at the end of the body, to carry one to another body.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: तेंचि बीज जलभूमीचे संगतीं । सवेंचि झाड वाढे पुढतीं । तैसी वासना उरे देहांतीं । देहांतराप्रती न्यावया

statements.statement: The feet wish for motion; thus the senses tug and tug, as many co-wives tear at the one master of the house.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पाय वांछिती गती । ऐशीं इंद्रियें वोढा वोढिती । जेवीं एका गेहपती । बहुतां सवती तोडिती

statements.statement: Thus the attachment of the senses to objects makes desires firm; those carry the person, from body to body, in every way.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: एवं इंद्रियांसी विषयासक्ती । तेणें वासना दृढ होती । त्या देहदेहांतराप्रती । पुरुषासी नेती सर्वथा

statements.statement: Therefore, to renounce objects, attachment to the body must surely be cut; for this the human body is good; the division of knowledge comes in this body.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: यालागीं करावया विषयत्यागु । अवश्य छेदावा देहसंगु । इये अर्थी मनुष्यदेह चांगु । ज्ञानविभागु ये देहीं

statements.statement: In the human body He placed His own knowledge in abundance, by which knowledge embodied beings attain the bodiless state.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: बाहुल्यें मनुष्यदेहीं । निजज्ञान घातलें पाहीं । जेणें ज्ञानें देहीं । विदेह पाहीं पावती

statements.statement: Food, sleep, fear and mating are equal in all species; the knowledge in the human body is greater than in all.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: आहार-निद्रा-भय मैथुन । सर्वा योनींसी समसमान । मनुष्यदेहींचें ज्ञान । अधिक जाण सर्वांशीं

statements.statement: Seeing the human body, the Lord was pleased; it has the fitness for Brahman-knowledge; through this body, attainment of Me.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देखोनि मनुष्यदेहासी । सुख झालें भगवंतासी । अधिकार ब्रह्मज्ञानासी । येणें देहेंसीं मत्प्राप्ती

statements.statement: He who, having got human life, does not accomplish Brahman-knowledge, know him a bearded ram, wandering in the pursuit of objects.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पावोनियां मनुष्यपणा । जो न साधी ब्रह्मज्ञाना । तो दाढीचा मेंढा जाणा । विषयाचरणा विचरतु

statements.statement: By the knowledge of the human body, one takes the state of Sat-Cit-Ānanda; this much authority Nārāyaṇa gave, by his gracious glance.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मनुष्यदेहींचेनि ज्ञानें । सच्चिदानंदपदवी घेणें । एवढा अधिकार नारायणें । कृपावलोकनें दीधला

statements.statement: When crores upon crores of cycles occur through the 84 lakh species, then by chance, by their own fortune, they obtain the human body.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: चौर्‍यांशीं लक्षयोनींप्रती । जैं कोटिकोटी फेरे होती । तैं नरदेहाची प्राप्ती । अवचटें लाहती निजभाग्यें

statements.statement: From the time the body came into being, death has been attached to it; as a snake that has seized a frog begins to swallow it in the twinkling of an eye.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: देह जैंपासोनि झाला । तैंपासूनि मृत्यु लागला । जेवीं सापें बेडूक धरिला । गिळूं लागला लवनिमिषें

statements.statement: The snake swallows the frog; the frog with its mouth seizes the fish; so those fallen in the mouth of death, deluded by objects, grab at them.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: साप बेडुकातें गिळी । बेडूक मुखें माशातें कवळी । तैशीं मृत्युमुखीं पडलीं । विषयभुलीं झोंबतीं

statements.statement: He who is lazy here is cheated of everything; the supreme goal in hand is lost; he falls into the whirlpool, the wheel of worldly existence.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: येथ आळसु जेणें केला । तो सर्वस्वें नागवला । थिता परमार्थ हातींचा गेला । आवर्ती पडला भवचक्रीं

statements.statement: Cutting off laziness, driving away sleep, one should practise contemplation of the Self night and day, without rest.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: छेदोनियां आळसासी । दवडूनियां निद्रेसी । आत्मचिंतन अहर्निशीं । अविश्रमेंसीं साधावें

statements.statement: As long as the stroke of Time's blow has not yet sounded here, one should not waste life, to accomplish the supreme goal.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: काळाचा चपेटघात । जंव वाजला नाहीं येथ । तंव साधावया परमार्थ । आयुष्य व्यर्थ न करावें

statements.statement: He who does not accomplish Brahman-knowledge in the body is equal to dogs and pigs, or lower even than that; listen to that reasoning.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: साधीना देहीं ब्रह्मज्ञान । तो श्वानसूकरांसमान । अथवा त्याहोनि हीन । तें विवेचन परियेसीं

statements.statement: When a beast is kicked it holds no enmity at all; but if one says 'you' [contemptuously] to a man, it proceeds to killing.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पशूसी हाणिल्या लाथा । द्वेष न धरी सर्वथा । मनुष्यासी ’तूं’ म्हणतां । जीवघाता प्रवर्ते

statements.statement: A beast has no greed for hoarding: it eats one meal, then abandons the remainder at once.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: पशूसी लोभ नाहीं संग्रहता । एक आहार होय भक्षिता । मग उरलिया अर्था । त्यागी सर्वथा तत्काळ

statements.statement: The greed of man: with a crore of wealth in his purse he does not eat even for his own belly; rather than give it up, he would give up his life.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मनुष्याचें लोभिष्ठपण । गांठीं असल्या कोटि धन । पोटा न खाय आपण । मा त्यागितां प्राण त्यजील

statements.statement: A beast has no worry of morning and evening at all; but if you look at man's worry, it does not end in a hundred births.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: सायंप्रातर्चिंता । पशूसी नाहीं सर्वथा । मनुष्याची चिंता पाहतां । जन्मशतां न राहे

statements.statement: Lust, anger, greed, worry, slander, excessive pride: these are on man's head alone; beasts do not have them at all.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: काम क्रोध सलोभता । चिंता निंदा अतिगर्वता । हें मनुष्याचेचि माथां । पशूसी सर्वथा असेना

statements.statement: Know that the happiness of sense-objects is the same in heaven and in hell; what a dog enjoys in this world, Indra [enjoys] in heaven.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: विषयाचें जें सुख जाण । तें स्वर्गी नरकीं समान । जें इहलोकीं भोगी श्वान । तें स्वर्गी जाण इंद्रासी

statements.statement: By very great merit one rises to heaven; by very great sin a fall to a lower state comes about; when merit and sin both wholly fall away, then one's own liberation is got.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: अत्यंत सुकृतें स्वर्गी चढे । अत्यंत पापें अधोगती घडे । पापपुण्य निःशेष झडे । तैं आतुडे निजमुक्ति

statements.statement: When merit and sin are exactly equal, then one takes a human body, is born in the land of action, in the observance of the stages of life, of good intelligence.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: जैं पापपुण्य समान समीं । तैं मनुष्यदेह आक्रमी । जन्म पावे कर्मभूमीं । आश्रमधर्मी सुमेधा

statements.statement: Priceless gems come for a price, but the wish-fulfilling jewel does not come to hand; births in many wombs occur, but obtaining the human body is rare.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: मोलें अनर्घ्य रत्‍नें येती । तैसा चिंतामणी न ये हातीं । बहुत योनिये जन्म होती । परी मनुष्यदेहप्राप्ती दुर्लभ

statements.statement: Having got such a human body, he who does not accomplish Brahman-bliss is the greatest fool among people, a betrayer of God's trust.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: ऐसा नरदेह पावोनि देख । जो न साधीचि ब्रह्मसुख । तो जनांमाजीं परम मूर्ख । विश्वासघातक देवाचा

statements.statement: For the attainment of one's own Self God made the human birth; having destroyed God's trust, one's fall comes through the service of sense-objects.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: निजात्मप्राप्तीलागोनी । देवें केली मनुष्ययोनी । तो देवाचा विश्वास बुडवूनी । विषयसेवनीं निजपतन

statements.statement: Of all good fortune the fruit is just the human body; to make it fruitful, I practised unshakeable dispassion.

source.work: Eknathi Bhagavat (Ekanathi Bhagavata), commentary on Bhāgavata Canto 11

original.text: हो का सकळ भाग्याचें फळ । मनुष्यदेह गा केवळ । तें करावया सफळ । वैराग्य अढळ म्यां केलें

statements.statement: That Viṣṇu is all-pervading; I alone am the One: such discrimination I took, having thus made these twenty-four gurus.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: तो विष्णु व्यापक। मीच असें एक। असा घेतला विवेक। असें हे चौवीस गुरू करून म्यां

statements.statement: This attribute-less knowledge of Brahman does not take hold without dispassion; for that I made the body a guru and took this lesson; listen.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: हे निर्विशेष ब्रह्मज्ञान। न ठसे वैराग्यावांचून। त्यासाठीं देहास गुरू करून। घेतलें हें शिक्षण ऐक तूं

statements.statement: 'This body is mine': thinking so, they nurse it in vain; at the end, jackals and dogs go off eating it; whose is it?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: माझाच हा देह म्हणून। व्यर्थ करिती पालन। अंतीं ज्याला कोल्हे श्वान। जाती खाऊन तो कोणाचा

statements.statement: That which arose from semen and blood, in the impurity [viṭāḷ] of the mother: to carry it constantly brings weariness.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: जो शुक्रशोणितापासून। मातेच्या विटाळांत झाला उत्पन्न। त्याचें नित्य धारण। करितां शीण वाटला

statements.statement: Without this impure body, from where could a cause of dispassion be brought? For one whose mind is disgusted here, who need instruct him?

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: या अमेध्य देहावांचून। वैराग्यकारण आणावें कोठून। येथें ज्याचें विटें मन। त्याला कोण बोध करी

statements.statement: The body is a lump of the elements, earth and the rest; it protects itself along with its family, and leaving seed behind, dies like a tree.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: देह पृथिव्यादि भूतांचा गोळा। जो आपुल्यासह परिवाराला। रक्षूनी मागे बीजाला। ठेवून मरे वृक्षापरी

statements.statement: On this earth, tree-species die leaving seed behind; trees arise again from the seed; the same is the way of the body.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: ह्या पृथिवीवरी वृक्षजाती। मागें बीज राखून मरती। बीजाचे वृक्ष पुनः होती। तीच रीती देहाची

statements.statement: Through various pursuits one produces the threefold karma; that itself later produces a body; such knowledge arises then.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: नाना व्यासंग करून। त्रिविध कर्म करी उत्पन्न। तेंच पुढें देह करी उत्पन्न। असें ज्ञान होई तंव

statements.statement: The mind raises resolves; the senses pull this way and that, like co-wives of one man; such is the state of the body.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: मन स्सङ्कल्प उठती। इंद्रियें इकडे तिकडे ओढती। जेवी एका पुरुषा सवती। ये ती गती देहास

statements.statement: It becomes as if distracted and agitated; this is the root of all afflictions; such is this inauspicious body, yet it is rare.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: विक्षिप्तसा होई व्याकुळ। सर्व तापांचे हें मूळ। असा हा देह अमंगळ। तरी दुर्मिळ असे हा

statements.statement: By this very human body this means of liberation is obtained; I took it, having accomplished it; therefore I lie here without doubt.

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: याच मनुष्यशरीरें करून। मिळे असें हे मोक्षसाधन। म्यां घेतले साधून। म्हणून निःशंक पडे येथें

statements.statement: By the reasonings stated before, O king, constantly, and by the intellect with which I discriminated my own true nature here, I have without doubt become one with Brahman. [Sanskrit verse]

source.work: Datta Mahatmya (Dattamahatmya)

original.text: युक्तिभिः सततं भूप पूर्वोक्ताभिर्यया धिया। स्वात्मरूपं विविच्येह ब्रह्मभूतोऽस्म्यसंशयः
